title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
proposal_tldr: SWE-bench is introduced, an evaluation framework consisting of software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and corresponding pull requests across popular Python repositories that shows that both state-of-the-art proprietary models and the fine-tuned model SWE-Llama can resolve only the simplest issues.

title: A survey on large language model based autonomous agents
proposal_tldr: This paper discusses the construction of LLM-based autonomous agents, proposing a unified framework that encompasses much of previous work, and presents a overview of the diverse applications of LLM-based autonomous agents in social science, natural science, and engineering.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper builds an environment for language-guided agents that is highly realistic and reproducible, and creates an environment with fully functional websites from four common domains: e-commerce, social forum discussions, collaborative software development, and content management.

title: ChatGLM: A Family of Large Language Models from GLM-130B to GLM-4 All Tools
proposal_tldr: This report primarily focuses on the GLM-4 language series, which includes GLM-4, GLM-4-Air, and GLM-4-9B, which represent the most capable models that are trained with all the insights and lessons gained from the preceding three generations of ChatGLM.

title: Expanding Performance Boundaries of Open-Source Multimodal Models with Model, Data, and Test-Time Scaling
proposal_tldr: This work explores the relationship between model scaling and performance, systematically exploring the performance trends in vision encoders, language models, dataset sizes, and test-time configurations and hopes this model contributes to the open-source community by setting new standards for developing and applying multimodal AI systems.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
proposal_tldr: AgentBench is presented, a multi-dimensional benchmark that consists of 8 distinct environments to assess LLM-as-Agent's reasoning and decision-making abilities and shows that poor long-term reasoning, decision-making, and instruction following abilities are the main obstacles for developing usable LLM agents.

title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: A novel agentic memory system for LLM agents that can dynamically organize memories in an agentic way, combining the structured organization principles of Zettelkasten with the flexibility of agent-driven decision making, allowing for more adaptive and context-aware memory management.

title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: CogAgent, an 18-billion-parameter visual language model (VLM) specializing in GUI understanding and navigation, outperforms LLM-based methods that consume extracted HTML text on both PC and Android GUI navigation tasks-Mind2Web and AITW, ad-vancing the state of the art.

title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: An extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLM-based autonomous agents, including several multimodal models are conducted, identifying several limitations of text-only LLM agents, and revealing gaps in the capabilities of state-of-the-art multimodal language agents.

title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models
proposal_tldr: Experimental evaluation across diverse domains, including programming, interactive question-answering (QA), web navigation, and math, validates the effectiveness and generality of LATS in decision-making while maintaining competitive or improved reasoning performance.

title: Large Language Models for Information Retrieval: A Survey
proposal_tldr: This survey delves into the confluence of LLMs and IR systems, including crucial aspects such as query rewriters, retrievers, rerankers, readers, and search agents.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces InjecAgent, a benchmark designed to assess the vulnerability of tool-integrated LLM agents to IPI attacks, and shows that agents are vulnerable to IPI attacks, with ReAct-prompted GPT-4 vulnerable to attacks 24% of the time.

title: SeeClick: Harnessing GUI Grounding for Advanced Visual GUI Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel visual GUI agent -- SeeClick, which only relies on screenshots for task automation and creates ScreenSpot, the first realistic GUI grounding benchmark that encompasses mobile, desktop, and web environments.

title: GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded
proposal_tldr: This work explores the potential of LMMs like GPT-4V as a generalist web agent that can follow natural language instructions to complete tasks on any given website, and proposes SEEACT, a generalist web agent that harnesses the power of LMMs for integrated visual understanding and acting on the web.

title: Large language models empowered agent-based modeling and simulation: a survey and perspectives
proposal_tldr: This paper surveys the landscape of utilizing large language models in agent-based modeling and simulation, discussing their challenges and promising future directions and provides a comprehensive overview of the recent works of large language model-empowered agent-based modeling and simulation in multiple scenarios.

title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: A novel LLM-based multimodal agent framework designed to operate smartphone applications that allows the agent to mimic human-like interactions such as tapping and swiping through a simplified action space, eliminating the need for system back-end access and enhancing its versatility across various apps.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents
proposal_tldr: CoALA describes a language agent with modular memory components, a structured action space to interact with internal memory and external environments, and a generalized decision-making process to choose actions.

title: Understanding the planning of LLM agents: A survey
proposal_tldr: This survey provides the first systematic view of LLM-based agents planning, covering recent works aiming to improve planning ability, and provides a taxonomy of existing works on LLM-Agent planning, which can be categorized into Task Decomposition, Plan Selection, External Module, Reflection and Memory.

title: The rise and potential of large language model based agents: a survey
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive survey on LLM-based agents is conducted, covering their construction frameworks, application scenarios, and the exploration of societies built upon LLM-based agents.

title: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes TravelPlanner, a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario and provides a challenging yet meaningful testbed for future language agents.

title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebVoyager, an innovative Large Multimodal Model (LMM) powered web agent that can complete user instructions end-to-end by interacting with real-world websites and introduces an automatic evaluation protocol leveraging multimodal understanding abilities of GPT-4V to evaluate open-ended web agents.

title: Navigating the Digital World as Humans Do: Universal Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: UGround substantially outperforms existing visual grounding models for GUI agents, by up to 20% absolute, and agents with UGround outperform state-of-the-art agents, despite the fact that existing agents use additional text-based input while the authors' only uses visual perception.

title: A Real-World WebAgent with Planning, Long Context Understanding, and Program Synthesis
proposal_tldr: WebAgent is introduced, an LLM-driven agent that learns from self-experience to complete tasks on real websites following natural language instructions, and HTML-T5, new pre-trained LLMs for long HTML documents using local and global attention mechanisms and a mixture of long-span denoising objectives, for planning and summarization.

title: OS-ATLAS: A Foundation Action Model for Generalist GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: OS-Atlas is developed - a foundational GUI action model that excels at GUI grounding and OOD agentic tasks through innovations in both data and modeling and is releasing the largest open-source cross-platform GUI grounding corpus to date, which contains over 13 million GUI elements.

title: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
proposal_tldr: This work proposes WorkArena, a remote-hosted benchmark of 33 tasks based on the widely-used ServiceNow platform and introduces BrowserGym, an environment for the design and evaluation of such agents, offering a rich set of actions as well as multimodal observations.

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work presents AgentTuning, a simple and general method to enhance the agent abilities of LLMs while maintaining their general LLM capabilities, and constructs AgentInstruct, a lightweight instruction-tuning dataset containing high-quality interaction trajectories.

title: MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback
proposal_tldr: MINT is introduced, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs' ability to solve tasks with multi-turn interactions by (1) using tools and (2) leveraging natural language feedback, and repurpose a diverse set of established evaluation datasets focusing on reasoning, coding, and decision-making into a compact subset for efficient evaluation.

title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: AgentBoard is introduced, a pioneering comprehensive benchmark and accompanied open-source evaluation framework tailored to analytical evaluation of LLM agents that sheds light on the capabilities and limitations of LLM agents but also propels the interpretability of their performance to the forefront.

title: Agent Workflow Memory
proposal_tldr: Online AWM robustly generalizes in cross-task, website, and domain evaluations, surpassing baselines from 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test task distribution gaps widen.

title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces TheAgentCompany, an extensible benchmark for evaluating AI agents that interact with the world in similar ways to those of a digital worker: by browsing the Web, writing code, running programs, and communicating with other coworkers.

title: Two Tales of Persona in LLMs: A Survey of Role-Playing and Personalization
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work presents the first survey for role-playing and personalization in LLMs under the unified view of persona, and introduces existing methods for LLM personality evaluation.

title: AutoDroid: LLM-powered Task Automation in Android
venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Mobile Computing and Networking
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AutoDroid, a mobile task automation system capable of handling arbitrary tasks on any Android application without manual efforts, and demonstrates that AutoDroid is able to precisely generate actions with an accuracy of 90.9%, and complete tasks with a success rate of 71.3%.

title: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Tool Use Capabilities
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: It is shown that open source and proprietary models have a significant performance gap, and complex tasks like State Dependency, Canonicalization and Insufficient Information defined in ToolSandbox are challenging even the most capable SOTA LLMs.

title: Agent-SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces Agent-SafetyBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the safety of LLM agents, and summarizes two fundamental safety defects in current LLM agents: lack of robustness and lack of risk awareness.

title: ScreenSpot-Pro: GUI Grounding for Professional High-Resolution Computer Use
proposal_tldr: A new benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate the grounding capabilities of MLLMs in high-resolution professional settings and proposes ScreenSeekeR, a visual search method that utilizes the GUI knowledge of a strong planner to guide a cascaded search, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

title: Aguvis: Unified Pure Vision Agents for Autonomous GUI Interaction
proposal_tldr: Aguvis is introduced, a unified vision-based framework for autonomous GUI agents that directly operates on screen images, standardizes cross-platform interactions and incorporates structured reasoning via inner monologue, marking the first fully autonomous vision-based GUI agent that operates without closed-source models.

title: ShowUI: One Vision-Language-Action Model for GUI Visual Agent
proposal_tldr: This work develops a vision-language-action model in digital world, namely ShowUI, which features the following innovations: UI-Guided Visual Token Selection to reduce computational costs by formulating screenshots as an UI connected graph, adaptively identifying their redundant relationship and serve as the criteria for token selection during self-attention blocks.

title: A Survey on Recent Advances in LLM-Based Multi-turn Dialogue Systems
proposal_tldr: This article aims to elaborate recent advances in multi-turn dialogue systems, covering both LLM-based open-domain dialogue (ODD) and task-oriented dialogue (TOD) systems, along with datasets and evaluation metrics.

title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
proposal_tldr: This work establishes comprehensive benefits of fine-tuning LMs for agents, and provides an initial set of experimental designs, insights, as well as open questions toward language agent fine- Tuning.

title: WebRL: Training LLM Web Agents via Self-Evolving Online Curriculum Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: WebRL is introduced, a self-evolving online curriculum reinforcement learning framework designed to train high-performance web agents using open LLMs that addresses three key challenges in building LLM web agents, including the scarcity of training tasks, sparse feedback signals, and policy distribution drift in online learning.

title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
proposal_tldr: ReasoningBank is proposed, a novel memory framework that distills generalizable reasoning strategies from an agent's self-judged successful and failed experiences, and memory-driven experience scaling is established as a new scaling dimension, enabling agents to self-evolve with emergent behaviors naturally arise.

title: Mobile-Agent-v2: Mobile Device Operation Assistant with Effective Navigation via Multi-Agent Collaboration
proposal_tldr: The proposed Mobile-Agent-v2, a multi-agent architecture for mobile device operation assistance, comprises three agents: planning agent, decision agent, and reflection agent that generates task progress, making the navigation of history operations more efficient.

title: MetaTool Benchmark for Large Language Models: Deciding Whether to Use Tools and Which to Use
proposal_tldr: MetaTool is introduced, a benchmark designed to evaluate whether LLMs have tool usage awareness and can correctly choose tools, and recommends that tool developers choose an appropriate rewrite model for generating new descriptions based on the downstream LLM the tool will apply to.

title: AI Agents That Matter
proposal_tldr: A focus on cost in addition to accuracy motivates the new goal of jointly optimizing the two metrics, and design and implement one such optimization, showing its potential to greatly reduce cost while maintaining accuracy.

title: Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper provides the first comprehensive survey of evaluation methods for these increasingly capable agents, identifying critical gaps that future research must address, particularly in assessing cost-efficiency, safety, and robustness, and in developing fine-grained, scalable evaluation methods.

title: Large Language Model Agent: A Survey on Methodology, Applications and Challenges
proposal_tldr: This survey systematically deconstructs LLM agent systems through a methodology-centered taxonomy, linking architectural foundations, collaboration mechanisms, and evolutionary pathways, and unify fragmented research threads by revealing fundamental connections between agent design principles and their emergent behaviors in complex environments.

title: APIGen: Automated Pipeline for Generating Verifiable and Diverse Function-Calling Datasets
proposal_tldr: APIGen, an automated data generation pipeline designed to synthesize verifiable high-quality datasets for function-calling applications, is presented and its 1B model achieves exceptional performance, surpassing GPT-3.5-Turbo and Claude-3 Haiku.

title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
proposal_tldr: MEM1, an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that enables agents to operate with constant memory across long multi-turn tasks, is introduced, an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that enables agents to operate with constant memory across long multi-turn tasks.

title: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Plan-and-Act, a novel framework that incorporates explicit planning into LLM-based agents and introduces a scalable method to enhance plan generation through a novel synthetic data generation method.

title: Agent Q: Advanced Reasoning and Learning for Autonomous AI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a framework that combines guided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) search with a self-critique mechanism and iterative fine-tuning on agent interactions using an off-policy variant of the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) algorithm, which allows LLM agents to learn effectively from both successful and unsuccessful trajectories, thereby improving their generalization in complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.

title: OmniParser for Pure Vision Based GUI Agent
proposal_tldr: This work introduces \textsc{OmniParser}, a comprehensive method for parsing user interface screenshots into structured elements, which significantly enhances the ability of GPT-4V to generate actions that can be accurately grounded in the corresponding regions of the interface.

title: OS-Copilot: Towards Generalist Computer Agents with Self-Improvement
proposal_tldr: OS-Copilot is introduced, a framework to build generalist agents capable of interfacing with comprehensive elements in an operating system (OS), including the web, code terminals, files, multimedia, and various third-party applications, and FRIDAY, a self-improving embodied agent for automating general computer tasks.

title: Ferret-UI: Grounded Mobile UI Understanding with Multimodal LLMs
proposal_tldr: Ferret-UI, a new MLLM tailored for enhanced understanding of mobile UI screens, equipped with referring, grounding, and reasoning capabilities, excels not only beyond most open-source UI MLLMs, but also surpasses GPT-4V on all the elementary UI tasks.

title: Windows Agent Arena: Evaluating Multi-Modal OS Agents at Scale
proposal_tldr: The Windows Agent Arena is introduced: a reproducible, general environment focusing exclusively on the Windows operating system (OS) where agents can operate freely within a real Windows OS and use the same wide range of applications, tools, and web browsers available to human users when solving tasks.

title: PrivacyLens: Evaluating Privacy Norm Awareness of Language Models in Action
proposal_tldr: PrivacyLens is proposed, a novel framework designed to extend privacy-sensitive seeds into expressive vignettes and further into agent trajectories, enabling multi-level evaluation of privacy leakage in LM agents' actions.

title: On the Effects of Data Scale on UI Control Agents
proposal_tldr: How performance measured on both high and low-level tasks in domain and out of domain scales as more training data is collected is investigated and suggests that in particular for high-level tasks, fine-tuning on more data alone may be insufficient for achieving robust out-of-domain performance.

title: Trial and Error: Exploration-Based Trajectory Optimization for LLM Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This study presents an exploration-based trajectory optimization approach, referred to as ETO, designed to enhance the performance of open LLM agents and allows agents to learn from their exploration failures, which leads to improved performance through an iterative optimization framework.

title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
proposal_tldr: Synapse, a computer agent featuring three key components: state abstraction, which filters out task-irrelevant information from raw states, allowing more exemplars within the limited context, and trajectory-as-exemplar prompting, which prompts the LLM with complete trajectories of the abstracted states and actions to improve multi-step decision-making.

title: GUIOdyssey: A Comprehensive Dataset for Cross-App GUI Navigation on Mobile Devices
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
proposal_tldr: Autonomous Graphical User Interface (GUI) navigation agents can enhance user experience in communication, entertainment, and productivity by streamlining workflows and reducing manual intervention. However, prior GUI agents often trained with datasets comprising tasks that can be completed within a

title: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: UI-TARS-2 is presented, a native GUI-centered agent model that addresses challenges through a systematic training methodology: a data flywheel for scalable data generation, a stabilized multi-turn RL framework, a hybrid GUI environment that integrates file systems and terminals, and a unified sandbox platform for large-scale rollouts.

title: Watch Out for Your Agents! Investigating Backdoor Threats to LLM-Based Agents
proposal_tldr: This work forms a general framework of agent backdoor attacks, then presents a thorough analysis of different forms of agent backdoor attacks, and implements variations of agent backdoor attacks on two typical agent tasks including web shopping and tool utilization.

title: WebLINX: Real-World Website Navigation with Multi-Turn Dialogue
proposal_tldr: A retrieval-inspired model that efficiently prunes HTML pages by ranking relevant elements is designed that finds that smaller finetuned decoders surpass the best zero-shot LLMs, but also larger finetuned multimodal models which were explicitly pretrained on screenshots.

title: WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: WebWalker is proposed, which is a multi-agent framework that mimics human-like web navigation through an explore-critic paradigm that demonstrates the effectiveness of RAG combined with WebWalker, through the horizontal and vertical integration in real-world scenarios.

title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
proposal_tldr: This paper develops and evaluates three automated failure attribution methods for LLM multi-agent systems and introduces the Who&When dataset, comprising extensive failure logs from 127 LLM multi-agent systems with fine-grained annotations linking failures to specific agents and decisive error steps.

title: Multi-agent Architecture Search via Agentic Supernet
proposal_tldr: MaAS is introduced, an automated framework that samples query-dependent agentic systems from the supernet, delivering high-quality solutions and tailored resource allocation and enjoys superior cross-dataset and cross-LLM-backbone transferability.

title: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an instruction-following multimodal agent, WebGUM, that observes both webpage screenshots and HTML pages and outputs web navigation actions, such as click and type, and achieves superior performance to the existing SoTA, PaLM-540B.

title: Prompt Injection Attack to Tool Selection in LLM Agents
venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
proposal_tldr: This work introduces ToolHijacker, a novel prompt injection attack targeting tool selection in no-box scenarios, and forms the crafting of such tool documents as an optimization problem and proposes a two-phase optimization strategy to solve it.

title: Magma: A Foundation Model for Multimodal AI Agents
proposal_tldr: Magma is a foundation model that serves multimodal AI agentic tasks in both the digital and physical worlds and creates new state-of-the-art results on UI navigation and robotic manipulation tasks, outperforming previous models that are specifically tailored to these tasks.

title: Android in the Zoo: Chain-of-Action-Thought for GUI Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work presents Chain-of-Action-Thought (dubbed CoAT), which takes the description of the previous actions, the current screen, and more importantly the action thinking of what actions should be performed and the outcomes led by the chosen action.

title: An Illusion of Progress? Assessing the Current State of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work conducts the first comprehensive and rigorous assessment of the current state of web agents, and presents the first comprehensive comparative analysis of current web agents, highlighting both their strengths and limitations to inspire future research.

title: WebAgent-R1: Training Web Agents via End-to-End Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work presents WebAgent-R1, a simple yet effective end-to-end multi-turn RL framework for training web agents that learns directly from online interactions with web environments by asynchronously generating diverse trajectories, entirely guided by binary rewards depending on task success.

title: EIA: Environmental Injection Attack on Generalist Web Agents for Privacy Leakage
proposal_tldr: This work presents a realistic threat model for attacks on the website, and proposes a novel attack method, termed Environmental Injection Attack (EIA), which injects malicious content designed to adapt well to environments where the agents operate and instantiates EIA specifically for privacy scenarios in web environments.

title: Language Agents with Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Play in the Werewolf Game
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel framework that powers LLM-based agents with reinforcement learning (RL) and shows that these agents overcome the intrinsic bias and outperform existing LLM-based agents in the Werewolf game.

title: A Human-Inspired Reading Agent with Gist Memory of Very Long Contexts
proposal_tldr: Current Large Language Models (LLMs) are not only limited to some maximum context length, but also are not able to robustly consume long inputs. To address these limitations, we propose ReadAgent, an LLM agent system that increases effective context length up to 20x in our experiments. Inspired by h

title: OmniACT: A Dataset and Benchmark for Enabling Multimodal Generalist Autonomous Agents for Desktop and Web
proposal_tldr: OmniACT is introduced, the first-of-a-kind dataset and benchmark for assessing an agent's capability to generate executable programs to accomplish computer tasks and motivates future work towards building multimodal models that bridge large language models and the visual grounding of computer screens.

title: Large Language Models can Strategically Deceive their Users when Put Under Pressure
proposal_tldr: To the authors' knowledge, this is the first demonstration of Large Language Models trained to be helpful, harmless, and honest, strategically deceiving their users in a realistic situation without direct instructions or training for deception.

title: The BrowserGym Ecosystem for Web Agent Research
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an extended BrowserGym-based ecosystem for web agent research, which unifies existing benchmarks from the literature and includes AgentLab, a complementary framework that aids in agent creation, testing, and analysis and offers flexibility for integrating new benchmarks while ensuring consistent evaluation and comprehensive experiment management.

title: AssistantBench: Can Web Agents Solve Realistic and Time-Consuming Tasks?
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AssistantBench, a challenging new benchmark consisting of 214 realistic tasks that can be automatically evaluated, covering different scenarios and domains, and introduces SeePlanAct, a new web agent that significantly outperforms previous agents, and an ensemble of SPA and closed-book models reaches the best overall performance.

title: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
proposal_tldr: OpenAgents enables general users to interact with agent functionalities through a web user interface optimized for swift responses and common failures while offering developers and researchers a seamless deployment experience on local setups, providing a foundation for crafting innovative language agents and facilitating real-world evaluations.

title: Agent S2: A Compositional Generalist-Specialist Framework for Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Agent S2, a novel compositional framework that delegates cognitive responsibilities across various generalist and specialist models and proposes a novel Mixture-of-Grounding technique to achieve precise GUI localization and introduces Proactive Hierarchy Planning, dynamically refining action plans at multiple temporal scales in response to evolving observations.

title: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
proposal_tldr: This work introduces SkillWeaver, a skill-centric framework enabling agents to self-improve by autonomously synthesizing reusable skills as APIs, and demonstrates the effectiveness of honing diverse website interactions into APIs, which can be seamlessly shared among various web agents.

title: GPT-4V in Wonderland: Large Multimodal Models for Zero-Shot Smartphone GUI Navigation
proposal_tldr: The findings demonstrate that large multimodal models, specifically GPT-4V, excel in zero-shot GUI navigation through its advanced screen interpretation, action reasoning, and precise action localization capabilities.

title: Hello Again! LLM-powered Personalized Agent for Long-term Dialogue
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The Long-term Dialogue Agent is introduced, which incorporates three independently tunable modules dedicated to event perception, persona extraction, and response generation and the effectiveness, generality, and cross-domain capabilities of LD-Agent are empirically demonstrated across various illustrative benchmarks, models, and tasks.

title: Tree Search for Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an inference-time search algorithm for LM agents to explicitly perform exploration and multi-step planning in interactive web environments, and is the first tree search algorithm for LM agents that shows effectiveness on realistic web tasks.

title: BadAgent: Inserting and Activating Backdoor Attacks in LLM Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work demonstrates the clear risk of constructing LLM agents based on untrusted LLMs or data and proposes a proposed backdoor attacks named BadAgent on various agent tasks, where a backdoor can be embedded by fine-tuning on the backdoor data.

title: OS-Genesis: Automating GUI Agent Trajectory Construction via Reverse Task Synthesis
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: It is demonstrated that training GUI agents with OS-Genesis significantly improves their performance on highly challenging online benchmarks, and in-depth analysis further validates OS-Genesis's efficiency and its superior data quality and diversity compared to existing synthesis methods.

title: Aria-UI: Visual Grounding for GUI Instructions
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Aria-UI is introduced, a large multimodal model specifically designed for GUI grounding that adopts a pure-vision approach, eschewing reliance on auxiliary inputs, and proposes a scalable data pipeline that synthesizes diverse and high-quality instruction samples for grounding.

title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces SceneCraft, a Large Language Model (LLM) Agent converting text descriptions into Blender-executable Python scripts which render complex scenes with up to a hundred 3D assets, and demonstrates that it surpasses existing LLM-based agents in rendering complex scenes.

title: OpenCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes OpenCUA, a comprehensive open-source framework for scaling CUA data and foundation models and releases the annotation tool, datasets, code, and models to build open foundations for further CUA research.

title: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents
proposal_tldr: It is shown that domain-general automatic evaluators can significantly improve the performance of agents for web navigation and device control and are used to improve the performance of existing agents via fine-tuning and inference-time guidance.

title: LlaSMol: Advancing Large Language Models for Chemistry with a Large-Scale, Comprehensive, High-Quality Instruction Tuning Dataset
proposal_tldr: SMolInstruct, a large-scale, comprehensive, and high-quality dataset for instruction tuning, is proposed and a set of open-source LLMs are fine-tune, among which, Mistral serves as the best base model for chemistry tasks.

title: Is Your LLM Secretly a World Model of the Internet? Model-Based Planning for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a model-based planning framework, WebDreamer, which employs LLMs to serve as both world models and value functions, and trains specialized LLMs as world models with a scalable data synthesis pipeline, highlighting the potential of specialized world models for efficient and effective planning in complex web environments.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: The Governance of the Commons Simulation (GovSim), a generative simulation platform designed to study strategic interactions and cooperative decision-making in LLMs, is introduced and agents that leverage "Universalization"-based reasoning, a theory of moral thinking, are able to achieve significantly better sustainability.

title: Mobile-Agent-E: Self-Evolving Mobile Assistant for Complex Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Mobile-Agent-E, a hierarchical multi-agent framework capable of self-evolution through past experience capable of achieving 22% absolute improvement over previous state-of-the-art approaches across three foundation model backbones.

title: ScreenAI: A Vision-Language Model for UI and Infographics Understanding
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: This work introduces ScreenAI, a vision-language model that specializes in UI and infographics understanding that improves upon the PaLI architecture with the flexible patching strategy of pix2struct and is trained on a unique mixture of datasets.

title: A Survey of WebAgents: Towards Next-Generation AI Agents for Web Automation with Large Foundation Models
proposal_tldr: Existing research studies on WebAgents are reviewed across three key aspects: architectures, training, and trustworthiness to provide deeper insights.

title: Scaling Computer-Use Grounding via User Interface Decomposition and Synthesis
proposal_tldr: OSWorld-G, a comprehensive benchmark comprising 564 finely annotated samples across diverse task types including text matching, element recognition, layout understanding, and precise manipulation, is introduced and improved grounding with Jedi directly enhances agentic capabilities of general foundation models on complex computer tasks.

title: Large multimodal agents: a survey
proposal_tldr: This paper conducts a systematic review of LLM-driven multimodal agents, introducing the essential components involved in developing LMAs and categorizing the current body of research into four distinct types.

title: MatPlotAgent: Method and Evaluation for LLM-Based Agentic Scientific Data Visualization
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This study introduces MatPlotAgent, an efficient model-agnostic LLM agent framework designed to automate scientific data visualization tasks, and introduces a scoring approach that utilizes GPT-4V for automatic evaluation.

title: Unveiling Privacy Risks in LLM Agent Memory
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work systematically investigates the vulnerability of LLM agents to the proposed Memory EXTRaction Attack (MEXTRA) under a black-box setting and proposes an effective attacking prompt design and an automated prompt generation method based on different levels of knowledge about the LLM agent.

title: Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work manually creates 200 targeted adversarial tasks and evaluation scripts in a realistic threat model on top of VisualWebArena, a real environment for web agents, and proposes the Agent Robustness Evaluation (ARE) framework, a framework to systematically examine the robustness of agents.

title: Web Agents with World Models: Learning and Leveraging Environment Dynamics in Web Navigation
proposal_tldr: A World-model-augmented (WMA) web agent, which simulates the outcomes of its actions for better decision-making and improves agents' policy selection without training and demonstrates their cost- and time-efficiency compared to recent tree-search-based agents.

title: ST-WebAgentBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Safety and Trustworthiness in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces the ST-WebAgentBench, a configurable and easily extensible suite for evaluating web agent ST across realistic enterprise scenarios, and proposes the CuP metric, which credits only completions that respect all applicable policies, and the Risk Ratio, which quantifies ST breaches across dimensions.

title: If LLM Is the Wizard, Then Code Is the Wand: A Survey on How Code Empowers Large Language Models to Serve as Intelligent Agents
proposal_tldr: An overview of the various benefits of integrating code into LLMs' training data and how these profound capabilities of LLMs, brought by code, have led to their emergence as intelligent agents in situations where the ability to understand instructions, decompose goals, plan and execute actions, and refine from feedback are crucial to their success on downstream tasks are traced.

title: When Search Engine Services Meet Large Language Models: Visions and Challenges
proposal_tldr: An in-depth examination of how integrating LLMs with search engines can mutually benefit both technologies and broader implications for service computing, such as scalability, privacy concerns, and the need to adapt search engine architectures for these advanced models are examined.

title: Attacking Vision-Language Computer Agents via Pop-ups
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: VLM agents can be easily attacked by a set of carefully designed adversarial pop-ups, which human users would typically recognize and ignore, and basic defense techniques are ineffective against the attack.

title: GUICourse: From General Vision Language Models to Versatile GUI Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: GUICourse is a suite of datasets to train visual-based GUI agents from general VLMs to strengthen the OCR and grounding capabilities of VLMs and demonstrate that these GUI agents have better performance on common GUI tasks than their baseline VLMs.

title: DRESS : Instructing Large Vision-Language Models to Align and Interact with Humans via Natural Language Feedback
proposal_tldr: We present DRESS , a large vision language model (LVLM) that innovatively exploits Natural Language feedback (NLF) from Large Language Models to enhance its alignment and interactions by addressing two key limitations in the state-of-the-art LVLMs. First, prior LVLMs generally rely only on the instr

title: SoK: Agentic Skills - Beyond Tool Use in LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper analyzes the security and governance implications of skill-based agents, covering supply-chain risks, prompt injection via skill payloads, and trust-tiered execution, grounded by a case study of the ClawHavoc campaign.

title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes GuardAgent, the first guardrail agent to protect target agents by dynamically checking whether their actions satisfy given safety guard requests, and proposes two novel benchmarks: EICU-AC benchmark to assess the access control for healthcare agents and Mind2Web-SC benchmark to evaluate the safety policies for web agents.

title: AIOS: LLM Agent Operating System
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a novel architecture for serving LLM-based agents by isolating resources and LLM-specific services from agent applications into an AIOS kernel, and introduces a comprehensive suite of APIs designed for utilizing functionalities provided by the AIOS kernel.

title: AMEX: Android Multi-annotation Expo Dataset for Mobile GUI Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The Android Multi-annotation EXpo (AMEX), a comprehensive, large-scale dataset designed for generalist mobile GUI-control agents which are capable of completing tasks by directly interacting with the graphical user interface (GUI) on mobile devices, is introduced.

title: AgentTrek: Agent Trajectory Synthesis via Guiding Replay with Web Tutorials
proposal_tldr: This work demonstrates that guided replay using web tutorials is a practical and scalable strategy for training advanced GUI agents, paving the way for more capable and autonomous digital assistants.

title: WebCanvas: Benchmarking Web Agents in Online Environments
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebCanvas, an innovative online evaluation framework for web agents that effectively addresses the dynamic nature of web interactions, and opens-source an agent framework with extensible modules for reasoning, providing a foundation for the community to conduct online inference and evaluations.

title: WebPilot: A Versatile and Autonomous Multi-Agent System for Web Task Execution with Strategic Exploration
proposal_tldr: WebPilot is developed, a multi-agent system with a dual optimization strategy that improves MCTS to better handle complex web environments, and advances autonomous agents, enabling more reliable decision-making in practical environments.

title: Evaluating Language-Model Agents on Realistic Autonomous Tasks
proposal_tldr: The ability of language model agents to acquire resources, create copies of themselves, and adapt to novel challenges they encounter in the wild is explored, and it is expected that fine-tuning of the existing models could produce substantially more competent agents, even if the fine- tuning is not directly targeted at ARA.

title: ScreenAgent: A Vision Language Model-driven Computer Control Agent
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: This paper constructs an environment for a Vision Language Model (VLM) agent to interact with a real computer screen and designs an automated control pipeline that includes planning, acting, and reflecting phases, guiding the agent to continuously interact with the environment and complete multi-step tasks.

title: xLAM: A Family of Large Action Models to Empower AI Agent Systems
proposal_tldr: The xLAM series includes five models with both dense and mixture-of-expert architectures, trained using a scalable, flexible pipeline that unifies, augments, and synthesizes diverse datasets to enhance AI agents' generalizability and performance across varied environments.

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work develops Task Shield, a test-time defense mechanism that systematically verifies whether each instruction and tool call contributes to user-specified goals, and demonstrates that Task Shield reduces attack success rates while maintaining high task utility on GPT-4o.

title: Motif: Intrinsic Motivation from Artificial Intelligence Feedback
proposal_tldr: Motif is based on the idea of grounding LLMs for decision-making without requiring them to interact with the environment: it elicits preferences from an LLM over pairs of captions to construct an intrinsic reward, which is then used to train agents with reinforcement learning.

title: Agentic AI for Scientific Discovery: A Survey of Progress, Challenges, and Future Directions
proposal_tldr: This survey provides a comprehensive overview of Agentic AI for scientific discovery, categorizing existing systems and tools, and highlighting recent progress across fields such as chemistry, biology, and materials science.

title: xbench: Tracking Agents Productivity Scaling with Profession-Aligned Real-World Evaluations
proposal_tldr: This work introduces xbench, a dynamic, profession-aligned evaluation suite designed to bridge the gap between AI agent capabilities and real-world productivity, and presents initial evaluation results for leading contemporary agents, establishing a baseline for these professional domains.

title: AndroidLab: Training and Systematic Benchmarking of Android Autonomous Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes AndroidLab as a systematic Android agent framework, which includes an operation environment with different modalities, action space, and a reproducible benchmark that supports both large language models (LLMs) and multimodal models (LMMs) in the same action space.

title: MindAgent: Emergent Gaming Interaction
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel infrastructure - MindAgent - to evaluate planning and coordination emergent capabilities for gaming interaction and introduces CUISINEWORLD, a new gaming scenario and related benchmark that dispatch a multi-agent collaboration efficiency and supervise multiple agents playing the game simultaneously.

title: BOLAA: Benchmarking and Orchestrating LLM-augmented Autonomous Agents
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive comparison of LAA in terms of both agent architectures and LLM backbones is provided and a new strategy to orchestrate multiple LAAs such that each labor LAA focuses on one type of action, BOLAA, where a controller manages the communication among multiple agents.

title: MLGym: A New Framework and Benchmark for Advancing AI Research Agents
proposal_tldr: It is found that current frontier models can improve on the given baselines, usually by finding better hyperparameters, but do not generate novel hypotheses, algorithms, architectures, or substantial improvements.

title: VisualWebBench: How Far Have Multimodal LLMs Evolved in Web Page Understanding and Grounding?
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces \bench{}, a multimodal benchmark designed to assess the capabilities of MLLMs across a variety of web tasks, and evaluates 14 open-source MLLMs, Gemini Pro, Claude-3 series, and GPT-4V(ision) on \bench{}, revealing significant challenges and performance gaps.

title: PPTAgent: Generating and Evaluating Presentations Beyond Text-to-Slides
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: PPTAgent is proposed, which comprehensively improves presentation generation through a two-stage, edit-based approach inspired by human workflows, and PPTEval, an evaluation framework that assesses presentations across three dimensions: Content, Design, and Coherence.

title: PlanGenLLMs: A Modern Survey of LLM Planning Capabilities
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This survey aims to offer a comprehensive overview of current LLM planners and examines six key performance criteria: completeness, executability, optimality, representation, generalization, and efficiency.

title: MCP-Universe: Benchmarking Large Language Models with Real-World Model Context Protocol Servers
proposal_tldr: MCP-Universe is introduced, the first comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs in realistic and hard tasks through interaction with real-world MCP servers, and implements execution-based evaluators, including format evaluators for agent format compliance, static evaluators for time-invariant content matching, and dynamic evaluators that automatically retrieve real-time ground truth for temporally sensitive tasks.

title: Inducing Programmatic Skills for Agentic Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work proposes agent skill induction (ASI), which allows agents to adapt themselves by inducing, verifying, and utilizing program-based skills on the fly, and finds that ASI can effectively reuse common skills, while also updating incompatible skills to versatile website changes.

title: VisualAgentBench: Towards Large Multimodal Models as Visual Foundation Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces VisualAgentBench (VAB), a comprehensive and pioneering benchmark specifically designed to train and evaluate LMMs as visual foundation agents across diverse scenarios, including Embodied, Graphical User Interface, and Visual Design, with tasks formulated to probe the depth of LMMs' understanding and interaction capabilities.

title: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
proposal_tldr: This work proposes AgentRewardBench, the first benchmark to assess the effectiveness of LLM judges for evaluating web agents, and finds that no single LLM excels across all benchmarks.

title: Agent-FLAN: Designing Data and Methods of Effective Agent Tuning for Large Language Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Through careful decomposition and redesign of the training corpus, Agent-FLAN enables Llama2-7B to outperform prior best works by 3.5\% across various agent evaluation datasets and consistently improves the agent capability of LLMs when scaling model sizes while slightly enhancing the general capability of LLMs.

title: Before Generation, Align it! A Novel and Effective Strategy for Mitigating Hallucinations in Text-to-SQL Generation
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work identifies and categorizes the common types of hallucinations at each stage in text-to-SQL and introduces a novel strategy, Task Alignment (TA), designed to mitigate hallucinations at each stage, and proposes TA-SQL, a text-to-SQL framework based on this strategy.

title: Lifelong Learning of Large Language Model Based Agents: A Roadmap
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
proposal_tldr: This survey is the first to systematically summarize the potential techniques for incorporating lifelong learning into LLM-based agents, and categorize the core components of these agents into three modules: the perception module for multimodal input integration, the memory module for storing and retrieving evolving knowledge, and the action module for grounded interactions with the dynamic environment.

title: Lemur: Harmonizing Natural Language and Code for Language Agents
proposal_tldr: Lemur and Lemur-Chat are introduced, openly accessible language models optimized for both natural language and coding capabilities to serve as the backbone of versatile language agents, demonstrating balanced proficiencies in both domains, unlike existing open-source models that tend to specialize in either.

title: GUI-Actor: Coordinate-Free Visual Grounding for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: gui-Actor, a VLM-based method for coordinate-free GUI grounding that introduces an attention-based action head that learns to align a dedicatedtoken with all relevant visual patch tokens, enabling the model to propose one or more action regions in a single forward pass, and designs a grounding verifier to evaluate and select the most plausible action region from the candidates proposed for action execution.

title: Put Your Money Where Your Mouth Is: Evaluating Strategic Planning and Execution of LLM Agents in an Auction Arena
proposal_tldr: This research demonstrates that LLMs, such as GPT-4, possess key skills for auction participation, such as budget management and goal adherence, which improve with adaptive strategies, which highlights LLMs' potential in modeling complex social interactions in competitive contexts.

title: Open Challenges in Multi-Agent Security: Towards Secure Systems of Interacting AI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces multi-agent security, a new field dedicated to securing networks of AI agents against threats that emerge or amplify through their interactions with each other, humans, and institutions, and characterise fundamental security-utility and security-security trade-offs across both distributed and decentralised settings.

title: KnowAgent: Knowledge-Augmented Planning for LLM-Based Agents
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces KnowAgent, a novel approach designed to enhance the planning capabilities of LLMs by incorporating explicit action knowledge, and employs an action knowledge base and a knowledgeable self-learning strategy to constrain the action path during planning, enabling more reasonable trajectory synthesis, and thereby enhancing the planning performance of language agents.

title: Large Language Models Empowered Personalized Web Agents
proposal_tldr: A Personalized User Memory-enhanced Alignment (PUMA) framework is proposed to adapt LLM-empowered personalized Web agents to adapt LLMs to the personalized Web agent task, and extensive experiments validate the superiority of PUMA over existing Web agents on PersonalWAB.

title: From Pixels to Insights: A Survey on Automatic Chart Understanding in the Era of Large Foundation Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
proposal_tldr: This survey paper provides a comprehensive overview of the recent developments, challenges, and future directions in chart understanding within the context of large foundation models, and examines various modeling strategies that enhance chart understanding performance.

title: Beyond Browsing: API-Based Web Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes two varieties of agents: an API-calling agent that attempts to perform online tasks through APIs only, similar to traditional coding agents, and a Hybrid Agent that can interact with online data through both web browsing and APIs.

title: Agent-E: From Autonomous Web Navigation to Foundational Design Principles in Agentic Systems
proposal_tldr: The learnings from the development of Agent-E are synthesized into general design principles for developing agentic systems that include the use of domain-specific primitive skills, the importance of distillation and de-noising of environmental observations, the advantages of a hierarchical architecture, and the role of agentic self-improvement to enhance agent efficiency and efficacy as the agent gathers experience.

title: PaSa: An LLM Agent for Comprehensive Academic Paper Search
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: We introduce PaSa, an advanced Paper Search agent powered by large language models. PaSa can autonomously make a series of decisions, including invoking search tools, reading papers, and selecting relevant references, to ultimately obtain comprehensive and accurate results for complex scholar querie

title: Empowering LLM to use Smartphone for Intelligent Task Automation
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Auto-Droid, a mobile task automation system that can handle arbitrary tasks on any Android application without manual efforts and aims to combine the commonsense knowledge of LLMs and domain-specific knowledge of apps through automated dynamic analysis.

title: Agent Lumos: Unified and Modular Training for Open-Source Language Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces LUMOS, one of the first frameworks for training open-source LLM-based agents with a learnable, unified, and modular architecture with a planning module that learns high-level subgoal generation, and a grounding module trained to translate these into actions using various tools in the execution module.

title: Self-evolving Agents with reflective and memory-augmented abilities
proposal_tldr: This research proposes a novel framework by integrating iterative feedback, reflective mechanisms, and a memory optimization mechanism based on the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve that significantly enhances the agents' capabilities in handling multi-tasking and long-span information.

title: MindSearch: Mimicking Human Minds Elicits Deep AI Searcher
proposal_tldr: MindSearch is introduced to mimic the human minds in web information seeking and integration, which can be instantiated by a simple yet effective LLM-based multi-agent framework, and demonstrates significant improvement in the response quality in terms of depth and breadth.

title: CRMArena: Understanding the Capacity of LLM Agents to Perform Professional CRM Tasks in Realistic Environments
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The findings highlight the need for enhanced agent capabilities in function-calling and rule-following to be deployed in real-world work environments and introduce CRMArena, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on realistic tasks grounded in professional work environments.

title: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
proposal_tldr: MemoryArena is introduced, a unified evaluation gym for benchmarking agent memory in multi-session Memory-Agent-Environment loops with explicitly interdependent subtasks, where agents must learn from earlier actions and feedback by distilling experiences into memory, and subsequently use that memory to guide later actions to solve the overall task.

title: Ask-before-Plan: Proactive Language Agents for Real-World Planning
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: A novel multi-agent framework, Clarification-Execution-Planning (\texttt{CEP}), which consists of three agents specialized in clarification, execution, and planning is proposed, which introduces the trajectory tuning scheme for the clarification agent and static execution agent, as well as the memory recollection mechanism for the dynamic execution agent.

title: StateFlow: Enhancing LLM Task-Solving through State-Driven Workflows
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes StateFlow, a novel LLM-based task-solving paradigm that conceptualizes complex task-solving processes as state machines and distinguishes between process grounding and sub-task solving through actions within a state, enhancing control and interpretability of the task-solving procedure.

title: Toward large reasoning models: A survey of reinforced reasoning with large language models
proposal_tldr: This survey reviews recent progress in LLM reasoning and covers foundational concepts behind LLMs and the key technical components that contribute to the development of large reasoning models, and it highlights popular open-source projects for building these models.

title: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an iterative self-training framework, Agent-R, that enables language Agent to Reflect on the fly, and demonstrates that Agent-R continuously improves the model's ability to recover from errors and enables timely error correction.

title: AutoGuide: Automated Generation and Selection of Context-Aware Guidelines for Large Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: A novel framework, called AutoGuide, is introduced, which addresses this limitation by automatically generating context-aware guidelines from offline experiences, and demonstrates that AutoGuide significantly outperforms competitive baselines in complex benchmark domains, including real-world web navigation.

title: A Survey on the Optimization of Large Language Model-based Agents
proposal_tldr: This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-based agent optimization approaches, categorizing them into parameter-driven and parameter-free methods, and discusses the major challenges and promising future directions.

title: Explorer: Scaling Exploration-driven Web Trajectory Synthesis for Multimodal Web Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper develops a scalable recipe to synthesize the largest and most diverse trajectory-level dataset to date, containing over 94K successful multimodal web trajectories, spanning 49K unique URLs, 720K screenshots, and 33M web elements, and trains Explorer, a multimodal web agent.

title: Collaborative Gym: A Framework for Enabling and Evaluating Human-Agent Collaboration
proposal_tldr: Co-Gym is introduced, an open framework for developing and evaluating collaborative agents that engage in bidirectional communication with humans while interacting with task environments and enables the implementation of new task environments and coordination between humans and agents through a flexible, non-turn-taking interaction paradigm.

title: From language to action: a review of large language models as autonomous agents and tool users
proposal_tldr: This review examines recent developments in employing LLMs as autonomous agents and tool users and identifies critical findings on verifiable reasoning of LLMs, the capacity for self-improvement, and the personalization of LLM-based agents.

title: AgentPRM: Process Reward Models for LLM Agents via Step-Wise Promise and Progress
proposal_tldr: This work explores constructing process reward models (PRMs) to evaluate each decision and guide the agent's decision-making process, and proposes a re-defined PRM for agent tasks, named AgentPRM, to capture both the interdependence between sequential decisions and their contribution to the final goal.

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work empirically validate the effectiveness of DRIFT on the AgentDojo, ASB, and AgentDyn benchmark, demonstrating its strong security performance while maintaining high utility across diverse models, showcasing both its robustness and adaptability.

title: UI-Vision: A Desktop-centric GUI Benchmark for Visual Perception and Interaction
proposal_tldr: UI-Vision is introduced, the first comprehensive, license-permissive benchmark for offline, fine-grained evaluation of computer use agents in real-world desktop environments, and is released as open-source to advance the development of more capable agents for real-world desktop tasks.

title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for LLM Multi-Step Reasoning
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: O (Offline Reasoning Optimization), an offline RL method for enhancing LLM multi-step reasoning, jointly learns a policy model and value function by optimizing the soft Bellman Equation and surpasses existing offline learning methods on multi-step reasoning benchmarks.

title: Understanding the Weakness of Large Language Model Agents within a Complex Android Environment
proposal_tldr: This work identifies a lack of four key capabilities, i.e. understanding, reasoning, exploration, and reflection, as primary reasons for the failure of LLM agents, and provides empirical analysis on the failure of reflection.

title: LASER: LLM Agent with State-Space Exploration for Web Navigation
proposal_tldr: This work proposes to model the interactive task as state space exploration, where the LLM agent transitions among a pre-defined set of states by performing actions to complete the task, which enables flexible backtracking, allowing the model to recover from errors easily.

title: The Obvious Invisible Threat: LLM-Powered GUI Agents' Vulnerability to Fine-Print Injections
proposal_tldr: The findings suggest that GUI agents are highly vulnerable, particularly to contextually embedded threats, and propose practical defense strategies to inform the development of safer and more reliable GUI agents.

title: Fully Autonomous AI Agents Should Not be Developed
proposal_tldr: This paper argues that fully autonomous AI agents should not be developed. In support of this position, we build from prior scientific literature and current product marketing to delineate different AI agent levels and detail the ethical values at play in each, documenting trade-offs in potential be

title: SteP: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions
proposal_tldr: Stacked LLM Policies for Web Actions is proposed, an approach to dynamically compose policies to solve a diverse set of web tasks and is competitive with prior works while using significantly less data.

title: AgentGym-RL: Training LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Decision Making through Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: AgentGym-RL, a new framework to train LLM agents for multi-turn interactive decision-making through RL, features a modular and decoupled architecture, ensuring high flexibility and extensibility, and proposes ScalingInter-RL, a training approach designed for exploration-exploitation balance and stable RL optimization.

title: UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces UserBench, a user-centric benchmark designed to evaluate agents in multi-turn, preference-driven interactions, and reveals a significant disconnect between task completion and user alignment.

title: AgentRxiv: Towards Collaborative Autonomous Research
proposal_tldr: AgentRxiv-a framework that lets LLM agent laboratories upload and retrieve reports from a shared preprint server in order to collaborate, share insights, and iteratively build on each other's research, suggests that autonomous agents may play a role in designing future AI systems alongside humans.

title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
proposal_tldr: A new generation of state-of-the-art foundation models that deliver frontier intelligence and industry-leading price performance are presented, and benchmarking results for core capabilities, agentic performance, long context, functional adaptation, runtime performance, and human evaluation are reported.

title: MobileAgentBench: An Efficient and User-Friendly Benchmark for Mobile LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper evaluates several existing mobile agents, including AppAgent and MobileAgent, to thoroughly and systematically compare their performance and proposes an efficient and user-friendly benchmark, MobileAgentBench, designed to alleviate the burden of extensive manual testing.

title: AgentLite: A Lightweight Library for Building and Advancing Task-Oriented LLM Agent System
proposal_tldr: AgentLite is a task-oriented framework designed to enhance the ability of agents to break down tasks and facilitate the development of multi-agent systems and introduces multiple practical applications developed with AgentLite to demonstrate its convenience and flexibility.

title: Large Language Model Instruction Following: A Survey of Progresses and Challenges
proposal_tldr: This survey tries to summarize and provide insights into the current research on instruction following by answering the following questions: What is task instruction, and what instruction types exist?

title: Agent Learning via Early Experience
proposal_tldr: In environments with verifiable rewards, the results provide promising signals that early experience offers a strong foundation for subsequent reinforcement learning, making it a practical bridge between imitation learning and fully experience-driven agents.

title: A Survey on (M)LLM-Based GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This survey identifies key technical challenges, including accurate element localization, effective knowledge retrieval, long-horizon planning, and safety-aware execution control, while outlining promising research directions for enhancing GUI Agents' capabilities.

title: ContextAgent: Context-Aware Proactive LLM Agents with Open-World Sensory Perceptions
proposal_tldr: ContextAgent is introduced, the first context-aware proactive agent that incorporates extensive sensory contexts surrounding humans to enhance the proactivity of LLM agents and can inspire the development of more advanced, human-centric, proactive AI assistants.

title: ExACT: Teaching AI Agents to Explore with Reflective-MCTS and Exploratory Learning
proposal_tldr: ExACT, an approach to combine test-time search and self-learning to build o1-like models for agentic applications, is presented, suggesting a promising research direction to enhance VLMs' capabilities for agentic applications via test-time search and self-learning.

title: MobileVLM: A Vision-Language Model for Better Intra- and Inter-UI Understanding
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a VLM called MobileVLM, which includes two additional pre-training stages to enhance both intra- and inter-UI understanding, and defines four UI-based pre-training tasks, enabling the model to better perceive fine-grained elements and capture page transition actions.

title: LLM-Based Framework for Administrative Task Automation in Healthcare
venue: International Symposium on Digital Forensics and Security
proposal_tldr: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been transformative in the healthcare sector, leading to enhanced precision in medical diagnosis, more effective treatment options, and a significant improvement in patient safety. However, computer-based administrative tasks, such as retrieval of medical and health

title: MMBench-GUI: Hierarchical Multi-Platform Evaluation Framework for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MMBench-GUI, a hierarchical benchmark for evaluating GUI automation agents across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and Web platforms, and proposes a novel Efficiency-Quality Area (EQA) metric to assess GUI agent execution efficiency in online automation scenarios.

title: Middleware for LLMs: Tools Are Instrumental for Language Agents in Complex Environments
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a novel class of tools, termed *middleware*, to aid in the proactive exploration within these massive environments of large language models, and demonstrates the significant potential of augmenting language agents with tools in complex environments.

title: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
proposal_tldr: This work proposes SEAgent, an agentic self-evolving framework enabling CUAs to autonomously evolve through interactions with unfamiliar software, and introduces a specialist-to-generalist training strategy that integrates individual experiential insights from specialist agents, facilitating the development of a stronger generalist CUA capable of continuous autonomous evolution.

title: Spider2-V: How Far Are Multimodal Agents From Automating Data Science and Engineering Workflows?
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces Spider2-V, the first multimodal agent benchmark focusing on professional data science and engineering workflows, featuring 494 real-world tasks in authentic computer environments and incorporating 20 enterprise-level professional applications and hopes that it paves the way for autonomous multimodal agents to transform the automation of data science and engineering workflow.

title: NESTFUL: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Nested Sequences of API Calls
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: NESTFUL is presented, a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on nested sequences of API calls, i.e., sequences where the output of one API call is passed as input to a subsequent call.

title: OfficeBench: Benchmarking Language Agents across Multiple Applications for Office Automation
proposal_tldr: OfficeBench, one of the first office automation benchmarks for evaluating current LLM agents' capability to address office tasks in realistic office workflows, is introduced and it is observed that most issues are related to operation redundancy and hallucinations, as well as limitations in switching between multiple applications, which may provide valuable insights for developing effective agent frameworks for office automation.

title: AGILE: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Framework of LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: We introduce a novel reinforcement learning framework of LLM agents named AGILE (AGent that Interacts and Learns from Environments) designed to perform complex conversational tasks with users, leveraging LLMs, memory, tools, and interactions with experts. The agent possesses capabilities beyond conv

title: AgentRL: Scaling Agentic Reinforcement Learning with a Multi-Turn, Multi-Task Framework
proposal_tldr: Experiments show that AgentRL, trained on open LLMs across five agentic tasks, significantly outperforms GPT-5, Clause-Sonnet-4, DeepSeek-R1, and other open-source LLM agents and matches the best results among all task-specific models.

title: Simulacrum of Stories: Examining Large Language Models as Qualitative Research Participants
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: It is argued that the use of LLMs as proxies for participants enacts the surrogate effect, raising ethical and epistemological concerns that extend beyond the technical limitations of current models to the core of whether LLMs fit within qualitative ways of knowing.

title: Ferret-UI 2: Mastering Universal User Interface Understanding Across Platforms
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces Ferret-UI 2, a multimodal large language model (MLLM) designed for universal UI understanding across a wide range of platforms, including iPhone, Android, iPad, Webpage, and AppleTV, and shows strong cross-platform transfer capabilities.

title: AgentBank: Towards Generalized LLM Agents via Fine-Tuning on 50000+ Interaction Trajectories
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentBank, by far the largest trajectory tuning data collection featuring more than 50k diverse high-quality interaction trajectories which comprises 16 tasks covering five distinct agent skill dimensions and fine-tune LLMs on AgentBank to get a series of agent models, Samoyed.

title: AgentOhana: Design Unified Data and Training Pipeline for Effective Agent Learning
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces \textbf{AgentOhana} as a comprehensive solution to address challenges faced by autonomous agents powered by large language models, and presents \textbf{xLAM-v0.1}, a large action model tailored for AI agents, which demonstrates exceptional performance across various benchmarks.

title: Language Models, Agent Models, and World Models: The LAW for Machine Reasoning and Planning
proposal_tldr: It is proposed that world and agent models are a better abstraction of reasoning, that introduces the crucial elements of deliberate human-like reasoning, including beliefs about the world and other agents, anticipation of consequences, goals/rewards, and strategic planning.

title: Lumos: Learning Agents with Unified Data, Modular Design, and Open-Source LLMs
proposal_tldr: L UMOS surpasses GPT-4/3.5-based agents in complex question answering and web tasks, while equalling the performance of significantly larger LLM agents on math tasks and out-performs open-source agents created through conventional training methods and those using chain-of-thoughts training.

title: WorkBench: a Benchmark Dataset for Agents in a Realistic Workplace Setting
proposal_tldr: It is found that agents' errors can result in the wrong action being taken, such as an email being sent to the wrong person, and raising questions about their use in high-stakes workplace settings.

title: MMInA: Benchmarking Multihop Multimodal Internet Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: MMInA, a multihop and multimodal benchmark to evaluate the embodied agents for compositional Internet tasks, and proposes a novel protocol for evaluating an agent's progress in completing multihop tasks, ensuring a high degree of realism and applicability to natural user tasks.

title: OS Agents: A Survey on MLLM-based Agents for General Computing Devices Use
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive survey of OS Agents research, exploring their key components including the environment, observation space, and action space, and outlining essential capabilities such as understanding, planning, and grounding to consolidate the state of OS Agents research.

title: AdvAgent: Controllable Blackbox Red-teaming on Web Agents
proposal_tldr: AdvAgent is proposed, a black-box red-teaming framework for attacking web agents that employs a reinforcement learning-based pipeline to train an adversarial prompter model that optimizes adversarial prompts using feedback from the black-box agent.

title: R2-Guard: Robust Reasoning Enabled LLM Guardrail via Knowledge-Enhanced Logical Reasoning
proposal_tldr: This work proposes R^2-Guard, a robust reasoning enabled LLM guardrail via knowledge-enhanced logical reasoning that significantly surpasses SOTA method LlamaGuard and demonstrates the robustness of $R^2$-Guard against four SOTA jailbreaking attacks.

title: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows
