proposal_tldr: OdysseyBench is introduced, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon workflows across diverse office applications including Word, Excel, PDF, Email, and Calendar and HomerAgents, a multi-agent framework that automates the generation of long-horizon workflow benchmarks through systematic environment exploration, task generation, and dialogue synthesis.

title: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems
proposal_tldr: It is argued that human-in-the-loop agentic systems offer a promising path forward, combining human oversight and control with AI efficiency to unlock productivity from imperfect systems.

title: WebEvolver: Enhancing Web Agent Self-Improvement with Coevolving World Model
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel framework that introduces a co-evolving World Model LLM, leveraging LLMs'pretrained knowledge of abundant web content, and establishes the necessity of integrating world models into autonomous agent frameworks to unlock sustained adaptability.

title: Contextual Experience Replay for Self-Improvement of Language Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Contextual Experience Replay (CER), a training-free framework to enable efficient self-improvement for language agents in their context window that accumulates and synthesizes past experiences into a dynamic memory buffer, allowing the agents to retrieve and augment themselves with relevant knowledge in new tasks, enhancing their adaptability in complex environments.

title: Proposer-Agent-Evaluator(PAE): Autonomous Skill Discovery For Foundation Model Internet Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Proposer-Agent-Evaluator, an effective learning system that enables foundation model agents to autonomously discover and practice skills in the wild that generalizes real-world human-annotated benchmarks with SOTA performances.

title: On the Multi-turn Instruction Following for Conversational Web Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: To tackle the limited context length of LLMs and the context-dependency issue of the conversational tasks, a novel framework is proposed, named self-reflective memory-augmented planning (Self-MAP), which employs memory utilization and self-reflection techniques.

title: CMMMU: A Chinese Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding Benchmark
proposal_tldr: CMMMU is introduced, a new Chinese Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding benchmark designed to evaluate LMMs on tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning in a Chinese context, inspired by and strictly follows the annotation and analysis pattern of MMMU.

title: AgentRefine: Enhancing Agent Generalization through Refinement Tuning
proposal_tldr: The findings establish the correlation between agent generalization and self-refinement and provide a new paradigm for future research as AgentRefine significantly outperforms state-of-the-art agent-tuning work in terms of generalization ability on diverse agent tasks.

title: Agentic AI Security: Threats, Defenses, Evaluation, and Open Challenges
proposal_tldr: This survey outlines a taxonomy of threats specific to agentic AI, reviews recent benchmarks and evaluation methodologies, and discusses defense strategies from both technical and governance perspectives, aiming to support the development of secure-by-design agent systems.

title: Advancing Tool-Augmented Large Language Models: Integrating Insights from Errors in Inference Trees
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a novel method for constructing step-wise preference data from tree-like expert trajectories, which leverages the previously ignored failed explorations in the decision trees and proposes an inference trajectory optimization framework based on preference learning to address this limitation.

title: EduAgent: Generative Student Agents in Learning
proposal_tldr: EduAgent is proposed, a novel generative agent framework incorporating cognitive prior knowledge to guide LLMs to first reason correlations among various behaviors and then make simulations, and could not only mimic and predict learning behaviors of real students but also generate realistic learning behaviors of virtual students without real data.

title: MLLM-CompBench: A Comparative Reasoning Benchmark for Multimodal LLMs
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces MLLM-CompBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate the comparative reasoning capability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and uses MLLM-COMPBENCH, a foundation for future enhancements in the comparative capability of MLLMs.

title: LLM as OS, Agents as Apps: Envisioning AIOS, Agents and the AIOS-Agent Ecosystem
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces the new AIOS-Agent Ecosystem, where users can easily program Agent Applications (AAPs) using natural language, democratizing the development of software, which is different from the traditional OS-APP ecosystem.

title: CowPilot: A Framework for Autonomous and Human-Agent Collaborative Web Navigation
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: CowPilot is proposed, a framework supporting autonomous as well as human-agent collaborative web navigation, and evaluation across task success and task efficiency, which can serve as a useful tool for data collection and agent evaluation across websites and will enable research in how users and agents can work together.

title: OpenWebVoyager: Building Multimodal Web Agents via Iterative Real-World Exploration, Feedback and Optimization
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces an open-source framework designed to facilitate the development of multimodal web agent that can autonomously conduct real-world exploration and improve itself, demonstrating strong performance across multiple test sets.

title: ASSISTGUI: Task-Oriented Desktop Graphical User Interface Automation
proposal_tldr: An advanced Actor-Critic Embodied Agent framework is proposed, which incorporates a sophisticated GUI parser driven by an LLM-agent and an enhanced reasoning mechanism adept at handling lengthy procedural tasks that outshine existing methods in performance.

title: AgentCPM-GUI: Building Mobile-Use Agents with Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: The training pipeline includes grounding-aware pre-training to enhance perception, supervised fine-tuning on high-quality Chinese and English trajectories to imitate human-like actions, and reinforcement fine-tuning with GRPO to improve reasoning capability, and a compact action space that reduces output length and supports low-latency execution on mobile devices.

title: Know where to go: Make LLM a relevant, responsible, and trustworthy searchers
Simulating Environments with Reasoning Models for Agent Training
proposal_tldr: This paper demonstrates that LLMs can simulate realistic environment feedback without access to actual testbed data or APIs, and proposes two frameworks: Simia-SFT, a pipeline that synthesizes SFT data by amplifying small seed sets into diverse trajectories in an environment-agnostic manner, and Simia-RL, a framework that enables RL training without real environment implementations through LLM-simulated feedback.

title: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
proposal_tldr: RedTeamCUA is proposed, an adversarial testing framework featuring a novel hybrid sandbox that integrates a VM-based OS environment with Docker-based web platforms that provides an essential framework for advancing realistic, controlled, and systematic analysis of CUA vulnerabilities.

title: AgentVigil: Generic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a generic black-box fuzzing framework, AgentVigil, designed to automatically discover and exploit indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse LLM agents, and exhibits strong transferability across unseen tasks and internal LLMs, as well as promising results against defenses.

title: AgentStudio: A Toolkit for Building General Virtual Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentStudio, a trinity of environments, tools, and benchmarks to address fundamental agent abilities, including GUI grounding, learning from videos, and success detection, pointing to the desiderata for robust, general, and open-ended virtual agents.

title: AdvWeb: Controllable Black-box Attacks on VLM-powered Web Agents
AutoWebGLM: Bootstrap And Reinforce A Large Language Model-based Web Navigating Agent
proposal_tldr: Inspired by human browsing patterns, an HTML simplification algorithm is designed to represent webpages, preserving vital information succinctly and bootstrap the model by reinforcement learning and rejection sampling to further facilitate webpage comprehension, browser operations, and efficient task decomposition by itself.

title: Less Defined Knowledge and More True Alarms: Reference-based Phishing Detection without a Pre-defined Reference List
proposal_tldr: This work designs PhishLLM to decode (or retrieve) the domain-brand relationships from LLM and effectively parse the credential-taking intention of a web-page, without the cost of maintaining and updating an explicit reference list, and introduces a search-engine-based validation mechanism to remove the misinformation.

title: Harnessing Uncertainty: Entropy-Modulated Policy Gradients for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: Entropy-Modulated Policy Gradients (EMPG), a framework that re-calibrates the learning signal based on step-wise uncertainty and the final task outcome, is proposed and achieves substantial performance gains and significantly outperforms strong policy gradient baselines.

title: REAL: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Deterministic Simulations of Real Websites
proposal_tldr: This work introduces REAL, a benchmark and framework for multi-turn agent evaluations on deterministic simulations of real-world websites, and releases a benchmark consisting of 112 practical tasks that mirror everyday complex user interactions requiring both accurate information retrieval and state-changing actions.

title: Open Models, Closed Minds? On Agents Capabilities in Mimicking Human Personalities through Open Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This work conducts an in-depth investigation of a significant body of 12 LLM Agents based on the most representative Open models, through the two most well-known psychological assessment tests, namely Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) and Big Five Inventory (BFI).

title: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: It is shown that current CUAs and BUAs can be deceived at rates of up to 51% and 100%, respectively, on certain platforms, and the need for robust, context-aware defenses to ensure the safe deployment of multimodal AI agents in real-world environments is highlighted.

title: AutoDroid-V2: Boosting SLM-based GUI Agents via Code Generation
venue: ACM SIGMOBILE International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications, and Services
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a document-centered approach that automatically builds fine-grained API documentation for each app and generates diverse task samples based on this documentation, which effectively improves the mobile task automation with significantly higher success rates and lower latency/token consumption.

title: General Agentic Memory Via Deep Research
proposal_tldr: The proposed general agentic memory (GAM) follows the principle of just-in time (JIT) compilation where it focuses on creating optimized contexts for its client at runtime while keeping only simple but useful memory during the offline stage.

title: DeepShop: A Benchmark for Deep Research Shopping Agents
proposal_tldr: A systematic evaluation of retrieval-augmented generation methods, web agents, and deep research systems shows that RAG struggles with complex queries due to its lack of web interaction, while other methods face significant challenges with filters and sorting preferences, leading to low overall success rates.

title: Agent-RLVR: Training Software Engineering Agents via Guidance and Environment Rewards
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Agent-RLVR, a framework that makes RLVR effective in challenging agentic settings, with an initial focus on software engineering tasks, and introduces agent guidance, a mechanism that actively steers the agent towards successful trajectories by leveraging diverse informational cues.

title: Large Language Models for Planning: A Comprehensive and Systematic Survey
proposal_tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive review of LLM-based planning, and discusses the underlying mechanisms enabling LLM-based planning and outline promising research directions for this rapidly evolving field.

title: A Survey of Large Language Model Empowered Agents for Recommendation and Search: Towards Next-Generation Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: The motivations and roles of LLM agents are discussed and a taxonomy is proposed to organize and summarize existing research, highlighting how LLM agents can address key challenges in information retrieval and charts potential directions for future work.

title: ToolTalk: Evaluating Tool-Usage in a Conversational Setting
proposal_tldr: The introduction of ToolTalk, a benchmark consisting of complex user intents requiring multi-step tool usage specified through dialogue, and an analysis of the errors reveals three major categories and suggests some future directions for improvement.

title: Towards General Computer Control: A Multimodal Agent for Red Dead Redemption II as a Case Study
proposal_tldr: This work proposes the General Computer Control (GCC) setting: building foundation agents that can master any computer task by taking only screen images of the computer as input, and producing keyboard and mouse operations as output, similar to human-computer interaction.

title: DeepPlanning: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Agentic Planning with Verifiable Constraints
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: DeepPlanning is introduced, a challenging benchmark for practical long-horizon agent planning that features multi-day travel planning and multi-product shopping tasks that require proactive information acquisition, local constrained reasoning, and global constrained optimization.

title: Thinking vs. Doing: Agents that Reason by Scaling Test-Time Interaction
proposal_tldr: This work proposes to scale test-time interaction, an untapped dimension of test-time scaling that increases the agent's interaction horizon to enable running rich behaviors such as exploration, backtracking, and dynamic re-planning within a single rollout.

title: AdvWave: Stealthy Adversarial Jailbreak Attack against Large Audio-Language Models
proposal_tldr: A dual-phase optimization method is proposed that addresses gradient shattering, enabling effective end-to-end gradient-based optimization and an adaptive adversarial target search algorithm is developed that dynamically adjusts the adversarial optimization target based on the response patterns of LALMs for specific queries.

title: VideoWebArena: Evaluating Long Context Multimodal Agents with Video Understanding Web Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work introduces VideoWebArena (VideoWA), a benchmark for evaluating the capabilities of long-context multimodal agents for video understanding and provides a testbed for future development with long-context video agents.

title: Benchmarking Agentic Workflow Generation
proposal_tldr: WorfBench, a unified workflow generation benchmark with multi-faceted scenarios and intricate graph workflow structures, and WorfEval, a systemic evaluation protocol utilizing subsequence and subgraph matching algorithms to accurately quantify the LLM agent's workflow generation capabilities are introduced.

title: MCPEval: Automatic MCP-based Deep Evaluation for AI Agent Models
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: MCPEval is introduced, an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based framework that automates end-to-end task generation and deep evaluation of LLM agents across diverse domains, and standardizes metrics, seamlessly integrates with native agent tools, and eliminates manual effort in building evaluation pipelines.

title: CRAB: Cross-environment Agent Benchmark for Multimodal Language Model Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Crab is the first agent benchmark framework designed to support cross-environment tasks, incorporating a graph-based fine-grained evaluation method and an efficient mechanism for task and evaluator construction.

title: MCPMark: A Benchmark for Stress-Testing Realistic and Comprehensive MCP Use
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive evaluation of cutting-edge LLMs using a minimal agent framework that operates in a tool-calling loop, significantly surpassing those in previous MCP benchmarks and highlighting the stress-testing nature of MCPMark.

title: ControlAgent: Automating Control System Design via Novel Integration of LLM Agents and Domain Expertise
proposal_tldr: ControlAgent mimics the design processes used by (human) practicing engineers, but removes all the human efforts and can be run in a fully automated way to give end-to-end solutions for control system design with user-specified requirements.

title: A Zero-Shot Language Agent for Computer Control with Structured Reflection
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work presents a zero-shot agent that plans for executable actions on a partially observed environment, and iteratively progresses a task by identifying and learning from its mistakes via self-reflection and structured thought management, which often outperforms recent SoTAs with more efficient reasoning.

title: A Survey of Post-Training Scaling in Large Language Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of post-training scaling, an emergent paradigm aiming to relieve the limitations of traditional pre-training by focusing on the alignment phase, which traditionally accounts for a minor fraction of the total training computation.

title: UI-Venus-1.5 Technical Report
proposal_tldr: This report presents UI-Venus-1.5, a unified, end-to-end GUI Agent designed for robust real-world applications, which synthesizes domain-specific models (grounding, web, and mobile) into one cohesive checkpoint via Model Merging.

title: STeCa: Step-level Trajectory Calibration for LLM Agent Learning
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Step-Level Trajectory Calibration (STeCa), a novel framework for LLM agent learning that identifies suboptimal actions through a step-level reward comparison during exploration, and constructs calibrated trajectories using LLM-driven reflection, enabling agents to learn from improved decision-making processes.

title: AGENTVIGIL: Automatic Black-Box Red-teaming for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: ZeroGUI: Automating Online GUI Learning at Zero Human Cost
proposal_tldr: ZeroGUI is proposed, a scalable, online learning framework for automating GUI Agent training at Zero human cost that integrates VLM-based automatic task generation to produce diverse training goals from the current environment state, and two-stage online reinforcement learning to continuously interact with and learn from GUI environments.

title: Reinforced MLLM: A Survey on RL-Based Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This paper provides a systematic review of recent advances in RL-based reasoning for MLLMs, covering key algorithmic designs, reward mechanism innovations, and practical applications, and highlights two main RL paradigms, value-model-free and value-model-based methods.

title: Toward Generalizable Evaluation in the LLM Era: A Survey Beyond Benchmarks
proposal_tldr: This survey probes the core challenges that the rise of LLMs poses for evaluation, and identifies and analyzes two pivotal transitions: from task-specific to capability-based evaluation and from manual to automated evaluation.

title: Large Language Models and Artificial Intelligence Generated Content Technologies Meet Communication Networks
proposal_tldr: This work aims to deepen the understanding of how LLMs and AIGC can synergize with and enhance the development of advanced intelligent communication networks, contributing to a more profound comprehension of next-generation intelligent communication networks.

title: VideoGUI: A Benchmark for GUI Automation from Instructional Videos
proposal_tldr: VideoGUI is introduced, a novel multi-modal benchmark designed to evaluate GUI assistants on visual-centric GUI tasks, revealing that even the SoTA large multimodal model GPT4o performs poorly on visual-centric GUI tasks, especially for high-level planning.

title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Scaling Agents for Computer Use
Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
proposal_tldr: DreamGym is introduced, the first unified framework designed to synthesize diverse experiences with scalability in mind to enable effective online RL training for autonomous agents, and yields significant additional performance gains while requiring far fewer real-world interactions, providing a scalable warm-start strategy for general-purpose RL.

title: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
proposal_tldr: Morae is a UI agent that automatically identifies decision points during task execution and pauses so that users can make choices, and exemplifies a mixed-initiative approach in which users benefit from the automation of UI agents while being able to express their preferences.

title: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes the first process reward model (PRM) called Web-Shepherd which could assess web navigation trajectories in a step-level and introduces the WebRewardBench, the first meta-evaluation benchmark for evaluating PRMs.

title: Towards Trustworthy GUI Agents: A Survey
proposal_tldr: A workflow-aligned taxonomy is introduced that decomposes trust into Perception Trust, Reasoning Trust, and Interaction Trust, showing how failures propagate across agent pipelines and compound through action/observation loops.

title: iAgent: LLM Agent as a Shield between User and Recommender Systems
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A new user-agent-platform paradigm is proposed, where agent serves as the protective shield between user and recommender system that enables indirect exposure.

title: Inference-Time Computations for LLM Reasoning and Planning: A Benchmark and Insights
proposal_tldr: This work constructs a comprehensive benchmark, known as Sys2Bench, and performs extensive experiments evaluating existing inference-time techniques on eleven diverse tasks across five categories, indicating that simply scaling inference-time computation has limitations, as no single inference-time technique consistently performs well across all reasoning and planning tasks.

title: Large Action Models: From Inception to Implementation
proposal_tldr: This paper provides a detailed, step-by-step guide on the key stages of LAM development, including data collection, model training, environment integration, grounding, and evaluation, and concludes by identifying the current limitations of LAMs.

title: OSCAR: Operating System Control via State-Aware Reasoning and Re-Planning
proposal_tldr: This work presents OSCAR: Operating System Control via state-Aware reasoning and Re-planning, a generalist agent designed to autonomously navigate and interact with various desktop and mobile applications through standardized controls, enabling precise control over graphical user interfaces (GUIs).

title: ComfyBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Agents in ComfyUI for Autonomously Designing Collaborative AI Systems
proposal_tldr: ComfyAgent is developed, a novel framework that empowers LLM-based agents to autonomously design collaborative AI systems by generating workflows and constructs a multi-agent system that cooperates to learn from existing workflows and generate new workflows for a given task.

title: Language Agents: Foundations, Prospects, and Risks
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This proposed tutorial aspires to fill the gap by providing a conceptual framework of language agents as well as giving a comprehensive discussion on important topic areas including tool augmentation, grounding, reasoning and planning, multi-agent systems, and rissk and societal impact.

title: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentSynth, a scalable and cost-efficient pipeline for automatically synthesizing high-quality tasks and trajectory datasets for generalist computer-use agents that achieves a low average cost of $0.60 per trajectory, orders of magnitude cheaper than human annotations.

title: Frontier AI's Impact on the Cybersecurity Landscape
proposal_tldr: This paper comprehensively analyzes the impact of frontier AI in cybersecurity through multiple aspects, including quantitative benchmarks, qualitative literature review, empirical evaluation, and expert survey, and provides concrete calls to action.

title: AI wellbeing
proposal_tldr: It is argued that there is a significant probability that some AI systems have or will soon have wellbeing and that this should lead us to reassess their relationship with the intelligent systems the authors create.

title: The Evolution of Multimodal Model Architectures
proposal_tldr: This work uniquely identifies and characterizes four prevalent multimodal model architectural patterns in the contemporary multimodal landscape and highlights the advantages and disadvantages of each architecture type based on data and compute requirements, architecture complexity, scalability, simplification of adding modalities, training objectives, and any-to-any multimodal generation capability.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainability Behaviors in a Society of LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: Governance of the Commons Simulation (G OV S IM ), a simulation platform designed to study strategic interactions and cooperative decision-making in LLMs, is introduced, finding that by removing the ability of agents to communicate, they overuse the shared resource, highlighting the importance of communication for cooperation.

title: From Assistant to Double Agent: Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks on OpenClaw for Personalized Local AI Agent
proposal_tldr: The proposed Personalized Agent Security Bench (PASB), an end-to-end security evaluation framework tailored for real-world personalized agents, incorporates personalized usage scenarios, realistic toolchains, and long-horizon interactions, enabling black-box, end-to-end security evaluation on real systems.

title: OPeRA: A Dataset of Observation, Persona, Rationale, and Action for Evaluating LLMs on Human Online Shopping Behavior Simulation
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Can large language models (LLMs) accurately simulate the next web action of a specific user? While LLMs have shown promising capabilities in generating ``believable''human behaviors, evaluating their ability to mimic real user behaviors remains an open challenge, largely due to the lack of high-qual

title: GPTVoiceTasker: Advancing Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency Through Dynamic Interface Exploration and Learning
venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
proposal_tldr: GptVoiceTasker is introduced, a virtual assistant poised to enhance user experiences and task efficiency on mobile devices and open-source, inviting further research into LLMs utilization for diverse tasks through prompt engineering and leveraging user usage data to improve efficiency.

title: ClawsBench: Evaluating Capability and Safety of LLM Productivity Agents in Simulated Workspaces
proposal_tldr: ClawsBench, a benchmark for evaluating and improving LLM agents in realistic productivity settings, is introduced and eight recurring patterns of unsafe behavior are identified, including multi-step sandbox escalation and silent contract modification.

title: DynaSaur: Large Language Agents Beyond Predefined Actions
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an LLM agent framework that can dynamically create and compose actions as needed and enables LLM agents to adapt and recover in scenarios where predefined actions are insufficient or fail due to unforeseen edge cases.

title: Planning with Multi-Constraints via Collaborative Language Agents
proposal_tldr: Planning with Multi-Constraints (PMC) is introduced, a zero-shot methodology for collaborative LLM-based multi-agent systems that simplifies complex task planning with constraints by decomposing it into a hierarchy of subordinate tasks.

title: Automating the Enterprise with Foundation Models
proposal_tldr: This work proposes ECLAIR, a system to automate enterprise workflows with minimal human supervision, and identifies human-AI collaboration, validation, and self-improvement as open challenges, and suggests ways they can be solved with data management techniques.

title: TRAD: Enhancing LLM Agents with Step-Wise Thought Retrieval and Aligned Decision
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: A novel framework for large language model agents that not only surpasses state-of-the-art models but also effectively reduces noise and promotes generalization, and has been deployed in real-world scenarios of a global business insurance company and yields an improved success rate of robotic process automation.

title: Mobile-Env: Building Qualified Evaluation Benchmarks for LLM-GUI Interaction
proposal_tldr: Mobile-Env is introduced, a comprehensive toolkit tailored for creating GUI benchmarks in the Android mobile environment that highlights a crucial gap in current models and underscores the importance of developing more capable foundation models and more effective GUI agent frameworks.

title: Fara-7B: An Efficient Agentic Model for Computer Use
proposal_tldr: FaraGen, a novel synthetic data generation system for multi-step web tasks, and Fara-7B, a native CUA model that perceives the computer using only screenshots, executes actions via predicted coordinates, and is small enough to run on-device, are introduced.

title: TripTailor: A Real-World Benchmark for Personalized Travel Planning
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: TripTailor is introduced, a benchmark designed specifically for personalized travel planning in real-world scenarios and identifies several critical challenges in travel planning, including the feasibility, rationality, and personalized customization of the proposed solutions.

title: macOSWorld: A Multilingual Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents macOSWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating GUI agents on macOS, and reveals a dramatic gap: proprietary computer-use agents lead at above 30% success rate, while open-source lightweight research models lag at below 5\%, highlighting the need for macOS domain adaptation.

title: Visual Test-Time Scaling for GUI Agent Grounding
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
proposal_tldr: This work introduces RegionFocus, a visual test-time scaling approach for Vision Language Model Agents that proposes an image-as-map mechanism that visualizes key landmarks at each step, providing a transparent action record and enables the agent to effectively choose among action candidates.

title: Chat with MES: LLM-driven user interface for manipulating garment manufacturing system through natural language
proposal_tldr: Chat with MES (CWM), an AI agent system, which integrates LLMs into the Manufacturing Execution System (MES), serving as the ‘‘ears, mouth, and the brain’’, promotes a paradigm shift in MES interactions from Graphical User Interface to natural language interface, offering a more natural and efficient way for workers to manipulate the manufacturing system.

title: A Survey on Large Language Models for Automated Planning
proposal_tldr: This survey critically investigate existing research on the use of LLMs in automated planning, examining both their successes and shortcomings in detail and advocates for a balanced methodology that leverages the inherent flexibility and generalized knowledge of LLMs alongside the rigor and cost-effectiveness of traditional planning methods.

title: A Survey on Multimodal Benchmarks: In the Era of Large AI Models
proposal_tldr: This survey systematically reviewing 211 benchmarks that assess MLLMs across four core domains: understanding, reasoning, generation, and application provides a detailed analysis of task designs, evaluation metrics, and dataset constructions, across diverse modalities.

title: AssistGUI: Task-Oriented PC Graphical User Interface Automation
UltraCUA: A Foundation Model for Computer Use Agents with Hybrid Action
proposal_tldr: This work establishes a scalable paradigm bridging primitive GUI interactions and high-level tool intelligence, enabling more resilient and adaptable computer use agents for diverse environments and complex real-world tasks.

title: The AI Agent Index
proposal_tldr: The AI Agent Index is introduced, the first public database to document information about currently deployed agentic AI systems, and finds that while developers generally provide ample information regarding the capabilities and applications of agentic systems, they currently provide limited information regarding safety and risk management practices.

title: Odyssey : Empowering Minecraft Agents with Open-World Skills
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Odyssey, a new framework that empowers Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents with open-world skills to explore the vast Minecraft world and demonstrates that the proposed Odyssey framework can effectively evaluate different capabilities of LLM-based agents.

title: Exploring Embodied Multimodal Large Models: Development, Datasets, and Future Directions
proposal_tldr: This paper discusses the evolution of EMLMs, with a focus on embodied perception, navigation, interaction, and simulation, and identifies key challenges faced by EMLMs, including issues of scalability, generalization, and real-time decision-making.

title: Harnessing Webpage UIs for Text-Rich Visual Understanding
proposal_tldr: This work proposes synthesizing general multimodal instructions from webpage UIs using text-based large language models, a dataset containing 7.3 million samples from 1 million websites, covering diverse multimodal tasks and UI layouts that generalize surprisingly well to non-web UI tasks and even to non-UI domains, such as document understanding, OCR, and chart interpretation.

title: A Survey on the Feedback Mechanism of LLM-based AI Agents
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive overview of feedback mechanisms in large language models, categorizing them into four distinct types: internal feedback, external feedback, multi-agent feedback, and human feedback, and highlighting the significant challenges and potential directions for future studies are presented.

title: Chat2Layout: Interactive 3D Furniture Layout With a Multimodal LLM
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Chat2Layout, a novel interactive furniture layout generation system that extends the functionality of MLLMs into the realm of interactive layout design, and establishes a unified vision-question paradigm for in-context learning, enabling seamless communication with MLLMs to steer their behavior without altering model weights.

title: OPID: On-Policy Skill Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: OPID preserves RL as the primary training objective while introducing dense, distribution-matched hindsight supervision, and generally improves agent performance, sample efficiency, and robustness over outcome-only RL and existing skill-distillation baselines.

title: OpenResearcher: A Fully Open Pipeline for Long-Horizon Deep Research Trajectory Synthesis
proposal_tldr: OpenResearcher is presented, a reproducible pipeline that decouples one-time corpus bootstrapping from multi-turn trajectory synthesis and executes the search-and-browse loop entirely offline using three explicit browser primitives: search, open, and find, over a 15M-document corpus.

title: GUI-Xplore: Empowering Generalizable GUI Agents with One Exploration
proposal_tldr: This work introduces GUI-Xplore, a dataset meticulously designed to enhance cross-application and cross-task generalization via an exploration-and-reasoning framework and proposes Xplore-Agent, a GUI agent framework that combines Action-aware GUI Modeling with Graph-Guided Environment Reasoning.

title: BEARCUBS: A benchmark for computer-using web agents
proposal_tldr: BEARCUBS, a "small but mighty"benchmark of 111 information-seeking questions designed to evaluate a web agent's ability to search, browse, and identify factual information from the web, is introduced.

title: AgentRM: Enhancing Agent Generalization with Reward Modeling
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work finds that finetuning a reward model to guide the policy model is more robust than directly finetuning the policy model, and proposes AgentRM, a generalizable reward model, to guide the policy model for effective test-time search.

title: Towards Internet-Scale Training For Agents
proposal_tldr: This work develops a pipeline to facilitate internet-scale training for agents without laborious human annotations, and trains agents based on Qwen 3 1.7B that are competitive with frontier LLMs as web agents, while being smaller and faster.

title: Foundations and Recent Trends in Multimodal Mobile Agents: A Survey
proposal_tldr: This survey provides a comprehensive review of mobile agent technologies, focusing on recent advancements that enhance real-time adaptability and multimodal interaction, and categorizes these advancements into two main approaches: prompt-based methods, which utilize large language models for instruction-based task execution, and training-based methods, which fine-tune multimodal models for mobile-specific applications.

title: RaDA: Retrieval-augmented Web Agent Planning with LLMs
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The proposed RaDA is a novel planning method for Web agents that does not require manual exemplars, efficiently leverages the LLMs’ context, and enhances generalization, and is compared with strong baselines covering a broad space of design choices.

title: The Long-Horizon Task Mirage? Diagnosing Where and Why Agentic Systems Break
proposal_tldr: HORIZON is introduced, an initial cross-domain diagnostic benchmark for systematically constructing tasks and analyzing long-horizon failure behaviors in LLM-based agents and proposes a trajectory-grounded LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline for scalable and reproducible failure attribution.

title: MedBrowseComp: Benchmarking Medical Deep Research and Computer Use
proposal_tldr: This work presents MedBrowseComp, the first benchmark that systematically tests an agent's ability to reliably retrieve and synthesize multi-hop medical facts from live, domain-specific knowledge bases, and sets concrete goals for future model and toolchain upgrades.

title: A Survey on the Safety and Security Threats of Computer-Using Agents: JARVIS or Ultron?
proposal_tldr: A systematization of knowledge on the safety and security threats of CUAs is presented, providing future researchers with a structured foundation for exploring unexplored vulnerabilities and offers practitioners actionable guidance in designing and deploying secure Computer-Using Agents.

title: RealWebAssist: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Web Assistance with Real-World Users
proposal_tldr: RealWebAssist is introduced, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate sequential instruction-following in realistic scenarios involving long-horizon interactions with the web, visual GUI grounding, and understanding ambiguous real-world user instructions.

title: Can LLM Agents Simulate Multi-Turn Human Behavior? Evidence from Real Online Customer Behavior Data
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work presents the first large-scale quantitative evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs'ability to accurately simulate human behavior and establishes the first rigorous benchmark for human behavior simulation.

title: AgentStore: Scalable Integration of Heterogeneous Agents As Specialized Generalist Computer Assistant
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Inspired by the rich functionality of the App store, AgentStore is presented, a scalable platform designed to dynamically integrate heterogeneous agents for automating computer tasks and demonstrates AgentStore's ability to enhance agent systems in both generalization and specialization.

title: LLaMA Rider: Spurring Large Language Models to Explore the Open World
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes an approach to spur Large Language Models to explore the open world, gather experiences, and learn to improve their task-solving capabilities, using a multi-round feedback-revision mechanism to encourage LLMs to actively select appropriate revision actions guided by feedback information from the environment.

title: Multi-Modal and Multi-Agent Systems Meet Rationality: A Survey
proposal_tldr: Whether multi-modal and multi-agent systems are advancing toward rationality is understood by surveying the state-of-the-art works, identifying advancements over single-agent and single-modal systems in terms of rationality, and discussing open problems and future directions.

title: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
proposal_tldr: ClawBench is an evaluation framework comprising 153 everyday online tasks that people need to accomplish regularly in their lives and work, spanning 144 platforms across 15 categories, from completing purchases and booking appointments to submitting job applications, to bring closer to AI agents that can function as general-purpose assistants.

title: FATH: Authentication-based Test-time Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces a novel test-time defense strategy, named Formatting AuThentication with Hash-based tags (FATH), which implements an authentication system, requiring LLMs to answer all received instructions with a security policy and selectively filter out responses to user instructions as the final output.

title: Unlocking the Future: Exploring Look-Ahead Planning Mechanistic Interpretability in Large Language Models
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This research analyzes the look-ahead planning mechanisms of LLMs, facilitating future research on LLMs performing planning tasks and finding that the output of MHSA in the middle layers at the last token can directly decode the decision to some extent.

title: AutoGuide: Automated Generation and Selection of State-Aware Guidelines for Large Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces a novel framework, called AutoGuide, that bridges the knowledge gap in pre-trained LLMs by leveraging implicit knowledge in offline experiences by extracting a set of state-aware guidelines.

title: From Novice to Expert: LLM Agent Policy Optimization via Step-wise Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces StepAgent, which utilizes step-wise reward to optimize the agent's reinforcement learning process, and proposes implicit-reward and inverse reinforcement learning techniques to facilitate agent reflection and policy adjustment.

title: Learning to Discuss Strategically: A Case Study on One Night Ultimate Werewolf
proposal_tldr: This work first presents the existence of the Perfect Bayesian Equilibria (PBEs) in two scenarios of the ONUW game: one with discussion and one without, and proposes an RL-instructed language agent framework, where a discussion policy trained by reinforcement learning (RL) is employed to determine appropriate discussion tactics to adopt.

title: Dual-View Visual Contextualization for Web Navigation
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes to contextualize HTML elements through their “dual views” in webpage screenshots: each HTML element has its corresponding bounding box and visual content in the screenshot, and consistently outperforms the baseline in all the scenarios, in-cluding cross-task, cross-website, and cross-domain ones.

title: Exposing Limitations of Language Model Agents in Sequential-Task Compositions on the Web
proposal_tldr: A new benchmark and detailed analysis emphasize the necessity of building LMAs that are robust and generalizable to task compositionality for real-world deployment, and highlights the promise of small-scale finetuned and transferred models for task compositionality.

title: PolySkill: Learning Generalizable Skills Through Polymorphic Abstraction
proposal_tldr: The findings show that separating a skill's goal from its execution is a crucial step toward developing autonomous agents that can learn and generalize across the open web continuously and provides a practical path toward building agents capable of continual learning in adaptive environments.

title: Difficulty-Aware Agentic Orchestration for Query-Specific Multi-Agent Workflows
proposal_tldr: Difficulty-Aware Agentic Orchestration (DAAO), which can dynamically generate query-specific multi-agent workflows guided by predicted query difficulty, is proposed, validating its effectiveness for adaptive, difficulty-aware reasoning.

title: AgentRecBench: Benchmarking LLM Agent-based Personalized Recommender Systems
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an interactive textual recommendation simulator incorporating rich user and item metadata and three typical evaluation scenarios (classic, evolving-interest, and cold-start recommendation tasks), and proposes the first comprehensive benchmark comparing 10 classical and agentic recommendation methods.

title: AutoGUI: Scaling GUI Grounding with Automatic Functionality Annotations from LLMs
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes the \textbf{AutoGUI} pipeline for automatically annotating UI elements with detailed functionality descriptions at scale, and leverage large language models (LLMs) to infer element functionality by comparing UI state changes before and after simulated interactions.

title: Falcon-UI: Understanding GUI Before Following User Instructions
proposal_tldr: The GUI agent model Falcon-UI is developed, which is initially pretrained on Insight-UI Dataset and subsequently fine-tuned on Android and Web GUI datasets, including AITW, AITZ, Android Control, and Mind2Web, validating the alignment between GUI context comprehension and agent performance.

title: GestureGPT: Toward Zero-Shot Free-Form Hand Gesture Understanding with Large Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: G gestureGPT is introduced, a free-form hand gesture understanding framework that mimics human gesture understanding procedures to enable a natural free-form gestural interface and validated offline under two real-world scenarios: smart home control and online video streaming.

title: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: InfiniteWeb is presented, a system that automatically generates functional web environments at scale for GUI agent training that surpasses commercial coding agents at realistic website construction and GUI agents trained on the authors' generated environments achieve significant performance improvements.

title: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: OSWorld-MCP is presented, the first comprehensive and fair benchmark for assessing computer-use agents'tool invocation, GUI operation, and decision-making abilities in a real-world environment and sets a new standard for evaluating performance in complex, tool-assisted environments.

title: Automatic Red Teaming LLM-Based Agents With Model Context Protocol Tools
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
proposal_tldr: AutoMalTool is proposed, an automated red teaming framework for LLM-based agents by generating malicious MCP tools capable of manipulating the behavior of mainstream LLM-based agents while evading current detection mechanisms, thereby revealing new security risks in these agents.

title: LLM Economist: Large Population Models and Mechanism Design in Multi-Agent Generative Simulacra
proposal_tldr: The results demonstrate that large language model-based agents can jointly model, simulate, and govern complex economic systems, providing a tractable test bed for policy evaluation at the societal scale to help build better civilizations.

title: FullFront: Benchmarking MLLMs Across the Full Front-End Engineering Workflow
proposal_tldr: FullFront is presented, a benchmark designed to evaluate Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), and quantitatively demonstrate performance disparities across models and tasks, and highlight a substantial gap between current MLLM capabilities and human expert performance in front-end engineering.

title: DemonAgent: Dynamically Encrypted Multi-Backdoor Implantation Attack on LLM-based Agent
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel backdoor implantation strategy called dynamic encryption, which maps the backdoor into benign content, effectively circumventing safety audits and further decomposes the backdoor into multiple sub-backdoor fragments to enhance stealthiness.

title: Symbiotic Cooperation for Web Agents: Harnessing Complementary Strengths of Large and Small LLMs
proposal_tldr: This study uncovers a complementary dynamic between LLM types: while large LLMs excel at generating high-quality trajectories for distillation, the distilled small LLMs-owing to their distinct reasoning capabilities-often choose actions that diverge from those of their larger counterparts, thereby enriching the synthesized data.

title: AdaptAgent: Adapting Multimodal Web Agents with Few-Shot Learning from Human Demonstrations
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The AdaptAgent framework is introduced that enables both proprietary and open-weights multimodal web agents to adapt to new websites and domains using few human demonstrations, and unlocks a complementary axis for developing widely applicable multimodal web agents beyond large-scale pre-training and fine-tuning.

title: ReSpAct: Harmonizing Reasoning, Speaking, and Acting Towards Building Large Language Model-Based Conversational AI Agents
venue: International Workshop on Spoken Dialogue Systems Technology
proposal_tldr: ReSpAct is introduced, an LLM-based agent designed to seamlessly integrate reasoning, decision-making, and dynamic dialogue for task-solving and outperforms ReAct with absolute success rate improvements, highlighting the value of integrating dynamic user-agent collaboration for more effective task resolution.

title: Towards Rationality in Language and Multimodal Agents: A Survey
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work discusses how to build more rational language and multimodal agents and what criteria define rationality in intelligent systems. Rationality is the quality of being guided by reason, characterized by decision-making that aligns with evidence and logical principles. It plays a crucial role

title: Large Language Model Powered Agents in the Web
proposal_tldr: This tutorial dives into the cutting-edge techniques of LLM-powered agents across various web applications, such as web mining, social networks, recommender systems, and conversational systems, to explore the prevailing challenges in seamlessly incorporating these agents.

title: Bring Your Own KG: Self-Supervised Program Synthesis for Zero-Shot KGQA
proposal_tldr: Performance of BYOKG reliably improves with continued exploration as well as improvements in the base LLM, notably outperforming a state-of-the-art fine-tuned model by 7.08 F1 on a sub-sampled zero-shot split of GrailQA.

title: SkillGrad: Optimizing Agent Skills Like Gradient Descent
proposal_tldr: SkillGrad treats the skill package as a structured parameter to optimize in a gradient descent fashion, and consistently outperforms training-based skill evolution baselines across two backbone LLMs, improving over the strongest training-based baseline by $6.7$ percentage points on average.

title: Evaluating Test-Time Scaling of General LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper systematically investigates two principal test-time scaling axes of LLM agents: sequential scaling through extended interaction and parallel scaling through trajectory sampling, and finds that neither scaling axis can consistently yield meaningful gains from additional test-time compute in realistic environments.

title: SABER: Small Actions, Big Errors - Safeguarding Mutating Steps in LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: A model-agnostic, gradient-free, test-time safeguard that adds mutation-gated verification, injects targeted reflection before mutating steps, and performs block-based context cleaning, which argues for action-level analysis, targeted safeguards, and reliable evaluations as prerequisites for robust multi-turn agents.

title: Learning on the Job: An Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agent for Long-Horizon Tasks
proposal_tldr: MUSE is proposed, a novel agent framework that introduces an experience-driven, self-evolving system centered around a hierarchical Memory Module that establishes a new paradigm for AI agents capable of real-world productivity task automation.

title: Phi-Ground Tech Report: Advancing Perception in GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: The Phi-Ground model family is developed, which achieves state-of-the-art performance across all five grounding benchmarks for models under $10B$ parameters in agent settings, and is likely to benefit other perception tasks.

title: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Comprehensive evaluations across multiple generalization settings and a fine-tuned Qwen2.5VL-7B model yields a substantial improvement in performance, boosting accuracy from 37% to 80% and HIGH-risk action recall from 20% to 76%.

title: Multimodal DeepResearcher: Generating Text-Chart Interleaved Reports From Scratch with Agentic Framework
proposal_tldr: Formal Description of Visualization (FDV) is proposed, a structured textual representation of charts that enables LLMs to learn from and generate diverse, high-quality visualizations and Multimodal DeepResearcher, an agentic framework that decomposes the task into four stages.

title: Learning to Contextualize Web Pages for Enhanced Decision Making by LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces LCoW, a framework for Learning language models to Contextualize complex Web pages into a more comprehensible form, thereby enhancing decision making by LLM agents, and demonstrates that the contextualization module effectively integrates with LLM agents of various scales to significantly enhance their decision-making capabilities in web automation tasks.

title: SpiritSight Agent: Advanced GUI Agent with One Look
proposal_tldr: This work proposes SpiritSight, a vision-based, end-to-end GUI agent that excels in GUI navigation tasks across various GUI platforms, and introduces the Universal Block Parsing (UBP) method to resolve the ambiguity problem inherited from the dynamic resolution strategy, further enhancing SpiritSight's ability to ground GUI objects.

title: Remote Labor Index: Measuring AI Automation of Remote Work
proposal_tldr: The Remote Labor Index (RLI), a broadly multi-sector benchmark comprising real-world, economically valuable projects designed to evaluate end-to-end agent performance in practical settings, is introduced to ground discussions of AI automation in empirical evidence.

title: How Do AI Agents Do Human Work? Comparing AI and Human Workflows Across Diverse Occupations
proposal_tldr: While agents exhibit promise in their alignment to human workflows, they take an overwhelmingly programmatic approach across all work domains, even for open-ended, visually dependent tasks like design, creating a contrast with the UI-centric methods typically used by humans.

title: WAInjectBench: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detections for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: The key findings show that while some detectors can identify attacks that rely on explicit textual instructions or visible image perturbations with moderate to high accuracy, they largely fail against attacks that omit explicit instructions or employ imperceptible perturbations.

title: UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: This work systematically vary turn-level reward assignment and trajectory-level score calculation to analyze how different formulations affect learning under the GRPO algorithm, and establishes UserRL as a practical pathway for developing robust user-centric agentic models.

title: Agent-RewardBench: Towards a Unified Benchmark for Reward Modeling across Perception, Planning, and Safety in Real-World Multimodal Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The proposed Agent-RewardBench is a benchmark designed to evaluate reward modeling ability in MLLMs, and allows for the assessment of agent capabilities at the individual steps of a task, providing a more granular view of performance during the planning process.

title: SHARE: An SLM-based Hierarchical Action CorREction Assistant for Text-to-SQL
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes SHARE, an SLM-based Hierarchical Action corREction assistant that enables LLMs to perform more precise error localization and efficient correction and proposes a novel hierarchical self-evolution strategy for data-efficient training.

title: UI-E2I-Synth: Advancing GUI Grounding with Large-Scale Instruction Synthesis
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A large-scale data synthesis pipeline UI-E2I-Synth is introduced for generating varying complex instruction datasets using GPT-4o instead of human annotators and a new GUI instruction grounding benchmark UI-I2E-Bench is proposed, designed to address the limitations of existing benchmarks by incorporating diverse annotation aspects.

title: Scaling Autonomous Agents via Automatic Reward Modeling And Planning
proposal_tldr: A framework that can automatically learn a reward model from the environment without human annotations is proposed, which paves the way for more sophisticated AI agents capable of tackling a wide range of real-world problems requiring multi-step decision-making.

title: Digi-Q: Learning Q-Value Functions for Training Device-Control Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper develops an approach to train VLM-based action-value Q-functions which are then used to extract the agent policy, and outperforms several prior methods on user-scale device control tasks in Android-in-the-Wild, attaining 21.2% improvement over prior best-performing method.

title: Infogent: An Agent-Based Framework for Web Information Aggregation
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Infogent is introduced, a novel modular framework for web information aggregation involving three distinct components: Navigator, Extractor and Aggregator that beats an existing SOTA multi-agent search framework, and improves over an existing information-seeking web agent.

title: Devil's Advocate: Anticipatory Reflection for LLM Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: The experimental results suggest that the introspection-driven approach not only enhances the agent's ability to navigate unanticipated challenges through a robust mechanism of plan execution, but also improves efficiency by reducing the number of trials and plan revisions by 45% needed to achieve a task.

title: YuraScanner: Leveraging LLMs for Task-driven Web App Scanning
venue: Network and Distributed System Security Symposium
proposal_tldr: Y URA S CANNER is introduced, a task-driven web application scanner that leverages large-language models (LLMs) to autonomously execute tasks and workﬂows and demonstrates Y URA S CANNER’s superiority in discovering new attack surfaces and deeper states, and improving vulnerability detection.

title: AgentNoiseBench: Benchmarking Robustness of Tool-Using LLM Agents Under Noisy Condition
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentNoiseBench, a framework for systematically evaluating the robustness of agentic models under noisy environments and develops an automated pipeline that injects controllable noise into existing agent-centric benchmarks while preserving task solvability.

title: A Survey on Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This survey explores the emerging paradigm of agentic MLLMs, delineating their conceptual foundations and distinguishing characteristics from conventional MLLM-based agents, and establishes a conceptual framework that organizes agentic MLLMs along three fundamental dimensions.

title: WebMMU: A Benchmark for Multimodal Multilingual Website Understanding and Code Generation
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: While multimodal large language models (MLLMs) perform well on basic information extraction, they struggle with reasoning and grounding, editing code to preserve functionality, and generating design-to-code that maintains hierarchy and supports multilingual content.

title: R-VLM: Region-Aware Vision Language Model for Precise GUI Grounding
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The R-VLM approach bridges the gap between VLMs and conventional object detection techniques, improving the state-of-the-art grounding accuracy by 13% across diverse GUI platforms on the GUI grounding benchmarks ScreenSpot and AgentStudio.

title: Embodied Web Agents: Bridging Physical-Digital Realms for Integrated Agent Intelligence
proposal_tldr: Embodied Web Agents is introduced, a novel paradigm for AI agents that fluidly bridge embodiment and web-scale reasoning, and Experimental results reveal significant performance gaps between state-of-the-art AI systems and human capabilities.

title: GUI-Robust: A Comprehensive Dataset for Testing GUI Agent Robustness in Real-World Anomalies
proposal_tldr: gui-Robust is introduced, a novel dataset designed for comprehensive GUI agent evaluation, explicitly incorporating seven common types of anomalies observed in everyday GUI interactions, and a semi-automated dataset construction paradigm that collects user action sequences from natural interactions via RPA tools and then generates corresponding step and task descriptions for these actions with the assistance of MLLMs.

title: FingerTip 20K: A Benchmark for Proactive and Personalized Mobile LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: The FingerTip 20K benchmark is introduced and the model fine-tuned with the data collected effectively utilized user information and achieved good results, highlighting the potential of the approach in building more user-oriented mobile LLM agents.

title: MMAU: A Holistic Benchmark of Agent Capabilities Across Diverse Domains
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The Massive Multitask Agent Understanding (MMAU) benchmark is introduced, featuring comprehensive offline tasks that eliminate the need for complex environment setups and sheds light on the capabilities and limitations of LLM agents but also enhances the interpretability of their performance.

title: MobileAgent: enhancing mobile control via human-machine interaction and SOP integration
proposal_tldr: Interactive tasks between agents and humans are designed to identify sensitive information and align with personalized user needs and Standard Operating Procedure information is integrated within the model's in-context learning to enhance the agent's comprehension of complex task execution.

title: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
proposal_tldr: eTAMP is introduced, the first attack to achieve cross-session, cross-site compromise without requiring direct memory access and Frustration Exploitation is discovered: agents under environmental stress become dramatically more susceptible, with ASR increasing up to 8 times when agents struggle with dropped clicks or garbled text.

title: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
proposal_tldr: This work proposes AutoWebWorld, a novel framework for synthesizing controllable and verifiable web environments by modeling them as Finite State Machines (FSMs) and use coding agents to translate FSMs into interactive websites and observes a clear scaling law: as the synthetic data volume increases, performance on WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web consistently improves.

title: MMDeepResearch-Bench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Deep Research Agents
proposal_tldr: Experiments across 25 state-of-the-art models reveal systematic trade-offs between generation quality, citation discipline, and multimodal grounding, highlighting that strong prose alone does not guarantee faithful evidence use and that multimodal integrity remains a key bottleneck for deep research agents.

title: Game-TARS: Pretrained Foundation Models for Scalable Generalist Multimodal Game Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents Game-TARS, a generalist game agent trained with a unified, scalable action space anchored to human-aligned native keyboard-mouse inputs that provides a promising path toward generalist agents with broad computer-use abilities.

title: VideoAgentTrek: Computer Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
proposal_tldr: VideoAgentTrek is presented, a scalable pipeline that automatically mines training data from publicly available screen-recorded videos at web scale, eliminating the need for manual annotation, providing a scalable alternative to expensive manual annotation.

title: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
proposal_tldr: This work proposes DART, a Decoupled Agentic RL Training framework for GUI agents, which coordinates heterogeneous modules in a highly decoupled manner and will fully open-source the training framework, data, and model checkpoints via computer-use-agents.

title: ToolFuzz - Automated Agent Tool Testing
proposal_tldr: It is shown that ToolFuzz identifies 20x more erroneous inputs compared to the prompt-engineering approaches, making it a key component for building reliable AI agents, and it is found that many publicly available tools suffer from underspecification.

title: UDora: A Unified Red Teaming Framework against LLM Agents by Dynamically Hijacking Their Own Reasoning
proposal_tldr: UDora is presented, a unified red teaming framework designed for LLM agents that dynamically hijacks the agent's reasoning processes to compel malicious behavior and demonstrates superior effectiveness compared to existing methods across three LLM agent datasets.

title: Tur[k]ingBench: A Challenge Benchmark for Web Agents
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: TurkingBench is a benchmark consisting of tasks presented as web pages with textual instructions and multi-modal contexts, which assess the performance of cutting-edge private and open-source models, including language-only and vision-language models (such as GPT4 and InternVL), on this benchmark.

title: Tapilot-Crossing: Benchmarking and Evolving LLMs Towards Interactive Data Analysis Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Tapilot-Crossing, a new benchmark to evaluate Large Language Model agents on interactive data analysis, and proposes Adaptive Interaction Reflection (AIR), a self-generated reflection strategy that guides LLM agents to learn from successful history.

title: PhishDecloaker: Detecting CAPTCHA-cloaked Phishing Websites via Hybrid Vision-based Interactive Models
proposal_tldr: This work develops PhishDecloaker, an AI-powered solution to soften the shield of the CAPTCHA-cloaking used by phishing websites, and evaluates its effectiveness, effectiveness, robustness, and robustness against potential adversaries.

title: OpenWebAgent: An Open Toolkit to Enable Web Agents on Large Language Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Towards Action Hijacking of Large Language Model-based Agent
proposal_tldr: A novel hijacking attack to manipulate the action plans of black-box agent system is introduced, which first collects the action-aware memory through prompt theft from long-term memory and leverages the internal memory retrieval mechanism of the agent to provide an erroneous context.

title: Temporary Authority, Permanent Effects: Commit-Time Authorization for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: A controlled-invalidation suite spanning browser, tool/API, and multi-agent workflows is built, which preserves the user goal and payload shape while invalidating the authority relation before durability, and is a reporting and runtime-design lesson: endpoint success is a utility metric; authorized commit is a security property.

title: WebXSkill: Skill Learning for Autonomous Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebXSkill, a framework that bridges a grounding gap with executable skills, each pairing a parameterized action program with step-level natural-language guidance, and finds that better skill deployment mode depends on a model's plan and execution capability.

title: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MolmoWebMix, a large and diverse mixture of browser task demonstrations and web-GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb, a family of fully open multimodal web agents that outperform similar scale open-weight-only models such as Fara-7B, UI-Tars-1.5-7B, and Holo1-7B.

title: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebWorld series, the first open-web simulator trained at scale, which leverages a scalable data pipeline to train on 1M+ open-web interactions, supporting reasoning, multi-format data, and long-horizon simulations of 30+ steps.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in LLM Agents: Foundations, Emerging Challenges, and Opportunities
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper argues that UQ research must shift to realistic settings with interactive agents, and that a new principled framework for agent UQ is needed, and presents the first general formulation of agent UQ that subsumes broad classes of existing UQ setups.

title: Can LLMs Help You at Work? A Sandbox for Evaluating LLM Agents in Enterprise Environments
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: EnterpriseBench is presented, a comprehensive benchmark that simulates enterprise settings, featuring 500 diverse tasks across software engineering, HR, finance, and administrative domains, and provides a novel data generation pipeline that creates internally consistent enterprise tasks from organizational metadata.

title: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes OS-Sentinel, a novel hybrid safety detection framework that synergistically combines a Formal Verifier for detecting explicit system-level violations with a VLM-based Contextual Judge for assessing contextual risks and agent actions.

title: SecureWebArena: A Holistic Security Evaluation Benchmark for LVLM-based Web Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a unified evaluation suite comprising six simulated but realistic web environments and a multi-layered evaluation pipeline that analyzes agent failures across three critical dimensions: internal reasoning, behavioral trajectory, and task outcome, facilitating a fine-grained risk analysis that goes far beyond simple success metrics.

title: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
proposal_tldr: A continuous memory that encodes each GUI trajectory into a fixed-length sequence of continuous embeddings using the VLM itself as an encoder; these embeddings are plugged directly into the backbone's input layer, sharply reducing context cost while preserving fine-grained visual information.

title: UItron: Foundational GUI Agent with Advanced Perception and Planning
proposal_tldr: This work introduces UItron, an open-source foundational model for automatic GUI agents, featuring advanced GUI perception, grounding, and planning capabilities, and identifies a general lack of Chinese capabilities even in state-of-the-art solutions.

title: LPO: Towards Accurate GUI Agent Interaction via Location Preference Optimization
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Location Preference Optimization (LPO), a novel approach that leverages locational data to optimize interaction preferences and introduces a dynamic location reward function based on physical distance, reflecting the varying importance of interaction positions.

title: MP-GUI: Modality Perception with MLLMs for GUI Understanding
proposal_tldr: MP-GUI is presented, a specially designed MLLM for GUI understanding that features three precisely specialized perceivers to extract graphical, textual, and spatial modalities from the screen as GUI-tailored visual clues, with spatial structure refinement strategy and adaptively combined via a fusion gate to meet the specific preferences of different GUI understanding tasks.

title: Learning Strategic Language Agents in the Werewolf Game with Iterative Latent Space Policy Optimization
proposal_tldr: Experiment on the Werewolf game shows that the proposed Latent Space Policy Optimization agents iteratively expand the strategy space with improving performance and outperform existing Werewolf agents, underscoring their effectiveness in free-form language games with strategic interactions.

title: VipAct: Visual-Perception Enhancement via Specialized VLM Agent Collaboration and Tool-use
proposal_tldr: VipAct is presented, an agent framework that enhances VLMs by integrating multi-agent collaboration and vision expert models, enabling more precise visual understanding and comprehensive reasoning and paving the way for more advanced visual perception systems across various real-world applications.

title: Large Language Model Powered Agents for Information Retrieval
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: This tutorial delves into the cutting-edge techniques of LLM-powered agents across various information retrieval fields, such as search engines, social networks, recommender systems, and conversational assistants, and explores the prevailing challenges in seamlessly incorporating these agents.

title: Read Anywhere Pointed: Layout-aware GUI Screen Reading with Tree-of-Lens Grounding
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a Tree-of-Lens (ToL) agent, utilizing a novel ToL grounding mechanism, to address the Screen Point-and-Read (ScreenPR) task, and constructs a Hierarchical Layout Tree based on the input point coordinate and the corresponding GUI screenshot.

title: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
proposal_tldr: This work presents MUZZLE, an automated agentic framework for evaluating the security of web agents against indirect prompt injection attacks, and demonstrates its ability to automatically and adaptively assess the security of web agents with minimal human intervention.

title: Reinforcement World Model Learning for LLM-based Agents
proposal_tldr: Reinforcement World Model Learning is proposed, a self-supervised method that learns action-conditioned world models for LLM-based agents on textual states using sim-to-real gap rewards and provides a more robust training signal and is empirically less susceptible to reward hacking than LLM-as-a-judge.

title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI): Architectures, Taxonomies, and Evaluation of Large Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper investigates architectures and proposes a unified taxonomy that breaks agents into Perception, Brain, Planning, Action, Tool Use, and Collaboration, and uses this lens to describe the move from linear reasoning procedures to native inference time reasoning models, and the transition from fixed API calls to open standards like the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Native Computer Use.

title: DECEPTICON: How Dark Patterns Manipulate Web Agents
proposal_tldr: It is shown that dark patterns are highly effective in steering agent trajectories, posing a significant risk to agent robustness, and DECEPTICON, an environment for testing individual dark patterns in isolation, is introduced, an environment for testing individual dark patterns in isolation.

title: DAComp: Benchmarking Data Agents across the Full Data Intelligence Lifecycle
proposal_tldr: DAComp provides a rigorous and realistic testbed to drive the development of truly capable autonomous data agents for enterprise settings, highlighting profound deficiencies in open-ended reasoning and demonstrating that engineering and analysis are distinct capabilities.

title: Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Agents via Environment Interaction
proposal_tldr: This work proposes two distinct strategies for adapting LLM agents by leveraging environment-specific information from interaction that is available during deployment, and finds that dynamics grounding is particularly effective in complex environments where unpredictable dynamics pose a major obstacle.
