title: Agent Data Protocol: Unifying Datasets for Diverse, Effective Fine-tuning of LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work argues that the bottleneck is not a lack of underlying data sources, but that a large variety of data is fragmented across heterogeneous formats, tools, and interfaces, and introduces the agent data protocol (ADP), a light-weight representation language that serves as an "interlingua"between agent datasets in diverse formats and unified agent training pipelines downstream.

title: Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory for LLM Agent Planning
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory (\The authors'), a novel framework that grounds coarse-to-fine memories with LLM, thereby fully leverage them for flexible adaptation to diverse scenarios.

title: Build the web for agents, not agents for the web
proposal_tldr: This position paper advocates for a paradigm shift in web agent research: rather than forcing web agents to adapt to interfaces designed for humans, a new interaction paradigm specifically optimized for agentic capabilities is introduced, an interface specifically designed for agents to navigate a website.

title: Evolutionary Perspectives on the Evaluation of LLM-Based AI Agents: A Comprehensive Survey
proposal_tldr: This paper provides a detailed analytical framework that clearly differentiates AI agents from LLM chatbots along five key aspects: complex environment, multi-source instructor, dynamic feedback, multi-modal perception, and advanced capability.

title: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: ScaleTrack explains the correspondence between GUI images and actions, which effectively describes the evolution rules of the GUI environment, and designs a novel training strategy that predicts the next action from the current GUI image, while also backtracking the historical actions that led to the GUI image.

title: VEM: Environment-Free Exploration for Training GUI Agent with Value Environment Model
proposal_tldr: An environment-free RL framework that decouples value estimation from policy optimization by leveraging a pretrained Value Environment Model (VEM), demonstrating that semantic-aware value estimation can achieve comparable performance with online-trained methods.

title: GUI-Bee: Align GUI Action Grounding to Novel Environments via Autonomous Exploration
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes GUI-Bee, an MLLM-based autonomous agent to collect high-quality, environment-specific data through exploration and then continuously fine-tune GUI grounding models with the collected data, and leverages a novel Q-value-Incentive In-Context Reinforcement Learning (Q-ICRL) method to optimize exploration efficiency and data quality.

title: Vision Search Assistant: Empower Vision-Language Models as Multimodal Search Engines
proposal_tldr: The Vision Search Assistant is proposed, a novel framework that facilitates collaboration between VLMs and web agents that leverages VLMs' visual understanding capabilities and web agents' real-time information access to perform open-world Retrieval-Augmented Generation via the web.

title: Leopard: A Vision Language Model For Text-Rich Multi-Image Tasks
proposal_tldr: Leopard, an MLLM tailored for handling vision-language tasks involving multiple text-rich images, is proposed and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art systems, such as Llama-3.2 and Qwen2-VL, in challenging text-rich, multi-image evaluations.

title: Policy Improvement using Language Feedback Models
proposal_tldr: Language Feedback Models that identify desirable behaviour - actions that help achieve tasks specified in the instruction - for imitation learning in instruction following improve in task-completion rate over strong behavioural cloning baselines on three distinct language grounding environments.

title: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
proposal_tldr: Odysseys isolates the critical evaluation of long-horizon proficiency in open-web environments, providing a realistic benchmark to measure progress towards computer-use agents that can potentially productively operate for hours.

title: ClawMark: A Living-World Benchmark for Multi-Turn, Multi-Day, Multimodal Coworker Agents
proposal_tldr: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and construction pipeline are released to support reproducible coworker-agent evaluation and turn-level analysis shows that performance drops after the first exogenous environment update, highlighting adaptation to changing state as a key open challenge.

title: AI Agent Systems: Architectures, Applications, and Evaluation
proposal_tldr: This survey synthesizes the emerging landscape of AI agent architectures across deliberation and reasoning, planning, planning, memory, and tool use, and identifies open challenges including verification and guardrails for tool actions, scalable memory and context management, interpretability of agent decisions, and reproducible evaluation under realistic workloads.

title: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
proposal_tldr: LiteAgent is introduced, a lightweight framework that automatically prompts agents to execute tasks while capturing comprehensive logs and screen-recordings of their interactions and TrickyArena, a controlled environment comprising web applications from domains such as e-commerce, streaming services, and news platforms, each containing diverse and realistic dark patterns that can be selectively enabled or disabled.

title: Automatic Failure Attribution and Critical Step Prediction Method for Multi-Agent Systems Based on Causal Inference
proposal_tldr: This work provides a principled and effective solution for debugging complex agent interactions, paving the way for more reliable and interpretable multi-agent systems.

title: MIRAGE-Bench: LLM Agent is Hallucinating and Where to Find Them
proposal_tldr: MIRAGE-Bench provides actionable insights on failure modes of LLM agents and lays the groundwork for principled progress in mitigating hallucinations in interactive environments.

title: The Hidden Dangers of Browsing AI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work outlines the first end-to-end threat model for browsing agents and provides actionable guidance for securing their deployment in real-world environments and proposes a defense in depth strategy incorporating input sanitization, planner executor isolation, formal analyzers, and session safeguards.

title: Attention-driven GUI Grounding: Leveraging Pretrained Multimodal Large Language Models without Fine-Tuning
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a novel Tuning-free Attention-driven Grounding (TAG) method that leverages the inherent attention patterns in pretrained MLLMs to accomplish this task without the need for additional fine-tuning, and achieves performance comparable to tuning-based methods.

title: Large Language Model Agents as Prognostics and Health Management Copilots
venue: Annual Conference of the PHM Society
proposal_tldr: This work automates maintenance recommendations triggered by PHM alerts for monitoring the health of physical assets, using LLM agents to execute structured components of the standard maintenance recommendation protocol, including data processing, failure mode discovery, and evaluation.

title: Auto-Intent: Automated Intent Discovery and Self-Exploration for Large Language Model Web Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: Auto-Intent is introduced, a method to adapt a pre-trained large language model (LLM) as an agent for a target domain without direct fine-tuning, where it empirically focus on web navigation tasks.

title: Don't Act Blindly: Robust GUI Automation via Action-Effect Verification and Self-Correction
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: VeriGUI (Verification-driven GUI Agent) is proposed, which explicitly models action outcomes and recovery under noisy environments and significantly reduces failure loops and improves recovery success while maintaining competitive standard task performance.

title: Evaluating Long-Context Reasoning in LLM-Based WebAgents
proposal_tldr: A benchmark for evaluating long context reasoning capabilities of WebAgents through sequentially dependent subtasks that require retrieval and application of information from extended interaction histories is introduced and an implicit RAG approach is proposed that provides modest improvements by generating task-relevant summaries, though fundamental limitations in long context reasoning persist.

title: WebMall - A Multi-Shop Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebMall, the first offline multi-shop benchmark for evaluating web agents on challenging comparison shopping tasks and validate WebMall using eight agents that differ in observation space, availability of short-term memory, and the employed LLM.

title: Mobile-Bench-v2: A More Realistic and Comprehensive Benchmark for VLM-based Mobile Agents
proposal_tldr: A slot-based instruction generation method is used to construct a more realistic and comprehensive benchmark named Mobile-Bench-v2, which includes a common task split, with offline multi-path evaluation to assess the agent's ability to obtain step rewards during task execution.

title: Generator-Assistant Stepwise Rollback Framework for Large Language Model Agent
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a novel framework called Generator-Assistant Stepwise Rollback (GA-Rollback), which utilizes a generator to interact with the environment and an assistant to examine each action produced by the generator, where the assistant triggers a rollback operation upon detection of incorrect actions.

title: A Token-Level Text Image Foundation Model for Document Understanding
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
proposal_tldr: TokenFD is the first token-level visual foundation model specifically tailored for text-image-related tasks, designed to support a variety of traditional downstream applications, and seamlessly replaces previous VFMs with TokenFD to construct a token-level visual-language MLLM, TokenVL, for VQA-based document understanding tasks.

title: Standard Benchmarks Fail -- Auditing LLM Agents in Finance Must Prioritize Risk
proposal_tldr: This work audits six API-based and open-weights LLM agents on three high-impact tasks and uncover hidden weaknesses that conventional benchmarks miss, and outlines a three-level agenda: model, workflow, and system, for stress-testing LLM agents under realistic failure modes.

title: SummAct: Uncovering User Intentions Through Interactive Behaviour Summarisation
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: This work proposes interactive behaviour summarisation as a novel computational task and demonstrates its usefulness for automatically uncovering latent user goals while interacting with graphical user interfaces by introducing SummAct – a novel hierarchical method to summarise low-level input actions into high-level goals to tackle this task.

title: KwaiAgents: Generalized Information-seeking Agent System with Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces KwaiAgents, a generalized information-seeking agent system that employs LLMs as its cognitive core, and proposes the Meta-Agent Tuning framework, designed to ensure even an open-sourced 7B or 13B model performs well among many agent systems.

title: TurnOPD: Making On-Policy Distillation Turn-Aware for Efficient Long-Horizon Agent Training
proposal_tldr: Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Multi-Hop Search with task-specialized teacher models show that TurnOPD achieves superior validation accuracy under equal wall-clock training budgets and advances the accuracy--time frontier beyond vanilla OPD.

title: Persona2Web: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents for Contextual Reasoning with User History
proposal_tldr: Persona2Web is the first benchmark for evaluating personalized web agents on the real open web, built upon the clarify-to-personalize principle, which requires agents to resolve ambiguity based on user history rather than relying on explicit instructions.

title: ArenaRL: Scaling RL for Open-Ended Agents via Tournament-based Relative Ranking
proposal_tldr: This work proposes ArenaRL, a reinforcement learning paradigm that shifts from pointwise scalar scoring to intra-group relative ranking, and introduces a process-aware pairwise evaluation mechanism, employing multi-level rubrics to assign fine-grained relative scores to trajectories.

title: Environment Scaling for Interactive Agentic Experience Collection: A Survey
proposal_tldr: This survey systematically review representative methods for environment scaling from a pioneering environment-centric perspective and organize them along the stages of the GEF loop, namely task generation, task execution, and feedback.

title: LLMs as Scalable, General-Purpose Simulators For Evolving Digital Agent Training
proposal_tldr: Experiments show that UI-Simulator rivals or surpasses open-source agents trained on real UIs with significantly better robustness, despite using weaker teacher models, and proposes a targeted scaling strategy that enables more rapid and data-efficient scaling by prioritizing high-impact tasks and synthesizes informative trajectory variants.

title: FocusAgent: Simple Yet Effective Ways of Trimming the Large Context of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: A variant of FocusAgent significantly reduces the success rate of prompt-injection attacks, including banner and pop-up attacks, while maintaining task success performance in attack-free settings, highlighting that targeted LLM-based retrieval is a practical and robust strategy for building web agents that are efficient, effective, and secure.

title: BrowserArena: Evaluating LLM Agents on Real-World Web Navigation Tasks
proposal_tldr: BrowserArena is introduced, a live open-web agent evaluation platform that collects user-submitted tasks, runs Arena-style head-to-head comparisons, and uses step-level human feedback to surface failure modes, and identifies three consistent failure modes: captcha resolution, pop-up banner removal and direct navigation to URLs.

title: UniECS: Unified Multimodal E-Commerce Search Framework with Gated Cross-modal Fusion
venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
proposal_tldr: UniECS is introduced, a unified multimodal e-commerce e-commerce search framework that handles all retrieval scenarios across image, text, and their combinations and develops a comprehensive training strategy to optimize learning.

title: Mirage-1: Augmenting and Updating GUI Agent with Hierarchical Multimodal Skills
proposal_tldr: A Hierarchical Multimodal Skills (HMS) module to tackle the issue of insufficient knowledge, which progressively abstracts trajectories into execution skills, core skills, and ultimately meta-skills, providing a hierarchical knowledge structure for long-horizon task planning.

title: Scalable Video-to-Dataset Generation for Cross-Platform Mobile Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MONDAY (Mobile OS Navigation Task Dataset for Agents from YouTube), a large-scale dataset of 313K annotated frames from 20K instructional videos capturing diverse real-world mobile OS navigation across multiple platforms, and presents an automated framework that leverages publicly available video content to create comprehensive task datasets without manual annotation.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Enhancing Agent Behavioral Safety with Thought Correction
proposal_tldr: Thought-Aligner is introduced, a lightweight plug-in safety model that performs causal correction on unsafe thoughts before action execution, without altering the underlying agent.

title: A Case for AI Consciousness: Language Agents and Global Workspace Theory
proposal_tldr: It is argued that if global workspace theory (GWT) is correct, then instances of one widely implemented AI architecture, the artificial language agent, might easily be made phenomenally conscious if they are not already.

title: TinyClick: Single-Turn Agent for Empowering GUI Automation
proposal_tldr: An UI agent for user interface (UI) interaction tasks, using Vision-Language Model Florence-2-Base, demonstrates very strong performance on Screenspot and OmniAct annotations, while maintaining a very small size of 0.27B parameters and minimal latency.

title: WebQuest: A Benchmark for Multimodal QA on Web Page Sequences
proposal_tldr: This work presents WebQuest, a multi-page question-answering dataset that requires reasoning across multiple related web pages, and investigates inference time techniques like Chain-of-Thought prompting to improve model capabilities on multi-screen reasoning.

title: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
proposal_tldr: Results establish GUI playtesting as an evaluation and refinement signal for interactive code generation and shows that GUI-agent feedback is fully logged and traceable, while its priorities vary substantially across model backbones.

title: WebCloak: Characterizing and Mitigating Threats From LLM-Driven Web Agents as Intelligent Scrapers
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
proposal_tldr: The rise of web agents powered by large language models (LLMs) is reshaping the landscape of human-computer interaction, enabling users to automate complex web tasks with natural language commands. However, this progress introduces significant, yet largely unexplored security concerns: adversaries c

title: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
proposal_tldr: Post-training GUI agents in interactive environments is critical for developing generalization and long-horizon planning capabilities. However, training on real-world applications is hindered by high latency, poor reproducibility, and unverifiable rewards relying on noisy visual proxies. To address

title: MobileDreamer: Generative Sketch World Model for GUI Agent
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes MobileDreamer, an efficient world-model-based lookahead framework to equip the GUI agents based on the future imagination provided by the world model, which consists of textual sketch world model and rollout imagination for GUI agent.

title: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: GUI agents powered by vision-language models (VLMs) show promise in automating complex digital tasks. However, their effectiveness in real-world applications is often limited by scarce training data and the inherent complexity of these tasks, which frequently require long-tailed knowledge covering r

title: SimuHome: A Temporal- and Environment-Aware Benchmark for Smart Home LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: SimuHome's time-accelerated simulation could serve as an environment for agents to pre-validate their actions before committing them to the real world, suggesting that SimuHome's time-accelerated simulation could serve as an environment for agents to pre-validate their actions before committing them to the real world.

title: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
proposal_tldr: The experiments show that introducing WAREX leads to significant drops in task success rates, highlighting the limited robustness of state-of-the-art agents.

title: Mano Technical Report
proposal_tldr: This work provides new insights into the effective integration of reinforcement learning with VLMs for practical GUI agent deployment, highlighting the importance of domain-specific data, iterative training, and holistic reward design.

title: Generalizability of Large Language Model-Based Agents: A Comprehensive Survey
proposal_tldr: This work provides the first comprehensive review of generalizability in LLM-based agents, clarifying the definition and boundaries of agent generalizability and establishing a foundation for principled research on building LLM-based agents that generalize reliably across diverse real-world applications.

title: Evaluating the Goal-Directedness of Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This work evaluates goal-directedness of LLMs from Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic on tasks that require information gathering, cognitive effort, and plan execution, where it uses subtasks to infer each model's relevant capabilities.

title: R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The findings suggest that a combination of memory-enhanced navigation and reflective learning promisingly advances the capabilities of web agents, potentially benefiting various applications such as automated customer service and personal digital assistants.

title: From Grounding to Planning: Benchmarking Bottlenecks in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a new benchmark for each of the components separately, identifying the bottlenecks and pain points that limit agent performance and suggests that grounding is not a significant bottleneck and can be effectively addressed with current techniques.

title: MUG: Interactive Multimodal Grounding on User Interfaces
proposal_tldr: MUG, a novel interactive task for multimodal grounding where a user and an agent work collaboratively on an interface screen, allows multiple rounds of interactions such that upon seeing the agent responses, the user can give further commands for the agent to refine or even correct its actions.

title: Evaluating and regulating agentic AI: A study of benchmarks, metrics, and regulation
Claw-Eval-Live: A Live Agent Benchmark for Evolving Real-World Workflows
proposal_tldr: Claw-Eval-Live is introduced, a live benchmark for workflow agents that separates a refreshable signal layer, updated across releases from public workflow-demand signals, from a reproducible, time-stamped release snapshot and suggests that workflow-agent evaluation should be grounded twice, in fresh external demand and in verifiable agent action.

title: ProAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Proactive Assistance with Real-World Data
proposal_tldr: This work introduces ProAgentBench, a rigorous benchmark for proactive agents in working scenarios that showed that long-term memory and historical context significantly enhance prediction accuracy, while real-world training data substantially outperforms synthetic alternatives.

title: MobileWorldBench: Towards Semantic World Modeling For Mobile Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MobileWorldBench, a benchmark that evaluates the ability of vision-language models (VLMs) to function as world models for mobile GUI agents and proposes a novel framework that integrates VLM world models into the planning framework of mobile agents, demonstrating that semantic world models can directly benefit mobile agents by improving task success rates.

title: SusBench: An Online Benchmark for Evaluating Dark Pattern Susceptibility of Computer-Use Agents
venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
proposal_tldr: It is found that both human participants and agents are particularly susceptible to the dark patterns of Preselection, Trick Wording, and Hidden Information, while being resilient to other overt dark patterns.

title: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
proposal_tldr: Behavior Judge is introduced, which addresses this challenge by representing agent executions as behavior narratives and comparing candidate behaviors at this level, substantially improving robustness and success rates and highlighting the strong effectiveness of scaling CUAs, when you do it right.

title: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
proposal_tldr: WALT (Web Agents that Learn Tools), a framework that reverse-engineers latent website functionality into reusable invocable tools, achieves higher success with fewer steps and less LLM-dependent reasoning, establishing a robust and generalizable paradigm for browser automation.

title: FinResearchBench: A Logic Tree based Agent-as-a-Judge Evaluation Framework for Financial Research Agents
venue: International Conference on AI in Finance
proposal_tldr: FinResearchBench is proposed, which is a logic tree-based Agent-as-a-Judge and targets specifically for the financial research agents, and provides a comprehensive and automatic assessment of the research agents across 7 key types of tasks in the financial research domain.

title: The Real Barrier to LLM Agent Usability is Agentic ROI
proposal_tldr: This position paper argues that the central question for LLM agent usability is no longer whether a task can be automated, but whether it delivers sufficient Agentic ROI, and proposes a zigzag developmental trajectory first scaling up to improve information gain and time savings, then scaling down to reduce cost.

title: WebRollback: Enhancing Web Agents with Explicit Rollback Mechanisms
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work enhances web agents with an explicit rollback mechanism, enabling the agent to revert back to a previous state in its navigation trajectory, giving models the flexibility to directly control the search process, leading to an effective and efficient web navigation method.

title: WinClick: GUI Grounding with Multimodal Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WinClick, a novel visual GUI agent developed in Windows platform that leverages screenshots to detect actionable regions and enhances WinClick with GUI grounding pre-training and proposes an LLM-based method for aligning GUI grounding data.

title: Identifying User Goals From UI Trajectories
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a new task-goal identification from observed UI trajectories-aiming to infer the user's detailed intentions when performing a task within UI environments, and introduces a novel evaluation methodology designed to assess whether two intent descriptions can be considered paraphrases within a specific UI environment.

title: Affordable Generative Agents
proposal_tldr: Affordable Generative Agents (AGA) is developed, a framework for enabling the generation of believable and low-cost interactions on both agent-environment and inter-agents levels, and investigates the mechanisms of emergent believable behaviors lying in LLM agents.

title: CompBench: A Comparative Reasoning Benchmark for Multimodal LLMs
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces C OMP B ENCH, a benchmark designed to evaluate the comparative reasoning capability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), and uses it to evaluate recent MLLMs, including GPT-4V(ision), Gemini-Pro, and LLaVA-1.6.

title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
proposal_tldr: On long-horizon complex search, TRACE substantially improves base-model tool-use ability using pure RL, without a cold-start supervised fine-tuning stage, an agentic mid-training stage, or training on live-web data.

title: Polar: Agentic RL on Any Harness at Scale
proposal_tldr: Polar is a rollout framework for scalable asynchronous RL over arbitrary agent harnesses that makes Polar agnostic to agent harnesses, training infrastructure, and RL algorithms while improving compute utilization for long-running agent workloads.

title: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: A plug-in agentic memory framework that equips MLLM-based GUI agents with MementoCore, a learned controller for online memory selection, compression, and retrieval, and develops a scalable data curation pipeline that converts computer-use trajectories into memory-controller training data.

title: MMSkills: Towards Multimodal Skills for General Visual Agents
proposal_tldr: MMSkills are introduced, a framework for representing, generating, and using reusable multimodal procedures for runtime visual decision making and a branch-loaded multimodal skill agent is introduced, suggesting that external multimodal procedural knowledge complements model-internal priors.

title: AgentHER: Hindsight Experience Replay for LLM Agent Trajectory Relabeling
proposal_tldr: AgentHER is introduced, which recovers this lost signal by adapting Hindsight Experience Replay to natural-language agent trajectories and converts discarded failures into SFT, DPO, and ShareGPT training data.

title: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: Inspired by the brain, HyMEM is proposed, a graph-based memory that couples discrete high-level symbolic nodes with continuous trajectory embeddings that consistently improves open-source GUI agents, enabling 7B/8B backbones to match or surpass strong closed-source models.

title: How Well Does Agent Development Reflect Real-World Work?
proposal_tldr: This work systematically study the relationship between agent development efforts and the distribution of real-world human work by mapping benchmark instances to work domains and skills, revealing substantial mismatches between agent development that tends to be programming-centric, and the categories in which human labor and economic value are concentrated.

title: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: UI-Mem is proposed, a novel framework that enhances GUI online RL with a Hierarchical Experience Memory, which significantly outperforms traditional RL baselines and static reuse strategies, with strong generalization to unseen applications.

title: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection via Instruction-Following Intent Analysis
proposal_tldr: Results demonstrate that IntentGuard achieves no utility degradation in all but one setting and strong robustness against adaptive prompt injection attacks (e.g., reducing attack success rates from 100% to 8.5% in a Mind2Web scenario).

title: Prune4Web: DOM Tree Pruning Programming for Web Agent
proposal_tldr: Prune4Web is introduced, a novel paradigm that transforms DOM processing from LLM-based filtering to programmatic pruning, and a key innovation is DOM Tree Pruning Programming, where an LLM generates executable Python scoring programs to dynamically filter DOM elements based on semantic clues from decomposed sub-tasks.

title: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
proposal_tldr: OpenApps is developed, a light-weight open-source ecosystem with six apps (messenger, calendar, maps, etc.) that are configurable in appearance and content that enable easy generation and deployment of thousands of versions of each app.

title: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebCoach, a model-agnostic self-evolving framework that equips web browsing agents with persistent cross-session memory, enabling improved long-term planning, reflection, and continual learning without retraining.

title: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
proposal_tldr: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents built on vision-language models have emerged as a promising approach to automate human-computer workflows. However, they also face the inefficiency challenge as they process long sequences of high-resolution screenshots and solving long-horizon tasks, making inf

title: Towards Understanding Visual Grounding in Visual Language Models
proposal_tldr: The importance of grounding in VLMs is outlined, the core components of the contemporary paradigm for developing grounded models are delineated, and their practical applications are examined, including benchmarks and evaluation metrics for grounded multimodal generation.

title: Atomic-to-Compositional Generalization for Mobile Agents with A New Benchmark and Scheduling System
proposal_tldr: This work introduces UI-NEXUS, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate mobile agents on three categories of compositional operations: Simple Concatenation, Context Transition, and Deep Dive, and proposes AGENT-NEXUS, a lightweight and efficient scheduling system to tackle compositional mobile tasks.

title: BIMgent: Towards Autonomous Building Modeling via Computer-use Agents
proposal_tldr: BIMgent automates the architectural building modeling process, including multimodal input for conceptual design, planning of software-specific workflows, and efficient execution of the authoring GUI actions, highlighting its potential for practical deployment in real-world architectural modeling scenarios.

title: PLAICraft: Large-Scale Time-Aligned Vision-Speech-Action Dataset for Embodied AI
proposal_tldr: PLAICraft, a novel data collection platform and dataset capturing multiplayer Minecraft interactions across five time-aligned modalities, opens a path toward training and evaluating agents that act fluently and purposefully in real time, paving the way for truly embodied artificial intelligence.

title: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
proposal_tldr: This paper investigates the feasibility of adapting AWAs for natural language test case execution and how to evaluate them, and identifies several limitations that need to be addressed to develop more resilient and reliable ATAs, paving the way for robust, low maintenance test automation.

title: Advancing Language Multi-Agent Learning with Credit Re-Assignment for Interactive Environment Generalization
proposal_tldr: This work proposes CollabUIAgents, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework with a novel multi-agent credit re-assignment (CR) strategy, assigning process rewards with LLMs rather than environment-specific rewards and learning with synthesized preference data, in order to foster generalizable, collaborative behaviors among the role-free agents'policies.

title: Lightweight Neural App Control
proposal_tldr: A novel mobile phone control architecture, Lightweight Multi-modal App Control (LiMAC), for efficient interactions and control across various Android apps by integrating a small Action Transformer integrated with a fine-tuned vision-language model (VLM) for real-time decision-making and task execution.

title: ReTA: Recursively Thinking Ahead to Improve the Strategic Reasoning of Large Language Models
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a simple yet effective Recursively Thinking-Ahead (ReTA) agent, incorporating a recursive prompting mechanism that automatically analyzes the opponents’ future moves/actions and assigns reward signals for these situations, to strengthen the strategic reasoning of LLMs.

title: HeaP: Hierarchical Policies for Web Actions using LLMs
proposal_tldr: A novel framework, Hierarchical Policies for Web Actions using LLMs (HeaP), that learns a set of hierarchical LLM prompts from demonstrations for planning high-level tasks and executing them via a sequence of low-level policies, and is able to outperform prior works using orders of magnitude less data.

title: Mobile-Env: An Evaluation Platform and Benchmark for LLM-GUI Interaction
proposal_tldr: This work introduces the GUI interaction platform, Mobile-Env, and conducts comprehensive evaluations of LLM agents, including various versions of GPT, LLaMA 2, and AgentLM, on Wiki-How task set to acquire insights into the potentials and challenges of LLMs in GUI interactions.

title: Policy and World Modeling Co-Training for Language Agents
proposal_tldr: PaW is a Policy and World modeling co-training framework that adds auxiliary WM supervision to the same policy during RL, without changing the inference paradigm, and shows consistent improvements over strong RL baselines across models and RL algorithms.

title: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
proposal_tldr: ContractSkill is presented, a framework that converts a draft skill into an executable artifact with explicit procedural structure, enabling deterministic verifica tion, fault localization, and minimal local repair.

title: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a hierarchical planning framework to analyze web agents across three layers, enabling process-based evaluation of reasoning, grounding, and recovery, and shows that improving perceptual grounding and adaptive control, not only high-level reasoning, is critical for achieving human-level reliability.

title: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: DynaWeb is introduced, a novel MBRL framework that trains web agents through interacting with a web world model trained to predict naturalistic web page representations given agent actions that establishes the viability of training web agents through imagination, offering a scalable and efficient way to scale up online agentic RL.

title: WebVIA: A Web-based Vision-Language Agentic Framework for Interactive and Verifiable UI-to-Code Generation
proposal_tldr: The proposed WebVIA, the first agentic framework for interactive UI-to-Code generation and validation, achieves more stable and accurate UI exploration than general-purpose agents and exhibits substantial improvements in generating executable and interactive HTML/CSS/JavaScript code.

title: SynthAgent: Adapting Web Agents with Synthetic Supervision
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes SynthAgent, a fully synthetic supervision framework that aims at improving synthetic data quality via dual refinement of both tasks and trajectories, and demonstrates that SynthAgent outperforms existing synthetic data methods, validating the importance of high-quality synthetic supervision.

title: GUI-360\°: A Comprehensive Dataset and Benchmark for Computer-Using Agents
proposal_tldr: We introduce GUI-360$^\circ$, a large-scale, comprehensive dataset and benchmark suite designed to advance computer-using agents (CUAs). CUAs present unique challenges and is constrained by three persistent gaps: a scarcity of real-world CUA tasks, the lack of automated collection-and-annotation pip

title: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: PAL-UI combines a dual-level summarization agent, capturing both observation-level cues and action-level outcomes, with a dedicated retrieval tool that allows the agent to recall specific historical screenshots during planning, highlighting the potential of active memory retrieval for long-horizon planning capabilities of vision-based GUI agents.

title: GUI-ReWalk: Massive Data Generation for GUI Agent via Stochastic Exploration and Intent-Aware Reasoning
venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: Results demonstrate that GUI-ReWalk enables superior coverage of diverse interaction flows, higher trajectory entropy, and more realistic user intent, establishing GUI-ReWalk as a scalable and data-efficient framework for advancing GUI agent research and enabling robust real-world automation.

title: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: PrivWeb is developed, a trusted add-on on web agents that utilizes a localized LLM to anonymize private information on interfaces based on user preferences, and identifies user delegation strategies: they prefer to manually execute sensitive steps for high-sensitivity data, while granting agent access to low-sensitivity data.

title: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A new benchmark called Amazon-Bench is proposed, and an automated evaluation framework is proposed that assesses both the performance and the safety of web agents, finding that current agents struggle with complex queries and pose safety risks.

title: Chain-of-Memory: Enhancing GUI Agents for Cross-Application Navigation
proposal_tldr: The proposed Chain-of-Memory (CoM), a novel approach for explicitly modeling short-term and long-term memory in GUI agents, enables GUI agents to better understand task states and retain critical historical information persistently.

title: From Standalone LLMs to Integrated Intelligence: A Survey of Compound Al Systems
proposal_tldr: This survey defines the concept of CAIS, proposes a multi-dimensional taxonomy based on component roles and orchestration strategies, and analyzes four foundational paradigms: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), LLM Agents, Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), and Orchestration.

title: Automated Web Application Testing: End-to-End Test Case Generation with Large Language Models and Screen Transition Graphs
proposal_tldr: An automated system for generating test cases for two key aspects of web application testing: site navigation and form filling and a novel integration of graph structures and LLMs for site navigation testing are presented.

title: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
proposal_tldr: AdInject is proposed, a novel and real-world black-box attack method that leverages the internet advertising delivery to inject malicious content into the Web Agent's environment and demonstrates that prevalent advertising delivery constitutes a potent and real-world vector for environment injection attacks against Web Agents.

title: ReGUIDE: Data Efficient GUI Grounding via Spatial Reasoning and Search
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Reasoning Graphical User Interface Grounding for Data Efficiency (ReGUIDE), a novel and effective framework for web grounding that enables MLLMs to learn data efficiently through self-generated reasoning and spatial-aware criticism.

title: Breaking the Data Barrier - Building GUI Agents Through Task Generalization
proposal_tldr: This work proposes training Vision Language Models on data-rich, reasoning-intensive tasks during a dedicated mid-training stage, and examines how incorporating these tasks facilitates generalization to GUI planning scenarios, providing valuable insights into cross-domain knowledge transfer for GUI agents.

title: From Captions to Rewards (CaReVL): Leveraging Large Language Model Experts for Enhanced Reward Modeling in Large Vision-Language Models
proposal_tldr: (CaReVL) is proposed, a novel method for preference reward modeling by reliably using both high- and low-confidence data, which achieves performance improvements over traditional distillation-based methods on VL-RewardBench and MLLM-as-a-Judge benchmark, demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Smoothing Grounding and Reasoning for MLLM-Powered GUI Agents with Query-Oriented Pivot Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a query-oriented pivot approach called query inference, which serves as a bridge between GUI grounding and reasoning, and shows that query inference outperforms previous grounding techniques under the same training data scale.

title: Toward Automated Scientific Discovery in Hydrology: The Opportunities and Dangers of AI Augmented Research Frameworks
proposal_tldr: It is argued that AI‐assisted workflows could democratise advanced hydrological modelling, enabling researchers worldwide to address critical water resources challenges, particularly in understudied regions.

title: DreamStruct: Understanding Slides and User Interfaces via Synthetic Data Generation
proposal_tldr: This work presents a method to generate synthetic, structured visuals with target labels using code generation, which allows people to create datasets with built-in labels and train models with a small number of human-annotated examples.

title: NaviQAte: Functionality-Guided Web Application Navigation
proposal_tldr: NaviQAte is introduced, which frames web application exploration as a question-and-answer task, generating action sequences for functionalities without requiring detailed parameters, and focuses on functionality-guided web application navigation, integrating multi-modal inputs such as text and images to enhance contextual understanding.

title: A Survey on Evaluation of LLM-based Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: VoxelPrompt: A Vision-Language Agent for Grounded Medical Image Analysis
proposal_tldr: By supporting accurate image processing with language interaction, VoxelPrompt provides comprehensive utility for numerous imaging tasks that traditionally require specialized models to address, while facilitating a much larger range of tasks.

title: GameCraft-Bench: Can Agents Build Playable Games End-to-End in a Real Game Engine?
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an interaction-grounded evaluation framework that assesses executable gameplay through replayed demonstrations and rubric-guided multimodal judging, and instantiates this framework as GameCraft-Bench, a benchmark comprising 140 Godot tasks across 15 game families.

title: GRASP: Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer for Self-Improving LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces GRASP (Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer), which treats agent improvement as a sequence of edits to a bounded skill library, admitting each candidate only if it produces a net improvement on a balanced held-out probe under a hard regression budget.

title: Agentic AI in Healthcare: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
proposal_tldr: This survey provides an in-depth discussion on the core aspects and challenges of Agentic AI in healthcare, including its applications in electronic health records interactions, clinical triage, medical question-answering, and disease diagnosis.

title: On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: The analysis shows that reliability depends on both how tasks are specified and how agent behavior varies across executions, and suggests the need to evaluate agents under repeated execution, to allow agents to resolve task ambiguity through interaction, and to favor strategies that remain stable across runs.

title: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
proposal_tldr: OpenMobile is presented, an open-source framework that synthesizes high-quality task instructions and agent trajectories, with two key components: a scalable task synthesis pipeline that constructs a global environment memory from exploration, then leverages it to generate diverse and grounded instructions.

title: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
proposal_tldr: HealthAdminBench is introduced, a benchmark comprising four realistic GUI environments: an EHR, two payer portals, and a fax system, and 135 expert-defined tasks spanning three administrative task types: Prior Authorization, Appeals and Denials Management, and Durable Medical Equipment Order Processing, which reveals a substantial gap between current agent capabilities and the demands of real-world administrative workflows.

title: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
proposal_tldr: UI-Voyager is proposed, a novel two-stage self-evolving mobile GUI agent that employs Rejection Fine-Tuning (RFT) and introduces Group Relative Self-Distillation (GRSD), which identifies critical fork points in group rollouts and constructs dense step-level supervision from successful trajectories to correct failed ones.

title: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: The findings demonstrate that combining explicit inference-time planning with milestone-based rewards significantly improves an agent's long-horizon capabilities, paving the way for more robust and general-purpose autonomous systems.

title: General Agent Evaluation
proposal_tldr: This is the first systematic study, comparing tool-calling, MCP, code-generation, and CLI agents on the same benchmarks with the same models, and finds that general agents adapt to every tested domain without per-domain customization.

title: AgenticShop: Benchmarking Agentic Product Curation for Personalized Web Shopping
proposal_tldr: This work presents AgenticShop, the first benchmark for evaluating agentic systems on personalized product curation in open-web environment, and features realistic shopping scenarios, diverse user profiles, and a verifiable, checklist-driven personalization evaluation framework.

title: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes WebSentinel, a two-step approach for detecting and localizing prompt injection attacks in webpages, and shows that WebSentinel is highly effective, substantially outperforming baseline methods across multiple datasets of both contaminated and clean webpages that were collected.

title: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
proposal_tldr: OmegaUse, a general-purpose GUI agent model for autonomous task execution on both mobile and desktop platforms, supporting computer-use and phone-use scenarios, is presented, built on a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) backbone.

title: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: GUI-Eyes, a reinforcement learning framework for active visual perception in GUI tasks, is presented, which introduces a progressive perception strategy that decomposes the decision-making into coarse exploration and fine-grained grounding, coordinated by a two-level policy.

title: MegaFlow: Large-Scale Distributed Orchestration System for the Agentic Era
proposal_tldr: Large-scale distributed orchestration system that enables efficient scheduling, resource allocation, and fine-grained task management for agent-environment workloads and addresses a critical infrastructure gap in the emerging agentic AI landscape.

title: Scaling Graph Chain-of-Thought Reasoning: A Multi-Agent Framework with Efficient LLM Serving
proposal_tldr: GLM decomposes reasoning into specialized agents for classification, reasoning, action generation, and graph retrieval, enabling branching and selective context sharing to reduce prompt length and reasoning iterations while preserving reasoning quality, thereby improving accuracy and reducing overall token consumption.

title: ColorBench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents with Graph-Structured Framework for Complex Long-Horizon Tasks
proposal_tldr: A novel graph-structured benchmarking framework that achieves static simulation of dynamic behaviors by modeling the finite states observed during real-device interactions, and develops ColorBench, a benchmark focused on complex long-horizon tasks.

title: Benchmarking MLLM-based Web Understanding: Reasoning, Robustness and Safety
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive web understanding benchmark, named WebRRSBench, that jointly evaluates Reasoning, Robustness, and Safety across eight tasks, such as position relationship reasoning, color robustness, and safety critical detection, etc.

title: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
proposal_tldr: This work reframe GUI grounding as an interactive search task, where the VLM generates actions to move a cursor in the GUI to locate UI elements, and trains the GUI grounding model, GUI-Cursor, using multi-step online reinforcement learning with a dense trajectory-based reward function.

title: PilotRL: Training Language Model Agents via Global Planning-Guided Progressive Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: An adaptive global plan-based agent paradigm AdaPlan is introduced, aiming to synergize high-level explicit guidance with execution to support effective long-horizon decision-making and PilotRL, a global planning-guided training framework for LLM agents driven by progressive reinforcement learning are put forward.

title: What Limits Virtual Agent Application? OmniBench: A Scalable Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Essential Virtual Agent Capabilities
proposal_tldr: OmniBench is introduced, a self-generating, cross-platform, graph-based benchmark with an automated pipeline for synthesizing tasks of controllable complexity through subtask composition and OmniEval, a multidimensional evaluation framework that includes subtask-level evaluation, graph-based metrics, and comprehensive tests across 10 capabilities.

title: ResTest: Targeted Coverage of Residual Not-Covered Code Using Large Language Models for Web GUI Testing
proposal_tldr: ResTest is proposed, a complementary approach that uses coverage-report-guided LLMs to target residual not-covered code left by existing AWGT approaches to improve code coverage.

title: OSUniverse: Benchmark for Multimodal GUI-navigation AI Agents
proposal_tldr: A benchmark of complex, multimodal desktop-oriented tasks for advanced GUI-navigation AI agents that focuses on ease of use, extensibility, comprehensive coverage of test cases, and automated validation, and an automated validation mechanism that has an average error rate less than 2%.

title: Browsing Lost Unformed Recollections: A Benchmark for Tip-of-the-Tongue Search and Reasoning
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: We introduce Browsing Lost Unformed Recollections, a tip-of-the-tongue known-item search and reasoning benchmark for general AI assistants. BLUR introduces a set of 573 real-world validated questions that demand searching and reasoning across multi-modal and multilingual inputs, as well as proficien

title: A Shopping Agent for Addressing Subjective Product Needs
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an agentic approach driven by large language models to streamline this process by autonomously executing various user actions to handle subjective queries in e-commerce, enhancing personalization, product exploration, and selection in a user-centric manner.

title: GenTool: Enhancing Tool Generalization in Language Models through Zero-to-One and Weak-to-Strong Simulation
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: GenTool is presented, a novel training framework that prepares LLMs for diverse generalization challenges in tool utilization and significantly enhances the tool-usage capabilities of LLMs ranging from 1B to 8B parameters, achieving performance that surpasses GPT-4o.

title: PC Agent: While You Sleep, AI Works - A Cognitive Journey into Digital World
proposal_tldr: The preliminary experiments in PowerPoint presentation creation reveal that complex digital work capabilities can be achieved with a small amount of high-quality cognitive data - PC Agent, trained on just 133 cognitive trajectories, can handle sophisticated work scenarios involving up to 50 steps across multiple applications.

title: Software Vulnerability Detection Using LLM: Does Additional Information Help?
venue: 2024 Annual Computer Security Applications Conference Workshops (ACSAC Workshops)
proposal_tldr: Unlike conventional machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) methods, Large Language Models (LLM) possess the ability to tackle complex tasks through intricate chains of reasoning, a facet often overlooked in existing work on vulnerability detection. Nevertheless, these models have demonstrated v

title: Towards Full Delegation: Designing Ideal Agentic Behaviors for Travel Planning
proposal_tldr: This work proposes APEC Agent Constitution, a list of criteria that an agent should follow for good agentic behaviors, including Accuracy, Proactivity, Efficiency and Credibility, and develops APEC-Travel, a travel planning agent that proactively extracts hidden personalized needs via multi-round dialog with travelers.

title: A Taxonomy of Architecture Options for Foundation Model-based Agents: Analysis and Decision Model
proposal_tldr: A taxonomy focused on the architectures of foundation-model-based agents is introduced, addressing critical aspects such as functional capabilities and non-functional qualities and unifying and detailing these classifications to improve the design of foundation-model-based agents.

title: MetaTool: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master Tools with Meta-task Augmentation
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd ACM Workshop in AI-powered Question & Answering Systems
proposal_tldr: By incorporating meta-task data into task-oriented training, the MetaTool method significantly enhances the performance of open-source LLMs, achieving results comparable to ChatGPT in both tool-based planning and chatting scenarios.

title: AQA-Bench: An Interactive Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs' Sequential Reasoning Ability
proposal_tldr: This paper comprehensively build AQA-Bench with three different algorithms, namely binary search, depth-first search, and breadth-first search, and to evaluate the sequential reasoning ability of 14 different LLMs, revealing several interesting findings.

title: Inherent limitations of LLMs regarding spatial information
proposal_tldr: A novel evaluation framework complemented by a baseline dataset is introduced to assess the spatial reasoning abilities of ChatGPT and reveals key insights into the model's capabilities and limitations in spatial understanding.

title: Thinking vs. Doing: Improving Agent Reasoning by Scaling Test-Time Interaction
proposal_tldr: The results establish interaction scaling as a powerful, complementary axis to scaling per-step compute, offering new avenues for training adaptive agents and introducing TTI (Test-Time Interaction), a curriculum-based online reinforcement learning (RL) approach that trains agents by adaptively adjusting their rollout lengths.

title: SimuCourt: Building Judicial Decision-Making Agents with Real-world Judgement Documents
proposal_tldr: SimuCourt is introduced, a judicial benchmark that encompasses 420 judgment documents from real-world, spanning the three most common types of judicial cases, and a novel task Judicial Decision-Making to evaluate the judicial analysis and decision-making power of agents is proposed.

title: Mitigating Generative Agent Social Dilemmas
proposal_tldr: An initial study of outcomes that arise when deploying generative agents in social dilemmas is performed, and preliminary experiments are conducted to provide evidence that contracting helps improve outcomes for generative agents in social dilemmas.

title: Lingering Authority: Revocable Resource-and-Effect Capabilities for Coding Agents
proposal_tldr: PORTICO is a reference monitor for revocable capabilities exposed to the planner that compiles an explicit task contract into initial capabilities, grant rules, trusted closure predicates, and global deny rules.

title: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: Experiments show that OpenComputer's hard-coded verifiers align more closely with human adjudication than LLM-as-judge evaluation, especially when success depends on fine-grained application state.

title: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
proposal_tldr: PlayCoder is introduced, a multi-agent, repository-aware framework that writes, evaluates and refines GUI application code via closed-loop control that substantially improves functional correctness and semantic alignment for both open-source and closed-source models.

title: OpAgent: Operator Agent for Web Navigation
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a robust Online Reinforcement Learning WebAgent, designed to optimize its policy through direct, iterative interactions with unconstrained wide websites, and introduces a modular agentic framework, namely OpAgent, that enables robust error recovery and self-correction.

title: OdysseyArena: Benchmarking Large Language Models For Long-Horizon, Active and Inductive Interactions
proposal_tldr: OdysseyArena is introduced, which re-centers agent evaluation on long-horizon, active, and inductive interactions, and establishes OdysseyArena-Lite for standardized benchmarking, providing a set of 120 tasks to measure an agent's inductive efficiency and long-horizon discovery.

title: FutureX-Pro: Extending Future Prediction to High-Value Vertical Domains
proposal_tldr: The performance gap between generalist reasoning and the precision required for high-value vertical applications is revealed and State-of-the-Art agentic LLMs possess the domain grounding necessary for industrial deployment are assessed.

title: SafePro: Evaluating the Safety of Professional-Level AI Agents
proposal_tldr: The evaluation of state-of-the-art AI models reveals significant safety vulnerabilities and uncovers new unsafe behaviors in professional contexts, and highlights the urgent need for robust safety mechanisms tailored to the next generation of professional AI agents.

title: PPTArena: A Benchmark for PowerPoint Editing
proposal_tldr: PPTArena is introduced, a benchmark for PowerPoint editing that evaluates how agents modify real slides from natural-language instructions, and PPTPilot, a structure-aware agent that plans semantic edit sequences, routes between programmatic tools and deterministic XML operations, and verifies each result in an iterative plan-edit-check loop.

title: ShoppingComp: Are LLMs Really Ready for Your Shopping Cart?
proposal_tldr: Error analysis reflects limitations in core agent competencies, including information grounding in open-world environments, reliable verification of multi-constraint requirements, consistent reasoning over noisy and conflicting evidence, and risk-aware decision making.

title: UINavBench: A Framework for Comprehensive Evaluation of Interactive Digital Agents
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision

title: CORE: Reducing UI Exposure in Mobile Agents via Collaboration Between Cloud and Local LLMs
proposal_tldr: Experiments show that CORE reduces UI exposure by up to 55.6% while maintaining task success rates slightly below cloud-only agents, effectively mitigating unnecessary privacy exposure to the cloud.

title: Fundamentals of Building Autonomous LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper shows how integrating these systems leads to more capable and generalized software bots that mimic human cognitive processes for autonomous and intelligent behavior.

title: Beyond Data Privacy: New Privacy Risks for Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This paper systematically examines emerging privacy risks of LLMs, discussing potential mitigation strategies and calling for the research community to broaden its focus beyond data privacy risks, developing new defenses to address the evolving threats posed by increasingly powerful LLMs and LLM-powered systems.

title: Multi-Turn Puzzles: Evaluating Interactive Reasoning and Strategic Dialogue in LLMs
proposal_tldr: A novel benchmark comprising a suite of multi-turn tasks each designed to test specific reasoning, interactive dialogue, and information-seeking abilities is introduced, showing that most errors emerge from poor instruction following, reasoning failures, and poor planning.

title: VeriWeb: Verifiable Long-Chain Web Benchmark for Agentic Information-Seeking
proposal_tldr: This work introduces VeriWeb, a novel verifiable long-chain web benchmark designed to facilitate the evaluation and development of web agents within realistic web environments, and highlights two critical dimensions: long-chain complexity and subtask-level verifiability.

title: Researchy Questions: A Dataset of Multi-Perspective, Decompositional Questions for Deep Research
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: Researchy Questions is presented, the world's first, only and largest public dataset of ''Deep Research'' questions filtered from real search engine logs to be non-factoid, ''decompositional'' and multi-perspective, and shows that ''slow thinking'' answering techniques, like decomposition into sub-questions shows benefit over answering directly.

title: Automated Skill Discovery for Language Agents through Exploration and Iterative Feedback
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel automatic skill discovery framework EXIF, designed to improve the feasibility of generated target behaviors while accounting for the agents'capabilities, and adopts an exploration-first strategy by employing an exploration agent to train the target agent to learn essential skills in the environment.

title: FormFactory: An Interactive Benchmarking Suite for Multimodal Form-Filling Agents
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art MLLMs is conducted and it is observed that no model surpasses 5% accuracy, underscoring the inherent difficulty of the task and revealing significant limitations in current models' visual layout reasoning and field-value alignment abilities.

title: Orca: Browsing at Scale Through User-Driven and AI-Facilitated Orchestration Across Malleable Webpages
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: This work explores how AI could instead augment user interactions with content across webpages and mitigate cognitive and manual efforts and presents novel interactions with the prototype web browser, Orca, which supports user-driven exploration, operation, organization, and synthesis of web content at scale.

title: PLANET: A Collection of Benchmarks for Evaluating LLMs' Planning Capabilities
proposal_tldr: This study examines a range of planning benchmarks to identify commonly used testbeds for algorithm development and highlight potential gaps, and recommends the most appropriate benchmarks for various algorithms and offers insights to guide future benchmark development.

title: Agent-Initiated Interaction in Phone UI Automation
proposal_tldr: A task formulation for detecting the need for user interaction and generating appropriate messages is introduced, including aspects like interaction timing and the scope of the agent's autonomy, within the context of phone UI automation.

title: Boosting Virtual Agent Learning and Reasoning: A Step-wise, Multi-dimensional, and Generalist Reward Model with Benchmark
proposal_tldr: Experimental results demonstrate that Similar, through its step-wise, multi-dimensional assessment and synergistic gain, provides GVAs with effective intermediate signals during both training and inference-time scaling.

title: WebGames: Challenging General-Purpose Web-Browsing AI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebGames, a comprehensive benchmark suite designed to evaluate general-purpose web-browsing AI agents through a collection of 50+ interactive challenges, and evaluates leading vision-language models including GPT-4o, Claude Computer-Use, Gemini-1.5-Pro, and Qwen2-VL against human performance.

title: DiMA: An LLM-Powered Ride-Hailing Assistant at DiDi
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces DiMA, an LLM-powered ride-hailing assistant deployed in DiDi Chuxing, and introduces a continual fine-tuning scheme that utilizes real-world interactions and simulated dialogues to align the assistant's behavior with human prefered decision-making processes.

title: Generalist Virtual Agents: A Survey on Autonomous Agents Across Digital Platforms
proposal_tldr: This paper aims to bridge the theoretical and practical aspects of GVAs, concluding those that operate in environments closely mirroring the real world are more likely to demonstrate human-like intelligence.

title: EDGE: Enhanced Grounded GUI Understanding with Enriched Multi-Granularity Synthetic Data
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes EDGE, a general data synthesis framework that automatically generates large-scale, multi-granularity training data from webpages across the Web and significantly reduces the dependence on manual annotations, empowering researchers to harness the vast public resources available on the Web to advance their work.

title: Robust RL with LLM-Driven Data Synthesis and Policy Adaptation for Autonomous Driving
proposal_tldr: Through fine-tuning via online environment interaction, RAPID reduces the forgetting of LLM knowledge while maintaining adaptability to different tasks, and demonstrates RAPID's capability to effectively integrate LLM knowledge into scaled-down RL policies in an efficient, adaptable, and robust way.

title: LangSuitE: Planning, Controlling and Interacting with Large Language Models in Embodied Text Environments
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: LangSuitE, a versatile and simulation-free testbed featuring 6 representative embodied tasks in textual embodied worlds, offers adaptability to diverse environments without multiple simulation engines, evaluates agents' capacity to develop ``internalized world knowledge'' with embodied observations, and allows easy customization of communication and action strategies.

title: Semantic Constraint Inference for Web Form Test Generation
venue: International Symposium on Software Testing and Analysis
proposal_tldr: This work bridges the existing gap in automated web form testing by intertwining the capabilities of LLMs with advanced semantic inference methods, and introduces an innovative approach, called FormNexus, for automated web form test generation, which emphasizes deriving semantic insights from individual form elements and relations among them.

title: "What's important here?": Opportunities and Challenges of Using LLMs in Retrieving Information from Web Interfaces
proposal_tldr: In contrast with prior works, which primarily focused on autonomous web navigation, this work decomposes the problem as an even atomic operation - Can LLMs identify the important information in the web page for a user given query?

title: Browsing Like Human: A Multimodal Web Agent with Experiential Fast-and-Slow Thinking
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a novel multimodal web agent framework called WebExperT, which is designed to emulate the human planning process of "thinking fast and slow" to effectively decompose complex user instructions.

title: GestureGPT: Zero-shot Interactive Gesture Understanding and Grounding with Large Language Model Agents
AndroidDaily: A Verifiable Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents on Real-World Closed-Source Applications
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Guideline-grounded Reviewer for Automatic Diagnostic Evaluation (GRADE), a process-aware evaluator built on a three-tiered system of observable external guidelines: operational obligations, output quality, and negative constraints, turning long-horizon, open-ended mobile interactions into verifiable evaluation without relying on hidden internal states.

title: WebGameBench: Requirement-to-Application Evaluation for Coding Agents via Browser-Native Games
proposal_tldr: To the authors' knowledge, WebGameBench is the first requirement-to-application benchmark for browser-native game delivery that validates delivered-application runtime labels against independent human gameplay review under the Usable-rate criterion.

title: WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A computer-use benchmark in cross-application workflows, named WindowsWorld, designed to systematically assess GUI Agents on complex multi-step tasks that mirror real-world professional activities, is presented.

title: CL-bench Life: Can Language Models Learn from Real-Life Context?
proposal_tldr: This work introduces CL-bench Life, a fully human-curated benchmark comprising 405 context-task pairs and 5,348 verification rubrics, covering common real-life scenarios, and evaluates ten frontier LMs, finding that real-life context learning remains highly challenging.

title: Quantifying Trust: Financial Risk Management for Trustworthy AI Agents
proposal_tldr: The Agentic Risk Standard (ARS), a payment settlement standard for AI-mediated transactions, is introduced, a payment settlement standard for AI-mediated transactions that integrates risk assessment, underwriting, and compensation into a single transaction framework that protects users when interacting with agents.

title: LiveClawBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Complex, Real-World Assistant Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work introduces LiveClawBench, a benchmark designed around this dual-fidelity requirement that combines a Triple-Axis Complexity Framework for difficulty-driven task construction with reproducible full-stack mock applications that preserve stateful execution semantics.

title: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
proposal_tldr: Through experiments on web agent benchmarks, it is shown that agents trained with VeriEnv generalize to unseen websites, achieve site-specific mastery through self-evolving training, and benefit from scaling the number of training environments.

title: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: MAGNET is introduced, a memory-driven adaptive agent framework with dual-level memory: stationary memory linking diverse visual features to stable functional semantics for robust action grounding and procedural memory capturing stable task intents across varying workflows for robust action grounding and generalization in evolving software environments.

title: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A scalable data synthesis pipeline is introduced that transforms noisy rollouts into reliable supervision without human annotation and establishes step-level filtering as a key principle for scalable CUA training and construct two new datasets and a lightweight process reward model as practical tools to advance robust and efficient CUAs.

title: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
proposal_tldr: Evaluations across thousands of trajectories from six web agents show that the graph abstraction captures cross-model regularities, highlights redundancy and inefficiency, and identifies critical decision points overlooked by outcome-based metrics.

title: Dyna-Mind: Learning to Simulate from Experience for Better AI Agents
proposal_tldr: Dyna-Mind, a two-stage training framework that explicitly teaches (V)LM agents to integrate simulation ability into AI agents, and Dyna-GRPO, an online reinforcement learning method that leverages outcome and interaction-level signals to learn better policies for long-horizon, planning-intensive tasks are introduced.

title: Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos
proposal_tldr: Watch&Learn (W&L), a framework that converts readily available Internet videos of human computer use into executable UI trajectories at scale, is presented, which casts trajectory annotation as an inverse dynamics problem that predicts user actions from consecutive screen states, which simplifies learning and generalizes across domains.

title: GEM-Bench: A Benchmark for Ad-Injected Response Generation within Generative Engine Marketing
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: Preliminary results indicate that, while simple prompt-based methods achieve reasonable engagement such as click-through rate, they often reduce user satisfaction, and highlight the need for future research on designing more effective and efficient solutions for generating ad-injected responses in GEM.

title: PG-Agent: An Agent Powered by Page Graph
proposal_tldr: An automated pipeline is designed to transform sequential episodes of multi-step operations across pages into page graphs, which explicitly model the graph structure of the pages that are naturally connected by actions.

title: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments
proposal_tldr: This work evaluates a diverse set of state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs as web agents, analyze failure cases, and conduct ablation studies to assess the impact of visual grounding, plan-based reasoning, and interaction design in EconWebArena.

title: WorkForceAgent-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLM-based Web Agents via Reinforcement Learning
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This study introduces WorkForceAgent-R1, an LLM-based web agent trained using a rule-based R1-style reinforcement learning framework designed explicitly to enhance single-step reasoning and planning for business-oriented web navigation tasks.

title: LaMDAgent: An Autonomous Framework for Post-Training Pipeline Optimization via LLM Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work introduces LaMDAgent (short for Language Model Developing Agent), a novel framework that autonomously constructs and optimizes full post-training pipelines through the use of LLM-based agents, and analyzes the impact of data and model size scaling to reduce computational costs on the exploration.

title: TransBench: Breaking Barriers for Transferable Graphical User Interface Agents in Dynamic Digital Environments
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: TransBench is introduced, the first benchmark designed to systematically evaluate and enhance the transferability of GUI agents across three key dimensions: cross-version transferability (adapting to version updates), cross-platform transferability (generalizing across platforms like iOS, Android, and Web), and cross-application transferability (handling tasks spanning functionally distinct apps).

title: Skill Discovery for Software Scripting Automation via Offline Simulations with LLMs
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This is the first attempt to use software scripting interfaces as a testbed for LLM-based systems, highlighting the advantages of leveraging execution feedback in a controlled environment and offering valuable insights into aligning AI capabilities with user needs in specialized software domains.

title: From Operation to Cognition: Automatic Modeling Cognitive Dependencies from User Demonstrations for GUI Task Automation
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: This work proposes TaskMind, a system that automatically identifies the semantics of operations, and the cognitive dependencies between operations from demonstrations, building a user-interpretable task graph, and compared it with a baseline end-to-end LLM which automates tasks from demonstrations and natural language commands, without task graph.

title: In-Context Defense in Computer Agents: An Empirical Study
