proposal_tldr: This work introduces textbf{in-context defense}, leveraging in-context learning and chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning to counter context deception attacks, and highlights that defensive reasoning must precede action planning for optimal performance, and a minimal number of exemplars is sufficient to induce an agent's defensive behavior.

title: Trishul: Towards Region Identification and Screen Hierarchy Understanding for Large VLM Based GUI Agents
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
proposal_tldr: TRISHUL is introduced, a novel, training-free agentic framework that enhances generalist LVLMs for holistic GUI comprehension and demonstrates TRISHUL's superior performance in action grounding across the ScreenSpot, VisualWebBench, AITW, and Mind2Web datasets.

title: Reverse Image Retrieval Cues Parametric Memory in Multimodal LLMs
proposal_tldr: RIR robustly improves knowledge-intensive visual question answering of GPT-4V by 37-43%, GPT-4 Turbo by 25-27%, and GPT-4o by 18-20% in terms of open-ended VQA evaluation metrics.

title: Knowing When to STOP , RECOVER , and SEARCH A Modular Framework for GUI Automation
MatrAIx: Simulating the World with 8.3 Billion Persona Agents
proposal_tldr: MatrAIx is introduced, a population-scale simulated-user evaluation infrastructure for testing AI systems and digital products with heterogeneous users and provides an end-to-end infrastructure for evaluating AI systems and digital products with diverse simulated human users.

title: SCALECUA: Scaling Computer Use Agents with Verifiable Task Synthesis and Efficient Online RL
proposal_tldr: This work introduces ScaleCUA, a unified framework that scales online RL for CUAs via verifiable task synthesis and efficient training, and designs VeriGen, an end-to-end framework for generating verifiable RL tasks through iterative docker interactions and a multi-agent feedback loop.

title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?
proposal_tldr: It is found that model scale, reasoning, and agent scaffolding affect abstention in different ways, where larger or more capable models sometimes perform worse at timely abstention.

title: Group-Graph Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: Group-Graph Policy Optimization (G2PO), a novel group-based RL algorithm tailored for multi-turn agentic tasks, which redefine agent actions as transitions between state nodes and propose an edge-centric advantage estimation strategy.

title: Search-Time Contamination in Deep Research Agents: Measuring Performance Inflation in Public Benchmark Evaluation
proposal_tldr: The findings show that existing evaluations may overestimate true reasoning ability, and advocate contamination-aware practices, including isolated sandboxes, transparent search trajectories, and controlled benchmark access.

title: CLI-Anything: Towards Agent-Native Computer Use
proposal_tldr: CLI-Hub is built as a comprehensive platform that operationalizes this agent-native computer use vision and provides methodology, architecture, and infrastructure for this fundamental transformation of computer use.

title: Agent-BRACE: Decoupling Beliefs from Actions in Long-Horizon Tasks via Verbalized State Uncertainty
proposal_tldr: Agent-BRACE is introduced, a method that decouples an LLM agent into a belief state model and a policy model, jointly optimized via reinforcement learning, and shows that the learned belief becomes increasingly calibrated over the course of an episode as evidence accumulates.

title: OCR-Memory: Optical Context Retrieval for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Experiments on long-horizon agent benchmarks show consistent gains under strict context limits, demonstrating that optical encoding increases effective memory capacity while preserving faithful evidence recovery.

title: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
proposal_tldr: This framework combines two complementary signals: a Stuck Monitor that detects degraded progress from recent reasoning-action history and triggers recovery, and a Milestone Monitor that identifies semantically meaningful checkpoints where sparse verification is most informative for catching drift.

title: Every Response Counts: Quantifying Uncertainty of LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Tensor Decomposition
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: MATU moves beyond analyzing final text outputs by representing entire reasoning trajectories as embedding matrices and organizing multiple execution runs into a higher-order tensor, offering a comprehensive reliability measure that is generalizable across different agent structures.

title: GUIDE: Interpretable GUI Agent Evaluation via Hierarchical Diagnosis
proposal_tldr: GUIDE (GUI Understanding and Interpretable Diagnostic Evaluation), a framework that decomposes trajectory assessment into three sequential stages mirroring the compositional structure of GUI tasks, substantially outperforms existing evaluators and mitigates the context overload that degrades existing evaluators as task complexity grows.

title: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
proposal_tldr: CarePilot, a multi-agent framework based on the actor-critic paradigm, achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming strong closed-source and open-source multimodal baselines by approximately 15.26% and 3.38%, respectively, on the authors' benchmark and out-of-distribution dataset.

title: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: HATS, a Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis framework designed to mitigate the impact of semantic ambiguity, is proposed and extensive experiments show that agents trained with HATS consistently outperform state-of-the-art baselines across benchmark GUI environments.

title: DIVE: Scaling Diversity in Agentic Task Synthesis for Generalizable Tool Use
proposal_tldr: DIVE is proposed, an evidence-driven recipe that inverts synthesis order, executing diverse, real-world tools first and reverse-deriving tasks strictly entailed by the resulting traces, thereby providing grounding by construction in scaling diversity.

title: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents a scalable and cost-effective paradigm for transforming passive internet knowledge into active, grounded intelligence, marking a critical step towards general-purpose interactive agents.

title: Atomicity for Agents: Exposing, Exploiting, and Mitigating TOCTOU Vulnerabilities in Browser-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: A lightweight mitigation based on pre-execution validation that monitors DOM and layout changes during planning and validates the page state immediately before action execution reduces the risk of insecure execution and mitigates unintended side effects in browser-use agents

title: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
proposal_tldr: CATTS is introduced, a simple technique for dynamically allocating compute for multi-step agents that improves performance on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web, and GoBrowse by up to 11.8% over majority voting while using fewer tokens than uniform scaling, providing both efficiency gains and an interpretable decision rule.

title: ShowUI-Aloha: Human-Taught GUI Agent
proposal_tldr: ShowUI-Aloha is introduced, a comprehensive pipeline that transforms unstructured, in-the-wild human screen recordings from desktop environments into structured, actionable tasks and provides a scalable solution for collecting and parsing real-world human data.

title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk Constraints
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 5th International Conference on Big Data, Information and Computer Network
proposal_tldr: A constrained Agentic reinforcement learning model for Web Agents is proposed, unifying page access, search requests, and external API calls into a unified long-term decision-making framework with associated costs, highlighting the necessity and effectiveness of constraint modeling for practical Web Agent deployment.

title: DeepResearch-Slice: Bridging the Retrieval-Utilization Gap via Explicit Text Slicing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes DeepResearch-Slice, a simple yet effective neuro-symbolic framework that predicts precise span indices to perform a deterministic hard filter before reasoning, and applies it to frozen backbones, highlighting the need for explicit grounding mechanisms in open-ended research.

title: Privacy Practices of Browser Agents
proposal_tldr: A framework of five broad factors (totaling 15 distinct measurements) is presented to measure the privacy risks in browser agents and identifies 30 vulnerabilities, ranging from disabled browser privacy features to"autocompleting"sensitive personal information in form fields.

title: GUI-AIMA: Aligning Intrinsic Multimodal Attention with a Context Anchor for GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: gui-AIMA, an attention-based and coordinate-free supervised fine-tuning framework for efficient GUI grounding that aligns the intrinsic multimodal attention of MLLMs with patch-wise grounding signals, achieves state-of-the-art performance among 3B models.

title: ReUseIt: Synthesizing Reusable AI Agent Workflows for Web Automation
venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
proposal_tldr: This work automatically synthesizes reusable workflows from an agent’s successful and failed attempts, which enables agents to successfully complete repetitive tasks of the same type with minimal user intervention.

title: Graph2Eval: Automatic Multimodal Task Generation for Agents via Knowledge Graphs
proposal_tldr: Graph2Eval is introduced, a knowledge-graph-driven framework for automated, scalable, and semantically grounded agent task generation that unifying both RAG Agent and Web Agent scenarios enables efficient generation of multimodal document understanding tasks and multi-step web interaction tasks.

title: Deep Research Comparator: A Platform For Fine-grained Human Annotations of Deep Research Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Deep Research Comparator, a holistic annotation platform for the human evaluation of deep research agents, and develops Simple Deepresearch, an agent scaffold that serves as a baseline to facilitate the integration of various large language models to transform them into deep research agents for evaluation.

title: ScholarSearch: Benchmarking Scholar Searching Ability of LLMs
proposal_tldr: Through ScholarSearch, the first dataset specifically designed to evaluate the complex information retrieval capabilities of Large Language Models in academic research is proposed, which is expected to more precisely measure and promote the performance improvement of LLMs in complex academic information retrieval tasks.

title: Benchmarking Vision, Language, & Action Models in Procedurally Generated, Open Ended Action Environments
proposal_tldr: MultiNet v0.2 is introduced, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate and analyze the generalization performance of state-of-the-art VLMs and VLAs on diverse procedural tasks from the Procgen benchmark, and identifies critical areas for improvement in their application to out-of-distribution digital tasks.

title: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an approach that guides VLM agents with process supervision by a reward model during GUI navigation and control at inference time that allows the VLM agent to optimize actions at each inference step, thereby improving performance in both static and dynamic environments.

title: Navi-plus: Managing Ambiguous GUI Navigation Tasks with Follow-up
proposal_tldr: The results show that agents equipped with the ability to ask GUI follow-up questions can fully recover their performance when faced with ambiguous user tasks.

title: Cerebrum (AIOS SDK): A Platform for Agent Development, Deployment, Distribution, and Discovery
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Cerebrum is an Agent SDK for AIOS that addresses the gap in agent development by providing a unified framework that standardizes agent development while maintaining flexibility for researchers and developers to innovate and distribute their agents.

title: Iris: Breaking GUI Complexity with Adaptive Focus and Self-Refining
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
proposal_tldr: Iris is introduced, a foundational visual agent that addresses challenges in visual perception through two key innovations: Information-Sensitive Cropping (ISC) and Self-Refining Dual Learning (SRDL).

title: Automated Test Transfer across Android Apps using Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: An innovative technique, LLMigrate, is introduced, which leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to efficiently transfer usage-based UI tests across mobile apps, and can achieve a 97.5% success rate, setting a new benchmark for automated test transfer.

title: Bavisitter: Integrating Design Guidelines into Large Language Models for Visualization Authoring
proposal_tldr: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable versatility in visualization authoring, but often generate suboptimal designs that are invalid or fail to adhere to design guidelines for effective visualization. We present Bavisitter, a natural language interface that integrates established

title: ActionEngine: From Reactive to Programmatic GUI Agents via State Machine Memory
proposal_tldr: ActionEngine is proposed, a training-free framework that transitions from reactive execution to programmatic planning through a novel two-agent architecture: a Crawling Agent that constructs an updatable state-machine memory of the GUIs through offline exploration, and an Execution Agent that leverages this memory to synthesize complete, executable Python programs for online task execution.

title: Beyond Believability: Accurate Human Behavior Simulation with Fine-Tuned LLMs
proposal_tldr: This work presents the first comprehensive quantitative evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., DeepSeek-R1, Llama, and Claude) on the task of web action generation, and shows that fine-tuning LLMs on real-world behavioral data substantially improves their ability to generate actions compared to prompt-only meth-ods.

title: Mobile-Agent-V: Learning Mobile Device Operation Through Video-Guided Multi-Agent Collaboration
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Mobile-Agent-V, a framework that leverages video guidance to provide rich and cost-effective operational knowledge for mobile automation, and enhances task execution capabilities by leveraging video inputs without requiring specialized sampling or pre-processing.

title: RealSafe: Quantifying Safety Risks of Language Agents in Real-World
proposal_tldr: Re-alSafe offers an empirical time frame for researchers and developers to better understand the security problems LLM agents might face in real deployment and offers specific directions and ideas for building safer and smarter LLM agents down the road.

title: Creative Planning with Language Models: Practice, Evaluation and Applications
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Annual Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 5: Tutorial Abstracts)

title: WinSpot: GUI Grounding Benchmark with Multimodal Large Language Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a new framework that leverages LLMs to generate large-scale GUI grounding data, enabling automated and scalable labeling across diverse interfaces, and creates WinSpot—the first benchmark specifically designed for GUI grounding tasks in Windows environments.

title: Frontier AI Ethics: Anticipating and Evaluating the Societal Impacts of Generative Agents
proposal_tldr: The potential societal impacts and normative questions raised by the looming prospect of 'Generative Agents', in which multimodal large language models form the executive centre of complex, tool-using AI systems that can take unsupervised sequences of actions towards some goal are explored.

title: Do Agent Benchmarks Measure Capability? Protocol Validity in the Age of Agentic AI
proposal_tldr: Agent benchmarks increasingly evaluate repository editing, web research, terminal use, and long-horizon interaction. Their scores support capability claims only when the evaluation protocol keeps the intended capability necessary for success. Recent reward-hacking benchmarks and system reports show

title: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This analysis reveals that mastering low level atomic skills does not guarantee high level planning competence, while high level task training yields stronger OOD generalization, and proposes the task decomposition hierarchical analysis framework (TDHAF) to systematically study compositional generalization across three task granularities: low, middle and high levels.

title: Beyond Function Calling: Benchmarking Tool-Using Agents under Tool-Environment Unreliability
proposal_tldr: Results suggest that tool-use evaluation should move beyond function-call accuracy toward task completion under unreliable tool environments, and suggest that tool-use evaluation should move beyond function-call accuracy toward task completion under unreliable tool environments.

title: RetailBench: Benchmarking long horizon reasoning and coherent decision making of LLM agents in realistic retail environments
proposal_tldr: RetailBench is introduced, a data-grounded simulation benchmark for evaluating tool-using LLM agents in single-store supermarket operation and provides a controlled testbed for studying reliable autonomy in economically grounded long-horizon decision-making.

title: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a novel constraint-based evaluation framework that provides fine-grained assessment of progress towards task completion, which enables it to leverage partially successful trajectories, which significantly expands the amount of usable training data.

title: DeepImageSearch: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Context-Aware Image Retrieval in Visual Histories
proposal_tldr: DeepImageSearch is introduced, a novel agentic paradigm that reformulates image retrieval as an autonomous exploration task and proposes a human-model collaborative pipeline that employs vision-language models to mine latent spatiotemporal associations, effectively offloading intensive context discovery before human verification.

title: Self-Improving World Modelling with Latent Actions
proposal_tldr: SWIRL is a self-improvement framework that learns from state-only sequences by treating actions as a latent variable and alternating between Forward World Modelling and an Inverse Dynamics Modelling, trained with reinforcement learning with the opposite frozen model's log-probability as a reward signal.

title: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: WebArbiter is introduced, a reasoning-first, principle-inducing WebPRM that formulates reward modeling as text generation, producing structured justifications that conclude with a preference verdict and identify the action most conducive to task completion under the current context.

title: Paying Less Generalization Tax: A Cross-Domain Generalization Study of RL Training for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: It is shown that increasing state information richness alone can already effectively improve cross-domain robustness and proposed a randomization technique, which is low-overhead and broadly applicable: add small amounts of distractive goal-irrelevant features to the state to make it richer without altering the task.

title: EntWorld: A Holistic Environment and Benchmark for Verifiable Enterprise GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces EntWorld, a large-scale benchmark consisting of 1,756 tasks across six representative enterprise domains, including customer relationship management (CRM), information technology infrastructure library (ITIL), and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and proposes a SQL-based deterministic verification mechanism in building datasets that replaces ambiguous visual matching with rigorous state-transition validation.

title: ProSoftArena: Benchmarking Hierarchical Capabilities of Multimodal Agents in Professional Software Environments
proposal_tldr: ProSoftArena is introduced, a benchmark and platform specifically for evaluating multimodal agents in professional software environments and the first capability hierarchy tailored to agent use of professional software is established, to ensure reliable and reproducible assessment.

title: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Nested Browser-Use Learning (NestBrowse), which introduces a minimal and complete browser-action framework that decouples interaction control from page exploration through a nested structure, and simplifies agentic reasoning while enabling effective deep-web information acquisition.

title: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
proposal_tldr: The resulting critic model, OS-Oracle-7B, achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source VLMs on OS-Critic Bench, and surpasses proprietary models on the mobile domain.

title: Atomic Skills are the Prerequisite: When Reinforcement Learning Synthesizes Compositional Reasoning, and When It Only Amplifies
proposal_tldr: It is suggested that decoupled atomic training followed by RL offers a scalable path to complex novel reasoning, and RL bridges this generalization gap, acting as a skill synthesizer rather than a mere amplifier.

title: MCP vs RAG vs NLWeb vs HTML: A Comparison of the Effectiveness and Efficiency of Different Agent Interfaces to the Web
proposal_tldr: This work develops specialized agents that perform the same sets of tasks, ranging from simple product searches and price comparisons to complex queries for complementary or substitute products and checkout processes, and evaluates the agents using GPT-5 and GPT-5-mini.

title: Genesis: Evolving Attack Strategies for LLM Web Agent Red-Teaming
proposal_tldr: Genesis is a novel agentic framework composed of three modules: Attacker, Scorer, and Strategist that dynamically uncovers effective strategies from interaction logs and compiles them into a continuously growing strategy library, which is then re-deployed to enhance the Attacker's effectiveness.

title: WebAggregator: Enhancing Compositional Reasoning Capabilities of Deep Research Agent Foundation Models
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The WebAggregatorQA testbed is introduced, which reveals that even with perfect retrieval, top-tier models still underperformed, demonstrating that compositional reasoning, not retrieval, is the true performance ceiling for next-generation research agents.

title: Interaction-Driven Browsing: A Human-in-the-Loop Conceptual Framework Informed by Human Web Browsing for Browser-Using Agents
proposal_tldr: A human-in-the-loop (HITL) conceptual framework informed by theories of human web browsing behavior that aims to reduce users' physical and cognitive effort while preserving users' traditional browsing mental model and supporting users in achieving satisfactory outcomes.

title: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
proposal_tldr: A realistic dynamic-environment threat model in which the attacker is a regular user and the trigger is embedded within a dynamically changing environment, and Chameleon, an attack framework with two key components designed for dynamic environments is proposed.

title: LLM-Based Agents for Competitive Landscape Mapping in Drug Asset Due Diligence
proposal_tldr: This paper describes and benchmark a competitor-discovery component used within an agentic AI system for fast drug asset due diligence and introduces a competitor validating LLM-as-a-judge agent that filters out false positives from the list of predicted competitors to maximize precision and suppress hallucinations.

title: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: The first evaluation and diagnostic standard for fine-grained GUI proxy operations, designed to quantify fine-grained control, is introduced and the plug-and-play Visual Diagnostic Assistant (VDA) is developed, enabling the first quantitative decoupling analysis of these capabilities.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Large Model: A Survey
proposal_tldr: A coherent map of the rapidly expanding landscape of visual RL is provided to provide researchers and practitioners with a coherent map of the rapidly expanding landscape of visual RL and to highlight promising directions for future inquiry.

title: Flex-Judge: Text-Only Reasoning Unleashes Zero-Shot Multimodal Evaluators
proposal_tldr: Flex-Judge is proposed, a reasoning-guided multimodal judge model that leverages minimal textual reasoning data to robustly generalize across multiple modalities and evaluation formats, and highlights reasoning-based text supervision as a powerful, cost-effective alternative to traditional annotation-intensive approaches, substantially advancing scalable multimodal model-as-a-judge.

title: WebLists: Extracting Structured Information From Complex Interactive Websites Using Executable LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: BardeenAgent is proposed, a novel framework that enables web agents to convert their execution into repeatable programs, and replay them at scale across pages with similar structure, and is also the first LLM agent to take advantage of the regular structure of HTML.

title: Automating XPath Query Generation Using NLP for Streamlined Web Crawling and GUI Testing
venue: 2025 2nd International Conference on Trends in Engineering Systems and Technologies (ICTEST)
proposal_tldr: Efficient web data extraction and automated testing often require precise XPath queries, but generating these queries manually is both time-consuming and prone to errors. This work presents an advanced approach to automate the creation of XPath queries by leveraging natural language processing (NLP)

title: DisMouse: Disentangling Information from Mouse Movement Data
venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
proposal_tldr: This work proposes DisMouse – the first method to disentangle user-specific and user-independent information and stochastic variations from mouse movement data, and shows that it captures complementary information of mouse input, hence providing an interpretable framework for modelling mouse movements.

title: Decoding Susceptibility: Modeling Misbelief to Misinformation Through a Computational Approach
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a computational approach to efficiently model users’ latent susceptibility levels and reveals that political leanings and other psychological factors exhibit varying degrees of association with susceptibility to COVID-19 misinformation, and shows that susceptibility is unevenly distributed across different professional and geographical backgrounds.

title: The Klarna Product Page Dataset: Web Element Nomination with Graph Neural Networks and Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This work empirically benchmark a range of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) on the web element nomination task and finds that a simple Convolutional GNN (GCN) outperforms complex state-of-the-art nomination methods.

title: From Tasks to Teams: A Risk-First Evaluation Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Systems in Finance
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: By turning safety into a measurable, model-agnostic quantity, M-SAEA shifts the evaluation focus from tasks to teams and provides a ready-to-use template for risk-first assessment of agentic AI in finance and beyond.

title: Bayesian-Agent: Posterior-Guided Skill Evolution for LLM Agent Harnesses
proposal_tldr: Bayesian-Agent is introduced, a native and cross-harness framework that treats reusable skills and SOPs as hypotheses about whether a frozen model will succeed under a particular prompt, context, and harness environment and its native backend and optional GenericAgent, mini-swe-agent, and Claude Code backends are evaluated.

title: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Model in GUI World
proposal_tldr: For vision-based agent tasks, the decoder parameters are unfrozen, while the image encoder remains frozen, and the training objective hyperparameters are λ text = 1 and L grd = 1 .

title: VeriGUI: Verifiable Long-Chain GUI Dataset
An Evaluation Mechanism of LLM-based Agents on Manipulating APIs
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
proposal_tldr: VISTA, a visual harness that gives a general-purpose multimodal model long-horizon vision, is introduced, a visual harness that allows the model to directly perceive the environment through visual observations and maintains a lossless visual memory that preserves past observations in their original form.

title: From Faulty Memories to Corrected Actions: Dependency-Guided Rollback Repair for Memory-Augmented Agents
proposal_tldr: The results do not imply uniformly better trace reconstruction, but show that dependency-guided rollback repair provides a strong recovery--cost trade-off while repairing faulty memory state and preserving benign memory.

title: SkillTracer: Structural Failure Attribution and Refinement of Agentic Skills in Long-Horizon Web Tasks
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: SkillTracer is introduced, a framework that represents skills as attributed plan graphs structured by hierarchical nodes and verifiable edge transitions, enabling programmatic verification of execution progress and demonstrating that structural attribution and skill repair are critical for reliable long-horizon web interaction.

title: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work employs an LLM to diagnose failure modes, propose inference-time solutions, and generate code patches -- lightly verified by humans -- that upgrade the agent, demonstrating that failure-driven self-improvement is a viable complement to success-based pipelines, enabling more efficient agent improvement.

title: Fara-1.5: Scalable Learning Environments for Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces FaraGen1.5, a scalable data pipeline for computer use agents composed of three modular components: environments, solvers, and verifiers, and trains Fara1.5, a family of native computer use agents at three scales built on Qwen3.5.

title: MobileForge: Annotation-Free Adaptation for Mobile GUI Agents with Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization
proposal_tldr: MobileForge is presented, an annotation-free adaptation system for mobile GUI agents that consists of MobileGym, which grounds task generation and rollout evaluation in real mobile app interaction, and Hierarchical Feedback-Guided Policy Optimization (HiFPO), which turns trajectory outcomes, step-level process feedback, and corrective hints into hint-contextualized step-level GRPO updates.

title: PreAct: Computer-Using Agents that Get Faster on Repeated Tasks
proposal_tldr: PreAct, which lets such an agent get faster on tasks it has done before, and applies the same discipline when deciding what to keep: a freshly compiled program enters the store only if, re-run from a clean state, an independent evaluator confirms it solved the task-catching programs that replay to their last step yet leave the task undone.

title: FragFuse: Bypassing Access Control of Large Language Model Agents via Memory-Based Query Fragmentation and Fusion
proposal_tldr: FragFuse is proposed, the first attack that enables unprivileged users to bypass agent access control by exploiting this temporal channel introduced by long-term memory, and a surrogate-based optimization scheme is developed that tunes fusion instructions and marker designs, enabling automated attack generation without violating the attacker's threat-model assumptions.

title: CODA-BENCH: Can Code Agents Handle Data-Intensive Tasks?
proposal_tldr: CODA-BENCH, the first benchmark to jointly evaluate code and data intelligence in a data-intensive environment, is introduced, where agents must actively explore complex file hierarchies to identify relevant resources and generate code for data-driven analytical tasks.

title: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: The results suggest that skills and workflow memory can be useful in specific domains, but their apparent gains often vanish against a budget-matched actor, and that run-to-run variance materially affects outcomes and should be reported as a core evaluation criterion for online web agents.

title: PhoneHarness: Harnessing Phone-Use Agents through Mixed GUI, CLI, and Tool Actions
proposal_tldr: PhoneHarness is introduced, a mixed-action benchmark and execution harness for studying phone-use agents on verifiable mobile workflows and suggests that reliable phone automation depends on action-surface routing and verifiable execution, not only visual GUI control.

title: iOSWorld: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Phone Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces iOSWorld, the first interactive native iOS simulator benchmark built around a persistent user identity spanning 26 newly built iOS apps, and evaluates frontier and open-source computer-use models in both vision-only and privileged vision+XML settings.

title: OpenWebRL: Demystifying Online Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning for Visual Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces OpenWebRL, an open framework for training visual web agents with online multi-turn RL on real websites, and trains OpenWebRL-4B, which establishes a new open-source state of the art on challenging live-web benchmarks.

title: WorldCoder-Bench: Benchmarking Physically Grounded 3D World Synthesis
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WorldCoder-Bench, a benchmark for autonomous, physically grounded 3D world synthesis, and proposes StateProbe, an execution-based protocol that probes generated programs in a sandboxed browser and verifies hidden, mutation-hardened contracts over runtime states and transitions.

title: What Twelve LLM Agent Benchmark Papers Disclose About Themselves: A Pilot Audit and an Open Scoring Schema
proposal_tldr: This paper read twelve well-known LLM agent benchmark papers and recorded, dimension by dimension, what each paper actually says about how its evaluation was run, and designed a small audit schema and wrote a scoring codebook with the boundary cases the authors hit during pilot scoring.

title: Evolving-RL: End-to-End Optimization of Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Capability within Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Evolving-RL, an efficient algorithmic framework that jointly improves the experience extraction and utilization capabilities required for self-evolution, and inherently functions as an experience-augmented RL algorithm.

title: FineState-Bench: Benchmarking State-Conditioned Grounding for Fine-grained GUI State Setting
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A benchmark that evaluates whether an agent can correctly ground an instruction to the intended UI control and reach the exact target state, and a plug-and-play VDA that generates a Description and a bounding-box Localization Hint to diagnose visual grounding reason.

title: SnapGuard: Lightweight Prompt Injection Detection for Screenshot-Based Web Agents
proposal_tldr: SnapGuard is proposed, a lightweight yet accurate method that reformulates prompt injection detection as multimodal representation analysis over webpage screenshots that leverages two complementary signals: a visual stability indicator that identifies abnormally smooth gradient distributions induced by malicious content, and action-oriented textual signals recovered via contrast-polarity reversal.

title: Revisable by Design: A Theory of Streaming LLM Agent Execution
proposal_tldr: The Revision Absorber is presented, a reactive algorithm based on the Earliest-Conflict Rollback rule that is structurally optimal under mild assumptions and matches the quality of a brute-force full-restart baseline while wasting an order of magnitude fewer steps of already-completed work.

title: AutomationBench
proposal_tldr: AutomationBench is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on cross-application workflow orchestration via REST APIs, and provides a challenging, realistic measure of where current models stand relative to the agentic capabilities businesses actually need.

title: What Is Your AI Agent Buying? Evaluation, Biases, Model Dependence, & Emerging Implications of Agentic E-Commerce
proposal_tldr: ACES, a sandbox environment that pairs a platform-agnostic agent with a fully programmable mock marketplace to study how AI agents behave in e-commerce, reveals how AI agents behave in e-commerce, and surface concrete monitoring, seller strategy, platform design, and regulatory questions.

title: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
proposal_tldr: Experiments on Phone-Harm and public benchmarks against diverse baselines validate that CORA improves the safety--helpfulness--interruption Pareto frontier, offering a practical, statistically grounded safety paradigm for autonomous GUI execution.

title: InCoder-32B-Thinking: Industrial Code World Model for Thinking
proposal_tldr: This work proposes InCoder-32B-Thinking, trained on the data from the Error-driven Chain-of-Thought synthesis framework with an industrial code world model (ICWM) to generate reasoning traces, which achieves top-tier open-source results across all domains.

title: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
proposal_tldr: It is argued that a coding agent equipped only with a terminal and a filesystem can solve many enterprise tasks more effectively by interacting directly with platform APIs and suggested that simple, flexible programmatic interfaces combined with strong foundation models should be the backbone of enterprise automation.

title: Anticipatory Planning for Multimodal AI Agents
proposal_tldr: TraceR1 is introduced, a two-stage reinforcement learning framework that explicitly trains anticipatory reasoning by forecasting short-horizon trajectories before execution, and achieves substantial improvements in planning stability, execution robustness, and generalization over reactive and single-stage baselines.

title: IQuest-Coder-V1 Technical Report
proposal_tldr: The IQuest-Coder-V1 series is introduced, a new family of code large language models (LLMs) that captures the dynamic evolution of software logic through different phases of the pipeline, and achieves state-of-the-art performance among competitive models across critical dimensions of code intelligence.

title: Can RL Improve Generalization of LLM Agents? An Empirical Study
proposal_tldr: The results show that RFT generalizes well across task difficulty within an environment, but exhibits weaker transfer to unseen environments, which correlates with shifts in both semantic priors and observation/action interfaces.

title: Modeling Distinct Human Interaction in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces the task of modeling human intervention to support collaborative web task execution and trains language models to anticipate when users are likely to intervene based on their interaction styles, showing structured modeling of human intervention leads to more adaptive, collaborative agents.

title: SPILLage: Agentic Oversharing on the Web
proposal_tldr: This paper formalizes Natural Agentic Oversharing -- the unintentional disclosure of task-irrelevant user information through an agent trace of actions on the web and introduces SPILLage, a framework that characterizes oversharing along two dimensions: channel (content vs. behavior) and directness (explicit vs. implicit).

title: Self-Consolidation for Self-Evolving Agents
proposal_tldr: A novel self-evolving framework for LLM agents is proposed that introduces a complementary evolution mechanism that distills non-parametric textual experience into compact learnable parameters and enables the agent to internalize extensive historical experience directly into its latent space.

title: MobileBench-OL: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Mobile GUI Agents in Real-World Environment
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: The proposed MobileBench-OL is an online benchmark with 1080 tasks from 80 Chinese apps that measures task execution, complex reasoning, and noise robustness of agents by including 5 subsets, which set multiple evaluation dimensions, enabling stable and repeatable real-world benchmarking.

title: AMA: Adaptive Memory via Multi-Agent Collaboration
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Adaptive Memory via Multi-Agent Collaboration (AMA), a novel framework that leverages coordinated agents to manage memory across multiple granularities, significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines while reducing token consumption by approximately 80% compared to full-context methods.

title: Gaming the Judge: Unfaithful Chain-of-Thought Can Undermine Agent Evaluation
proposal_tldr: By systematically rewriting agent CoTs while holding actions and observations fixed, it is demonstrated that manipulated reasoning alone can inflate false positive rates of state-of-the-art VLM judges by up to 90% across 800 trajectories spanning diverse web tasks.

title: VLN-MME: Diagnosing MLLMs as Language-guided Visual Navigation agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A unified and extensible evaluation framework to probe MLLMs as zero-shot agents by bridging traditional navigation datasets into a standardized benchmark, named VLN-MME, which lays the groundwork for systematic evaluation of general-purpose MLLMs in embodied navigation settings and reveals limitations in their sequential decision-making capabilities.

title: Using GUI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
proposal_tldr: This work extends GUI agents from generic office automation to specialized, high-value engineering domains and offers a new avenue for advancing EDA productivity.

title: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: gui Exploration Lab is introduced, a simulation environment engine for GUI agent navigation research that enables flexible definition and composition of screens, icons, and navigation graphs, while providing full access to environment information for comprehensive agent training and evaluation.

title: UI-CUBE: Enterprise-Grade Computer Use Agent Benchmarking Beyond Task Accuracy to Operational Reliability
proposal_tldr: UI-CUBE (UiPath Computer Use BEnchmark) functions as an enterprise-readiness diagnostic, revealing that while current CUAs can manipulate individual interface elements, they cannot yet function as reliable workflow automation tools.

title: Web3Agent: Automating On-Chain Operations via Natural Language Interfaces
proposal_tldr: This article presents Web3Agent, an AI agent system that integrates LLM-based interaction with blockchain environments to enable language-driven on-chain operations and evaluates the system and performs ablation study with customized dataset in a simulated environment, demonstrating its feasibility in orchestrating complex Web3 tasks and highlighting implications for agent-based abstraction in decentralized systems.

title: Optimal-Agent-Selection: State-Aware Routing Framework for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes STRMAC, a state-aware routing framework designed for efficient collaboration in multi-agent systems, which separately encodes interaction history and agent knowledge to power the router, which adaptively selects the most suitable single agent at each step for efficient and effective collaboration.

title: SIRAJ: Diverse and Efficient Red-Teaming for LLM Agents via Distilled Structured Reasoning
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work presents SIRAJ: a generic red-teaming framework for arbitrary black-box LLM agents, using a dynamic two-step process that starts with an agent definition and generates diverse seed test cases that cover various risk outcomes, tool-use trajectories, and risk sources.

title: APTBench: Benchmarking Agentic Potential of Base LLMs During Pre-Training
proposal_tldr: APTBench is proposed, a framework that converts real-world agent tasks and successful trajectories into multiple-choice or text completion questions tailored for base models and offers a more predictive signal of a model's downstream performance as an agent while remaining significantly more lightweight and cost-effective than full-scale, end-to-end agent evaluations after post-training.

title: Branch-and-Browse: Efficient and Controllable Web Exploration with Tree-Structured Reasoning and Action Memory
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Branch-and-Browse is a fine-grained web agent framework that unifies structured reasoning-acting, contextual memory, and efficient execution and demonstrates that Branch-and-Browse is a reliable and efficient framework for LLM-based web agents.

title: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation
proposal_tldr: Just-in-time Episodic Feedback Hinter (JEF-Hinter), an agentic system that distills offline traces into compact, context-aware hints, and consistently outperforms strong baselines, including human- and document-based hints.

title: Recon-Act: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Browser-Use System via Web Reconnaissance, Tool Generation, and Task Execution
proposal_tldr: Recon-Act is introduced, a self-evolving multi-agent framework grounded in Reconnaissance-Action behavioral paradigm that substantially improves adaptability to unseen websites and solvability on long-horizon tasks, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the challenging VisualWebArena dataset.

title: OmniActor: A Generalist GUI and Embodied Agent for 2D&3D Worlds
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a high-performance generalist agent OmniActor, designed from both structural and data perspectives, and proposes Layer-heterogeneity MoE to eliminate the conflict between GUI and embodied data by separating deep-layer parameters, while leverage their synergy by sharing shallow-layer parameters.

title: Think, Act, Learn: A Framework for Autonomous Robotic Agents using Closed-Loop Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces the Think, Act, Learn (T-A-L) framework, a novel architecture that enables an embodied agent to autonomously learn and refine its policies through continuous interaction, and demonstrates through extensive experiments that this T-A-L agent significantly outperforms baseline methods, including open-loop LLMs, Behavioral Cloning, and traditional Reinforcement Learning.

title: Task Mode: Dynamic Filtering for Task-Specific Web Navigation using LLMs
venue: International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility
proposal_tldr: This work demonstrates how designing new interactions simultaneously for visual and non-visual access can reduce rather than reinforce accessibility disparities in future technology created by researchers and practitioners.

title: Mobile GUI Agents under Real-world Threats: Are We There Yet?
venue: ACM SIGMOBILE International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications, and Services
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a scalable app content instrumentation framework to enable flexible and targeted content modifications within existing applications and creates a test suite comprising both a dynamic task execution environment and a static dataset of challenging GUI states.

title: LineRetriever: Planning-Aware Observation Reduction for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces \textit{LineRetriever}, a novel approach that leverages a language model to identify and retrieve observation lines most relevant to future navigation steps, and explicitly considers the planning horizon, prioritizing elements that contribute to action prediction.

title: Universal Retrieval for Multimodal Trajectory Modeling
proposal_tldr: Comprehensive evaluations across multiple datasets show that GAE-Retriever consistently outperforms strong baselines in retrieval recall, highlighting its effectiveness in advancing multimodal trajectory retrieval.

title: Leveraging In-Context Learning for Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: An algorithm that leverages an LLM with retries along with demonstrations to automatically and efficiently annotate agentic tasks with solution trajectories is proposed and it is shown that set-selection of trajectories of similar tasks as demonstrations significantly improves performance, reliability, robustness, and efficiency of LLM agents.

title: Designing Algorithmic Delegates: the Role of Indistinguishability in Human-AI Handoff
venue: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation
proposal_tldr: This paper defines the problem of designing the optimal algorithmic delegate in the presence of categories, and discovers that this problem is fundamentally combinatorial, and illustrates the complex relationship between the optimal design and the properties of the decision-making task even in simple settings.

title: A Red Teaming Roadmap Towards System-Level Safety
proposal_tldr: This work contends that system-level safety is a necessary step to move red teaming research forward, as AI models present new threats as well as affordances for threat mitigation once placed in a deployment context.

title: FieldWorkArena: Agentic AI Benchmark for Real Field Work Tasks
proposal_tldr: Evaluation results confirmed that performance evaluation considering the characteristics of Multimodal LLM (MLLM) such as GPT-4o is feasible and identified both the effectiveness and limitations of the proposed new evaluation methodology.

title: VisEscape: A Benchmark for Evaluating Exploration-driven Decision-making in Virtual Escape Rooms
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: It is found that integrating memory management and reasoning contributes to efficient exploration and enables successive hypothesis formulation and testing, thereby leading to significant improvements in dynamic and exploration-driven environments.

title: WebNav: An Intelligent Agent for Voice-Controlled Web Navigation
proposal_tldr: This work presents the complete architecture and implementation of WebNav, a novel agent for multi-modal web navigation that leverages a dual Large Language Model (LLM) architecture to translate natural language commands into precise, executable actions on a graphical user interface.

title: DeskVision: Large Scale Desktop Region Captioning for Advanced GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an automated GUI data generation pipeline, AutoCaptioner, which generates data with rich descriptions while minimizing human effort, and creates a novel large-scale desktop GUI dataset, DeskVision, along with the largest desktop test benchmark, DeskVision-Eval.

title: Haste Makes Waste: Evaluating Planning Abilities of LLMs for Efficient and Feasible Multitasking with Time Constraints Between Actions
proposal_tldr: Recipe2Plan is presented, a novel benchmark framework based on real-world cooking scenarios that challenges agents to optimize cooking time through parallel task execution while respecting temporal constraints i.e. specific actions need to be performed within a particular time intervals following the preceding steps.

title: Mobile-Agent-V: A Video-Guided Approach for Effortless and Efficient Operational Knowledge Injection in Mobile Automation
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Mobile-Agent-V, an innovative framework that utilizes video as a guiding tool to effortlessly and efficiently inject operational knowledge into mobile automation processes, significantly reducing the effort and time required for knowledge acquisition.

title: EDGE: Efficient Data Selection for LLM Agents via Guideline Effectiveness
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: This work proposes the Guideline Effectiveness (GE) metric, which selects challenging samples by measuring the impact of human-provided guidelines in multi-turn interaction tasks, and provides a fresh perspective on the data quality of LLM-agent fine-tuning.

title: Towards Action Hijacking of Large Language Model-based Agent
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces AI, a novel attack to manipulate the action plans of LLM-based applications by leveraging the knowledge from the application's database to facilitate the construction of malicious but semantically-harmless prompts.

title: Generative Prompt Internalization
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Generative Prompt Internalization (GenPI), a lightweight method that employs a joint training approach that internalizes complex prompts and introduces a data synthesis technique that autonomously collects conversational datasets by swapping the roles of the agent and environment.

title: AssistEditor: Multi-Agent Collaboration for GUI Workflow Automation in Video Creation
proposal_tldr: A novel PC-Copilot, AssistEditor, that focuses on automating the video editing workflow, and significantly streamlines the video editing process, making advanced editing accessible to users with varying levels of expertise.

title: Thread: A Logic-Based Data Organization Paradigm for How-To Question Answering with Retrieval Augmented Generation
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Thread, a novel data organization paradigm enabling systems to handle how-to questions more effectively, and introduces a new knowledge granularity,'logic unit'(LU), where large language models transform documents into more structured and loosely interconnected LUs.

title: KAOS: Large Model Multi-Agent Operating System
proposal_tldr: KAOS, a multi-agent operating system based on the open-source Kylin, is proposed, providing a new perspective for the development of multi-agent operating systems.

title: Grounded Language Agent for Product Search via Intelligent Web Interactions
proposal_tldr: Interestingly, behavioral cloning-based methods that straightforwardly use human demonstrations do not outperform unsupervised variants of GLAINTEL and it is shown that combining human demonstrations with reinforcement learning-based training yields results comparable to methods utilizing GPT-4.

title: Frontier AI Ethics: Anticipating and Evaluating the Societal Impacts of Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: The potential societal impacts and normative questions raised by the looming prospect of 'Language Model Agents', in which multimodal large language models form the executive centre of complex, tool-using AI systems that can take unsupervised sequences of actions towards some goal are explored.

title: AgentGroupChat: An Interactive Group Chat Simulacra For Better Eliciting Emergent Behavior
proposal_tldr: AgentGroupChat is introduced, a simulation that delves into the complex role of language in shaping collective behavior through interactive debate scenarios, and introduces the Verbal Strategist Agent, utilizing large language models to enhance interaction strategies by incorporating elements of persona and action.

title: ColorBrowserAgent: An Intelligent GUI Agent for Complex Long-Horizon Web Automation
proposal_tldr: Col-orBrowserAgent is introduced, a framework designed for Collaborative Autonomy in complex web tasks that integrates two human-centred mechanisms and allows the agent to learn from human tips without extensive retraining, effectively combining the scalability of AI with the adaptability of human cognition.

title: OS-Marathon: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents on Long-Horizon Repetitive Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work establishes OS-Marathon, comprising 242 long-horizon, repetitive tasks across 2 domains to evaluate state-of-the-art (SOTA) agents, and introduces a cost-effective method to construct a condensed demonstration using only few-shot examples to teach agents the underlying workflow logic, enabling them to execute similar workflows effectively on larger, unseen data collections.

title: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
Grounded Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Agents
Transcending Cost-Quality Tradeoff in Agent Serving via Session-Awareness
proposal_tldr: This work introduces A G S ERVE for AG ent SERVing, a model serving system that allows agents to select and upgrade models during the session lifetime, and to achieve similar quality at much lower costs, effectively transcending the tradeoff.

title: Information Retrieval Induced Safety Degradation in AI Agents
proposal_tldr: Investigating how expanding retrieval access affects model reliability, bias propagation, and harmful content generation reveals a consistent degradation in refusal rates, bias sensitivity, and harmfulness safeguards as models gain broader access to external sources, culminating in a phenomenon the authors term safety degradation.

title: Fine-Tuning Web Agents: It Works, But It’s Trickier Than You Think
proposal_tldr: It is found that the fine-tuned agents’ ability to predict expert trajectories does not consistently lead to improved downstream task performance, which raises issues such as off-policy bias and the loss of reasoning abilities during fine-tuning.

title: Position: Agent-Specific Trustworthiness Risk as a Research Priority
proposal_tldr: This position paper comprehensively analyzes trustworthiness risks specific to LLM-based agents, emphasizing threats arising from agent-specific modules going beyond stan-dalone LLMs and advocates for more research efforts to bridge this gap.

title: ComBodied Agents: a New Paradigm of Human-Centric Agentic AI
proposal_tldr: Combodied Agents is introduced, a human-centered paradigm that perceives, models, predicts, and supports individual human-state trajectories over time, using software tools, sensors, wearables, robots, and human services as action channels rather than end goals.

title: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
proposal_tldr: Qwen-CUA is introduced, a native computer-use agent with a 397B-A17B Qwen mixture-of-experts backbone that outperforms Qwen3.7 and remains competitive with leading proprietary systems, and scalable verifiable interaction and hybrid tool use as key directions.

title: Is Deep Research Reliable? Misleading Knowledge Induces False Conclusions
proposal_tldr: MisKnow-Agent is introduced, a controlled evaluation framework that constructs task-specific documents supporting manually audited false conclusions with controlled authority cues and source styles that evaluates DeerFlow and WebThinker with three backbone LLMs using a report-level false-conclusion adoption rate that counts only reports endorsing the false conclusion.

title: FinResearchBench II: A Deep Research Benchmark with Consensus-Derived Gold Rubrics for Distinguishing Financial Report Quality
proposal_tldr: A scalable pipeline for generating high-quality rubrics without human experts in the final loop is proposed, which is naturally scalable for benchmark evaluation, automatic system comparison, and future studies of evaluation-driven system improvement.

title: StructAgent: Harness Long-horizon Digital Agents with Unified Causal Structure
proposal_tldr: This paper presents StructAgent, a state-centered framework that introduces a unified state for maintaining compact, verifiable task progress and a structured workflow that regulates progress through verifier-backed state transitions and generalizes beyond desktop environments to Minecraft, demonstrating the generality of the design.

title: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: TUA-Bench aims to accelerate the transition from narrow, task-specific assistants to general-purpose agents capable of operating reliably across diverse digital environments by providing a broad and realistic evaluation of terminal-use capabilities.

title: PhoneBuddy: Training Open Models for Agentic Phone Use
proposal_tldr: Results show that mock-app training is not a replacement for real-app RL, but a complementary source of scalable, resettable, and automatically checked interaction, and gains are strongest on app and mini-app tasks, while long-horizontal cross-app workflows remain an important open challenge.

title: When AUC 0.998 Is Not Enough: A Candidate Evaluation Protocol for Hidden-State Probes of Indirect Prompt Injection in Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: It is argued, on a single-backbone cautionary case study (Qwen2.5-VL-7B on Mind2Web, teacher-forced replay), that a high probing AUC on a clean-vs-attack split is not, on its own, evidence of malicious-content detection.

title: GUI vs. CLI: Execution Bottlenecks in Screen-Only and Skill-Mediated Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: The results suggest that GUI and CLI expose different execution bottlenecks: GUI agents are limited by reliable grounded interaction over long-horizon workflows, whereas CLI agents are limited by the coverage and scalability of their skill interfaces.

title: EComAgentBench: Benchmarking Shopping Agents on Long-Horizon Tasks with Distributed Hidden Intent
proposal_tldr: EComAgentBench is introduced, a benchmark of 662 tasks grounded in real Amazon products and reviews that will serve as a reproducible foundation for moving shopping agents from single-query search toward dependable assistance over long horizons.

title: MyPCBench: A Benchmark for Personally Intelligent Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MyPCBench, which tests computer-use agents as personal assistants on a Linux desktop populated with 17 simulated real-world web applications and a full desktop stack, all seeded for one canonical persona, Michael Scott from The Office.

title: What makes a harness a harness: necessary and sufficient conditions for an agent harness
proposal_tldr: An operational definition of agent harness is proposed, with a shared vocabulary, able to guide engineering practice and the scientific comparison of agentic systems.

title: SentinelBench: A Benchmark for Long-Running Monitoring Agents
proposal_tldr: SentinelBench is introduced, an open-source benchmark for time-evolving monitoring tasks, and results show that SentinelBench distinguishes meaningful differences in agent behavior, demonstrating how agent design choices can dramatically impact key metrics.

title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
proposal_tldr: Within-network analyses show that high-betweenness bridges suffer a brokerage penalty while agents in locally clustered neighborhoods achieve higher coordination success, and it is found that agents' choices are well captured by Fictitious Play, indicating belief-based rather than reward-based adaptation.

title: LiveBrowseComp: Are Search Agents Searching, or Just Verifying What They Already Know?
proposal_tldr: Analysis of LLM-based search agents on BrowseComp reveals Intrinsic Knowledge Dependence (IKD), and introduces LiveBrowseComp, a deep-search benchmark designed to evaluate agents beyond intrinsic coverage.

title: Learning to Act under Noise: Enhancing Agent Robustness via Noisy Environments
proposal_tldr: NoisyAgent is proposed, an agentic training framework that explicitly incorporates environmental imperfections into the agent learning process, and reveals that training under noise conditions also yields performance gains on idealized benchmarks, suggesting that controlled exposure to environmental noise promotes more generalizable reasoning and decision-making behaviors.

title: IdleSpec: Exploiting Idle Time via Speculative Planning for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces IdleSpec, a scalable and generic inference approach that leverages idle-time computation to improve agent performance while minimizing latency overhead and significantly improves agent performance in various agentic scenarios by effectively utilizing idle time.

title: PPAI: Enabling Personalized LLM Agent Interoperability for Collaborative Edge Intelligence
proposal_tldr: PPAI, the first personalized LLM agent interoperability system, which enables users to collaborate with each other based on agent specialization is introduced and a scalable query-agent pair scoring mechanism based on prototypes to identify suitable agents within a P2P network with churn is proposed.

title: AtlasVA: Self-Evolving Visual Skill Memory for Teacher-Free VLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes AtlasVA, a teacher-free visual skill memory framework that organizes memory into three complementary layers: spatial heatmaps, visual exemplars, and symbolic text skills, and reuses these self-evolving atlases as potential-based shaping rewards for reinforcement learning.

title: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
proposal_tldr: ShopGym is an integrated framework for realistic simulation and scalable benchmarking of e-commerce web agents that produces self-contained, resettable, inspectable, and stable evaluation artifacts that preserve structural properties and agent-evaluation signals relevant to shopping tasks.

title: SaaS-Bench: Can Computer-Use Agents Leverage Real-World SaaS to Solve Professional Workflows?
proposal_tldr: SaaS-Bench is introduced, a benchmark built on 23 deployable SaaS systems across six professional domains, containing 106 tasks grounded in realistic work scenarios, showing that representative LLM-based agents struggle on SaaS-Bench, exposing limitations in planning, state tracking, cross-application context maintenance, and error recovery.

title: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Video2GUI, a fully automated framework that extracts grounded GUI interaction trajectories directly from unlabeled Internet videos and constructs WildGUI, a large-scale dataset containing 12 million interaction trajectories spanning over 1,500 applications and websites.

title: Web Agents Should Adopt the Plan-Then-Execute Paradigm
proposal_tldr: This work identifies the main barrier to adopting plan-then-execute on the web: For it to work well, tools must map cleanly to semantic actions, with effects known before execution, so agents have enough information to plan.

title: EcoGEO: Trajectory-Aware Evidence Ecosystems for Web-Enabled LLM Search Agents
proposal_tldr: The proposed TRACE, a Trajectory-Aware Coordinated Evidence Ecosystem, supports an ecosystem research paradigm for GEO, where web-enabled LLM agents are studied in relation to the broader evidence environments that guide search, browsing, and answer synthesis.

title: Can Agent Benchmarks Support Their Scores? Evidence-Supported Bounds for Interactive-Agent Evaluation
proposal_tldr: An outcome evidence reporting layer is introduced for existing benchmarks, without modifying their tasks, agents, or evaluators, and it is evaluated on five public benchmarks: ANDROIDWORLD, AGENTDOJO, APPWORLD, tau3 bench retail, and MINIWOB.

title: gwBenchmarks: Stress-Testing LLM Agents on High-Precision Gravitational Wave Astronomy
proposal_tldr: Modern gravitational wave astronomy relies on modeling tasks that often require months of graduate-level effort, including building fast waveform surrogates from expensive numerical relativity simulations, modeling orbital dynamics of black holes, fitting merger remnant properties and constructing t

title: GUI Agents with Reinforcement Learning: Toward Digital Inhabitants
proposal_tldr: This work presents the first comprehensive overview of the intersection between RL and GUI agents, and proposes a principled taxonomy that organizes existing methods into Offline RL, Online RL, and Hybrid Strategies, and complement it with analyses of reward engineering, data efficiency, and key technical innovations.

title: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
proposal_tldr: WebForge is presented, the first fully automated framework that resolves this trilemma through a four-agent pipeline -- Plan, Generate, Refine, and Validate -- that produces interactive, self-contained web environments end-to-end without human annotation.

title: OccuBench: Evaluating AI Agents on Real-World Professional Tasks via Language Environment Simulation
proposal_tldr: OccuBench provides the first systematic cross-industry evaluation of AI agents on professional occupational tasks, enabled by Language Environment Simulators (LESs) that simulate domain-specific environments through LLM-driven tool response generation.

title: FileGram: Grounding Agent Personalization in File-System Behavioral Traces
proposal_tldr: Extensive experiments show that FileGramBench remains challenging for state-of-the-art memory systems and that FileGramEngine and FileGramOS are effective, and by open-sourcing the framework, it hopes to support future research on personalized memory-centric file-system agents.

title: Read More, Think More: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: It is demonstrated that the optimal observation representation depends on model capability and thinking token budget, and it is found that incorporating observation history improves performance across most models and settings, and a diff-based representation offers a token-efficient alternative.

title: Agentic Tool Use in Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: The literature is organized into three paradigms: prompting as plug-and-play, supervised tool learning and reward-driven tool policy learning, analyzes their methods, strengths and failure modes, and reviews the evaluation landscape and highlights key challenges.

title: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
proposal_tldr: Emergence WebVoyager is introduced, an enhanced version of the WebVoyager benchmark that standardizes evaluation methodology through clear guidelines for task instantiation, failure handling, annotation, and reporting, demonstrating the utility of the approach for more rigorous and comparable web agent evaluation.

title: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: This work adapts LLaDA-V for single-turn action and bounding-box prediction and proposes a hybrid masking schedule that combines linear and deterministic masking, improving grounding accuracy and representing an important step toward diffusion-based GUI agents.

title: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Ego2Web, the first benchmark designed to bridge egocentric video perception and web agent execution, and develops a novel LLM-as-a-Judge automatic evaluation method, Ego2WebJudge, which achieves approximately 84% agreement with human judgment, substantially higher than existing evaluation methods.

title: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
proposal_tldr: ZoomUI is proposed that leverages inference scaling to guide common MLLMs in progressively anchor instruction elements to increasingly detailed interface elements and first optimizes the latent thinking to transform original instruction into element visual features description, and subsequently leverages internal attention to iteratively zoom in target element interface region.

title: AI Planning Framework for LLM-Based Web Agents
proposal_tldr: A taxonomy that maps modern agent architectures to traditional planning paradigms: Step-by-Step agents to Breadth-First Search (BFS), Tree Search agents to Best-First Tree Search, and Full-Plan-in-Advance agents to Depth-First Search (DFS) is introduced.

title: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
proposal_tldr: Experimental results on Mind2Web and WebArena show that HMT significantly outperforms flat-memory methods, particularly in cross-website and cross-domain scenarios, highlighting the necessity of structured memory for robust generalization of web agents.

title: WebChain: A Large-Scale Human-Annotated Dataset of Real-World Web Interaction Traces
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebChain, the largest open-source dataset of human-annotated trajectories on real-world websites, and proposes a Dual Mid-Training recipe that decouples spatial grounding from planning, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the proposed WebChainBench and other public GUI benchmarks.

title: Egocentric Co-Pilot: Web-Native Smart-Glasses Agents for Assistive Egocentric AI
proposal_tldr: Egocentric Co-Pilot is presented, a web-native neuro-symbolic framework that runs on smart glasses and uses a Large Language Model (LLM) to orchestrate a toolbox of perception, reasoning, and web tools that support education, accessibility, and social inclusion for people who may benefit most from contextual, egocentric AI.

title: World-Model-Augmented Web Agents with Action Correction
proposal_tldr: WAC, a web agent that integrates model collaboration, consequence simulation, and feedback-driven action refinement, is proposed, and introduces a two-stage deduction chain to achieve risk-aware resilient task execution.

title: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
proposal_tldr: ScreenParse is introduced, a large-scale dataset for complete screen parsing, with dense annotations of all visible UI elements across 771K web screenshots, and ScreenVLM, a compact, 316M-parameter vision language model (VLM) that decodes a compact ScreenTag markup representation with a structure-aware loss that upweights structure-critical tokens is trained.

title: A11y-CUA Dataset: Characterizing the Accessibility Gap in Computer Use Agents
venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
proposal_tldr: This work presents A11y-CUA, a dataset of BLVUs and SUs performing 60 everyday tasks with 40.4 hours and 158,325 events and reveals that collected interaction traces quantitatively confirm distinct interaction styles between SU and BLVU groups and demonstrate interaction diversity within each group.

title: ANCHOR: Branch-Point Data Generation for GUI Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A trajectory expansion framework Anchor is presented that bootstraps scalable desktop supervision from a small set of verified seed demonstrations, and models fine-tuned on the expanded corpus achieve consistent improvements over zero-shot agents and representative synthesis baselines, and generalize across applications and operating systems.

title: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
proposal_tldr: Avenir-Web is introduced, a web agent that achieves a new open-source state of the art on the Online-Mind2Web benchmark in real-world deployment and establishes a new open-source state of the art for reliable web agents on live websites.

title: What Do Agents Learn from Trajectory-SFT: Semantics or Interfaces?
proposal_tldr: PIPE is proposed, a protocol-level evaluation augmentation for diagnosing interface reliance by minimally rewriting environment interfaces while preserving task semantics and execution behavior and introduces Interface Reliance (IR), a counterbalanced alias-based metric that quantifies preference for training-time interfaces.

title: SimGym: Traffic-Grounded Browser Agents for Offline A/B Testing in E-Commerce
proposal_tldr: SimGym is introduced, a scalable system for rapid offline A/B testing using traffic-grounded synthetic buyers powered by Large Language Model agents operating in a live browser and validated against real human outcomes from real UI changes on a major e-commerce platform under confounder control.

title: How do Visual Attributes Influence Web Agents? A Comprehensive Evaluation of User Interface Design Factors
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: VAF is introduced, a controlled evaluation pipeline for quantifying how webpage Visual Attribute Factors influence web-agent decision-making by quantitatively measuring the decision-making difference between the original and variant.

title: The Behavioral Fabric of LLM-Powered GUI Agents: Human Values and Interaction Outcomes
venue: International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces
proposal_tldr: This work built a controlled testbed of 14 common interactive web tasks, spanning shopping, travel, dining, and housing, each replicated from real websites and integrated with a low-fidelity LLM-based recommender system and showed that preference and value-infused prompts consistently guided agents toward outcomes that reflected these preferences and values.

title: Can Deep Research Agents Retrieve and Organize? Evaluating the Synthesis Gap with Expert Taxonomies
proposal_tldr: The results identify retrieval and hierarchical organization as separate bottlenecks and show why hierarchy metrics must be calibrated before they are used to compare models.

title: ShowUI-π: Flow-based Generative Models as GUI Dexterous Hands
proposal_tldr: ShowUI-$\pi$ is developed, the first flow-based generative model as GUI dexterous hand, featuring the following designs: Unified Discrete-Continuous Actions, integrating discrete clicks and continuous drags within a shared model, enabling flexible adaptation across diverse interaction modes.

title: QuadSentinel: Sequent Safety for Machine-Checkable Control in Multi-agent Systems
proposal_tldr: A four-agent guard that compiles policies into machine-checkable rules built from predicates over observable state and enforces them online, which improves guardrail accuracy and rule recall while reducing false positives.

title: Mistake Notebook Learning: Batch-Clustered Failures for Training-Free Agent Adaptation
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
