proposal_tldr: This work proposes Mistake Notebook Learning (MNL), a novel memory framework that enables agents to self-curate generalizable guidance from batch-clustered failures, enabling continuous improvement without the cost of parameter updates.

title: AgentCrypt: Advancing Privacy and (Secure) Computation in AI Agent Collaboration
proposal_tldr: AgentCrypt is introduced, a three-tiered framework for secure agent communication that adds a deterministic protection layer atop any AI platform, and a benchmark dataset simulating privacy-critical tasks to enable systematic evaluation and foster the development of trustworthy, regulatable machine learning systems.

title: AUTO-Explorer: Automated Data Collection for GUI Agent
proposal_tldr: The proposed Auto-Explorer incorporates a simple yet effective exploration mechanism that autonomously parses and explores GUI environments, gathering data efficiently and fine-tune a multimodal large language model (MLLM) to enhance the capabilities of an MLLM in explored software.

title: Beyond Clicking:A Step Towards Generalist GUI Grounding via Text Dragging
proposal_tldr: This work introduces GUI-Drag, a diverse dataset of 161K text dragging examples synthesized through a scalable pipeline, and constructs ScreenDrag, a benchmark with 5,333 examples spanning three levels of interface context, together with three dedicated metrics designed for assessing text dragging capability.

title: GUI-Rise: Structured Reasoning and History Summarization for GUI Navigation
proposal_tldr: This framework employs specialized rewards, including a history-aware objective, directly linking summary quality to subsequent action performance, which validate the framework's ability to maintain robust reasoning and generalization across diverse GUI navigation tasks.

title: Empowering Real-World: A Survey on the Technology, Practice, and Evaluation of LLM-driven Industry Agents
proposal_tldr: This review systematically reviews the technologies, applications, and evaluation methods of industry agents based on large language models to clarify the current state and offer a clear roadmap and theoretical foundation for understanding and building the next generation of industry agents.

title: AgentChangeBench: A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework for Goal-Shift Robustness in Conversational AI
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentChangeBench, a benchmark explicitly designed to measure how tool augmented language model agents adapt to mid dialogue goal shifts across three enterprise domains, and establishes a reproducible testbed for diagnosing and improving agent resilience in realistic enterprise settings.

title: AutoQual: An LLM Agent for Automated Discovery of Interpretable Features for Review Quality Assessment
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: AutoQual is designed as a general framework for transforming tacit knowledge embedded in data into explicit, computable features, which mimics a human research process, iteratively generating feature hypotheses through reflection, operationalizing them via autonomous tool implementation, and accumulating experience in a persistent memory.

title: Improving GUI Grounding with Explicit Position-to-Coordinate Mapping
proposal_tldr: RULER tokens serve as explicit coordinate markers, letting the model reference positions similar to gridlines on a map and adjust rather than generate coordinates from scratch, which enables more reliable GUI automation across diverse resolutions and platforms.

title: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
proposal_tldr: D2Snap, an algorithm to downsample the DOM, premised on preserving actionability and actionability-discriminating features, is proposed and evaluated using a snapshot-variant web agent (GPT-4o) on a dataset sampled from Online-Mind2Web.

title: Galaxy: A Cognition-Centered Framework for Proactive, Privacy-Preserving, and Self-Evolving LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Cognition Forest, a semantic structure designed to align cognitive modeling with system-level design and unify cognitive architecture and system design into a self-reinforcing loop instead of treating them separately.

title: Turbocharging Web Automation: The Impact of Compressed History States
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a novel web history compressor approach to turbocharge web automation using history states by employing a history compressor module that distills the most task-relevant information from each history state into a fixed-length short representation, mitigating the challenges posed by the highly verbose history states.

title: OS-MAP: How Far Can Computer-Using Agents Go in Breadth and Depth?
proposal_tldr: OS-MAP is presented, a benchmark for daily computer-using automation that organizes its 416 realistic tasks across 15 applications along two key dimensions: a five-level taxonomy of automation and a generalization scope derived from a real-world user demand hierarchy.

title: LiteCUA: Computer as MCP Server for Computer-Use Agent on AIOS
proposal_tldr: The results suggest that contextualizing computer environments for language models represents a promising direction for developing more capable computer-use agents and advancing toward AI that can interact with digital systems.

title: LA-RCS: LLM-Agent-Based Robot Control System
proposal_tldr: This work categorized the scenarios that LA-RCS needs to perform into four distinct types and conducted a quantitative assessment of its performance in each scenario, demonstrating the system capability to fulfill user requests satisfactorily.

title: Empowering LLMs in Task-Oriented Dialogues: A Domain-Independent Multi-Agent Framework and Fine-Tuning Strategy
proposal_tldr: A Domain-Independent Multi-Agent Framework (DIMF), which contains Intent Classification Agent, Slot Filling Agent and Response Agent, and a simple and effective Data Distribution Adaptation (DDA) method to mitigate degradation issues during DPO training is designed.

title: Agentic AI Optimisation (AAIO): What It Is, How It Works, Why It Matters, and How to Deal with It
proposal_tldr: Agentic AI Optimisation (AAIO) is introduced as an essential methodology for ensuring effective integration between websites and agentic AI systems, and its essential role as part of a fundamental digital infrastructure in the era of autonomous digital agents is affirmed.

title: EscapeBench: Towards Advancing Creative Intelligence of Language Model Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: EscapeBench is introduced, a benchmark suite of room escape game environments designed to challenge agents with creative reasoning, unconventional tool use, and iterative problem-solving to uncover implicit goals in language model agents.

title: "When to Hand Off, When to Work Together": Expanding Human-Agent Co-Creative Collaboration through Concurrent Interaction
Steve-Evolving: Open-World Embodied Self-Evolution via Fine-Grained Diagnosis and Dual-Track Knowledge Distillation
proposal_tldr: Steve-Evolving is presented, a non-parametric self-evolving framework that tightly couples fine-grained execution diagnosis with dual-track knowledge distillation in a closed loop to solve long-horizon tasks where the main bottleneck is not single-step planning quality but how interaction experience is organized and evolved.

title: Towards Self-Evolving Agents: Enabling Autonomy through Interactive Experience Refinement
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: MUSE is a framework that enables iterative self-improvement through a hierarchical Memory Module that organizes cross-domain insights to facilitate the orchestration of long-horizon workflows and demonstrates that MUSE’s performance scales with the accumulation of insights and exhibits strong cross-task transferability.

title: Programming with Pixels: Computer-Use Meets Software Engineering
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Programming with Pixels ( PwP), an agent environment that unifies software development tasks by enabling computer-use agents —agents that operate directly within an IDE through visual perception, typing, and clicking, rather than relying on predefined tool APIs.

title: AGENTFUZZER: Generic Black-Box Fuzzing for Indirect Prompt Injection against LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a generic black-box fuzzing framework, A GENT F UZZER, designed to automatically discover and exploit indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse LLM agents, and exhibits strong transferability across unseen tasks and internal LLMs, as well as promising results against defenses.

title: Flex-Judge: Think Once, Judge Anywhere
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes F LEX -Judge, a reasoning-guided multimodal judge model that leverages minimal textual reasoning data to robustly generalize across multiple modalities and evaluation formats, and highlights reasoning-based text supervision as a powerful, cost-effective alternative to traditional annotation-intensive approaches.

title: Difficulty-Aware Agent Orchestration in LLM-Powered Workflows
proposal_tldr: Difficulty-Aware Agentic Orchestration is proposed, a dynamic framework that adapts workflow depth, operator selection, and LLM assignment based on the difficulty of each input query and outperforms prior multi-agent systems in both accuracy and inference efficiency across six benchmarks.

title: WhodunitBench: Evaluating Large Multimodal Agents via Murder Mystery Games
proposal_tldr: An LMA expected to perform practical tasks must possess a range of capabilities, including multimodal perception, interaction, reasoning, and decision-making skills, however, existing benchmarks are limited in assessing compositional skills and actions.

title: Efficient Morphology-Aware Policy Transfer to New Embodiments
Agentic-DPO: From Imitation to Agentic Policy Optimization on Expert Trajectories
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Agentic-DPO, a lightweight offline agent policy optimization method that turns expert trajectories into state-conditioned preference supervision, and introduces Policy-Preserving Augmentation (PPA), which renders the same latent trajectory under multiple schemas while keeping the expert policy fixed.

title: Capable but Careless: Do Computer-Use Agents Follow Contextual Integrity?
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentCIBench, an evaluation harness that turns privacy risk into executable, deterministically scored scenarios in CUAs and releases AgentCIBench to encourage the development of safer computer-use agents and position contextual disclosure testing as a pre-deployment safety check.

title: Who Pays the Price? Stakeholder-Centric Prompt Injection Benchmarking for Real-world Web Agents
proposal_tldr: StakeBench is introduced, a stakeholder-centric benchmark that systematically categorizes and attributes harm in real-world web agent systems for online shopping, and finds substantial and heterogeneous vulnerabilities in LLM-based web agents.

title: Self-Evolving Agents as Dynamic Graph Transformation: A Survey and New Perspective
proposal_tldr: This survey model agent state as a dynamic graph, where memories, tools, skills, workflows, and inter-agent relations are represented as typed nodes, edges, and subgraphs updated through schema-constrained rewrites to provide a compact structural lens for designing and governing self-evolving agents.

title: SKILL.nb: Selective Formalization and Gated Execution for Durable Agent Workflows
proposal_tldr: Results identify lifecycle governance and gate-conditioned execution as reliability axes beyond one-shot task success, especially in web automation.

title: FinEvolveBench: A Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents on Low-Repetition Tasks with Implicit Rewards
proposal_tldr: A scenario-oriented analysis of experience mechanisms for LLM agents is presented, and a reproducible benchmark built on a chronological stream of rich financial news and market data is introduced that enables systematic evaluation of experience-based self-evolution under challenging experience regimes characterized by noisy feedback, ambiguous credit assignment, environmental non-stationarity, and limited experience reusability.

title: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
proposal_tldr: SGDR consists of three components: a sliding-window extraction process that turns completed trajectories into reusable sub-procedures invokable at intermediate execution states, a dual text-code representation that connects skill retrieval with executable action, and a state-grounded dynamic retrieval mechanism that matches skills to both the task goal and the current webpage state.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs on Code Generation for Complex Interactive Webpages
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebIGBench, the first benchmark designed to evaluate code generation for interactive webpages with complex interactions, and proposes a novel evaluation pipeline to address the gap in automated assessment of interactive actions.

title: AgentHijack: Benchmarking Computer Use Agent Robustness to Common Environment Corruptions
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentHijack, a benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of computer-use agents under common corruptions, and proposes AgentHijack-Agent, a framework that integrates an action generator with enhanced grounding capabilities and an onlooker responsible for behavior summarization and environment checking.

title: EngiAI: Capability-Based Evaluation of Tool-Connected LLM Agents for Engineering Design
proposal_tldr: A capability-based evaluation framework for tool-connected engineering agents is introduced, which provides common evaluation dimensions for identifying failure mechanisms and structuring comparisons of models, agent architectures, and tool interfaces.

title: DRS-GUI: Dynamic Region Search for Training-Free GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: DRS-GUI is proposed, a training-free dynamic region search framework for GUI grounding that can be seamlessly integrated into existing MLLMs, and introduces a lightweight UI Perceptor that performs three human-like perceptual actions to progressively explore the interface and generate region proposals.

title: WARD: Adversarially Robust Defense of Web Agents Against Prompt Injections
proposal_tldr: This work proposes WARD (Web Agent Robust Defense against Prompt Injection), a practical guard model for secure and efficient web agents, and introduces A3T, an adaptive adversarial attack training framework that iteratively strengthens WARD through a memory-based attacker and guard co-evolution process.

title: Learning Agentic Policy from Action Guidance
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a new paradigm for agentic RL that reduces the reliance on heavy SFT data by using scalable action guidance instead, and adopts a minimal intervention principle that invokes guidance only as an adaptive fallback, matching task difficulty while minimizing off-policy risk.

title: ComplexMCP: Evaluation of LLM Agents in Dynamic, Interdependent, and Large-Scale Tool Sandbox
proposal_tldr: This work evaluates various LLMs across full-context and RAG paradigms, revealing a stark performance gap: even top-tier models fail to exceed a 60% success rate, far trailing human performance 90%.

title: LiteGUI: Distilling Compact GUI Agents with Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: A novel SFT-free training paradigm that significantly enhances the performance of small-scale models and introduces a Multi-solution Dual-level GRPO framework that jointly aligns macro-level subtask planning with micro-level execution matching, thereby improving exploration in long-horizon GUI agent scenarios.

title: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Weblica (Web Replica), a framework for constructing reproducible and scalable web environments that leverages HTTP-level caching to capture and replay stable visual states while preserving interactive behavior and LLM-based environment synthesis grounded in real-world websites and core web navigation skills.

title: Skills as Verifiable Artifacts: A Trust Schema and a Biconditional Correctness Criterion for Human-in-the-Loop Agent Runtimes
proposal_tldr: This paper gives a trust schema that includes an explicit verification level on every skill manifest; a capability gate whose HITL policy is a function of that verification level; a biconditional correctness criterion that any candidate verification procedure must satisfy on an adversarial-ensemble exercise; and a portable runtime profile with ten normative guidelines abstracted from a working open-source reference implementation.

title: Agentic AI systems: A systematic survey of multi-agent architectures, cognitive foundations, interaction, explainability, security, and performance evaluation
Benchmarking Web Agent Safety under E-commerce Deceptive Interfaces
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work studies web agent behavior under realistic deceptive interfaces in the e-commerce domain and introduces WebDecept, a lightweight and configurable plugin framework that enables controlled injection of deceptive interface patterns into existing web environments.

title: WebUncertainty: Dual-Level Uncertainty Driven Planning and Reasoning For Autonomous Web Agent
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work designs a Task Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Planning Mechanism that adaptively selects planning modes to navigate unknown environments and introduces an Action Uncertainty-Driven Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) Reasoning Mechanism, designed to tackle dual-level uncertainty in planning and reasoning.

title: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
proposal_tldr: GUI-Perturbed is introduced, a controlled perturbation framework that independently varies visual scenes and instructions to measure grounding robustness and isolates which specific capability axes are affected-spatial reasoning, visual robustness, reasoning calibration-providing diagnostic signal that aggregate benchmarks cannot.

title: AgentWebBench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Coordination in Agentic Web
proposal_tldr: AgentWebBench is introduced, a benchmark that evaluates how well a user agent synthesizes answers by interacting with website-specific content agents, and suggests that user agents need better planning and answer synthesis, while content agents need more reliable retrieval and evidence quality.

title: EE-MCP: Self-Evolving MCP-GUI Agents via Automated Environment Generation and Experience Learning
proposal_tldr: This work forms MCP-GUI interplay as a unified hybrid policy learning problem where the agent learns when each modality provides complementary advantages, and shows that distillation and experience augmentation target fundamentally different failure modes - requiring application-aware mechanism selection.

title: Structured Distillation of Web Agent Capabilities Enables Generalization
proposal_tldr: Agent-as-Annotators is introduced, a framework that structures synthetic trajectory generation for web agents by analogy to human annotation roles, replacing the Task Designer, Annotator, and Supervisor with modular LLM components.

title: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
proposal_tldr: This work conducts a process-level analysis of web agents, providing fine-grained and actionable insight into where and how each agent should be improved, and introduces WebStep, a benchmark of 1,800 task instances with controlled difficulty and automatic semantic state tracking.

title: Agentic-MME: What Agentic Capability Really Brings to Multimodal Intelligence?
proposal_tldr: Agentic-MME is introduced, a process-verified benchmark for Multimodal Agentic Capabilities, featuring over 2,000 stepwise checkpoints that average 10+ person-hours of manual annotation per task, and auditing fine-grained intermediate states rather than just final answers.

title: The Tool Illusion: Rethinking Tool Use in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This study revisits tool use in web agents through an extensive and carefully controlled study across diverse tool sources, backbone models, tool-use frameworks, and evaluation benchmarks, and hopes it provides a more reliable empirical basis and inspires future research on tool-use web agents.

title: PaperVoyager : Building Interactive Web with Visual Language Models
proposal_tldr: A Paper-to-Interactive-System Agent that converts research papers into executable interactive web systems and a structured generation framework that explicitly models mechanisms and interaction logic during synthesis are proposed.

title: ClawTrap: A MITM-Based Red-Teaming Framework for Real-World OpenClaw Security Evaluation
proposal_tldr: ClawTrap is presented, a MITM-based red-teaming framework for real-world OpenClaw security evaluation that supports diverse and customizable attack forms, and provides a reproducible pipeline for rule-driven interception, transformation, and auditing.

title: Gym-V: A Unified Vision Environment System for Agentic Vision Research
proposal_tldr: Gym-V, a unified platform of 179 procedurally generated visual environments across 10 domains with controllable difficulty, is introduced, finding that observation scaffolding is more decisive for training success than the choice of RL algorithm, with captions and game rules determining whether learning succeeds at all.

title: GUI-CEval: A Hierarchical and Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: gui-CEval is introduced, the first comprehensive benchmark for Chinese mobile GUI agents, built entirely on physical device environments and adopts a two-level structure that evaluates both atomic abilities and realistic application-level performance along five dimensions: perception, planning, reflection, execution, and evaluation.

title: AgentOS: From Application Silos to a Natural Language-Driven Data Ecosystem
proposal_tldr: It is argued that realizing AgentOS fundamentally becomes a Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD) problem, where the Agent Kernel must operate as a real-time engine for intent mining and knowledge discovery.

title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents
proposal_tldr: This work establishes a reproducible baseline for developing search-robust and epistemically humble agents capable of resisting manipulation in high-stakes domains by injecting a single high-plausibility misinformation article into a controllable search rank, and measuring the causal effect of adversarial exposure in six frontier models.

title: Turing Test on Screen: A Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agent Humanization
proposal_tldr: This work establishes the Agent Humanization Benchmark (AHB) and detection metrics to quantify the trade-off between imitability and utility, and proposes methods ranging from heuristic noise to data-driven behavioral matching to demonstrate that agents can achieve high imitability theoretically and empirically without sacrificing performance.

title: AD-Bench: A Real-World, Trajectory-Aware Advertising Analytics Benchmark for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: AD-Bench introduces two key designs: a dynamic ground-truth pipeline that replays expert tool-call trajectories to regenerate answers consistent with the current environment, mitigating answer obsolescence and a trajectory-aware evaluation that jointly measures end-to-end answer correctness (Pass@k) and trajectory coverage.

title: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
proposal_tldr: This work proposes TreeCUA to efficiently scale GUI automation with tree-structured verifiable verifiable evolution, a multi-agent collaborative framework to explore the environment, verify actions, summarize trajectories, and evaluate quality to generate high-quality and scalable GUI trajectories, and develops world knowledge guidance and global memory backtracking to avoid low-quality generation.

title: Next-Gen CAPTCHAs: Leveraging the Cognitive Gap for Scalable and Diverse GUI-Agent Defense
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Next-Gen CAPTCHAs, a scalable defense framework designed to secure the next-generation web against the advanced agents, and exploits the persistent human-agent "Cognitive Gap" in interactive perception, memory, decision-making, and action.

title: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving Perfect Accuracy on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
proposal_tldr: Minitap is presented, a multi-agent system that achieves 100% success on the AndroidWorld benchmark, the first to fully solve all 116 tasks and surpassing human performance and released as open-source software.

title: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
proposal_tldr: Trifuse is proposed, an attention-based grounding framework that explicitly integrates complementary spatial anchors in GUI images and integrates attention, OCR-derived textual cues, and icon-level caption semantics via a Consensus-SinglePeak (CS) fusion strategy that enforces cross-modal agreement while retaining sharp localization peaks.

title: BeSafe-Bench: Unveiling Behavioral Safety Risks of Situated Agents in Functional Environments
proposal_tldr: BeSafe-Bench is presented, a benchmark for exposing behavioral safety risks of situated agents in functional environments, covering four representative domains: Web, Mobile, Embodied VLM, and Embodied VLA, and a hybrid evaluation framework that combines rule-based checks with LLM-as-a-judge reasoning to assess real environmental impacts.

title: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes Coordinate Compression Policy Optimization (CCPO), an efficient policy optimization framework that couples visual compression with policy optimization for multi-turn GUI agents, and introduces Coordinate-Aware Spatial Compression (CASC), which aggregates coordinates from multiple rollouts to capture target-relevant regions and progressively narrow historical attention around key visual areas.

title: LegalWebAgent: Empowering Access to Justice via LLM-Based Web Agents
proposal_tldr: The LegalWebAgent framework is introduced, which employs a web agent powered by multimodal large language models to bridge the gap in access to justice for ordinary citizens, and combines the natural language understanding capabilities of large language models with multimodal perception.

title: Promoting Sustainable Web Agents: Benchmarking and Estimating Energy Consumption through Empirical and Theoretical Analysis
proposal_tldr: This work provides an initial exploration of the energy and CO₂ cost associated with web agents from both a theoretical —via estimation— and an empirical perspective —by benchmarking.

title: Aspect-augmented distillation of task-oriented dialogues to small language models
How Can AI Augment Access to Justice? Public Defenders' Perspectives on Responsible AI Adoption
venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency
proposal_tldr: A comprehensive task-level map of public defense work is developed, dividing it into five pillars to clarify where AI can and cannot contribute: evidence investigation, legal research & writing, client communication & support, courtroom representation, and defense strategies.

title: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
proposal_tldr: HackWorld is presented, the first framework for systematically evaluating CUAs'capabilities to exploit web application vulnerabilities via visual interaction and exposes the current limitations of CUAs in web security contexts and highlights opportunities for developing more security-aware agents capable of effective vulnerability detection and exploitation.

title: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability for GUI Agents
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
proposal_tldr: UIPro, a novel generalist GUI agent trained with extensive multi-platform and multi-task GUI interaction data, coupled with a unified action space is proposed, establishing a unified action space to harmonize heterogeneous GUI agent task datasets and producing a merged dataset to foster the action prediction ability of UIPro via continued fine-tuning.

title: See, Think, Act: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Effectively Interact with GUI by Identifying Toggles
proposal_tldr: A state control benchmark with binary toggle instructions derived from public datasets is constructed and proposed State-aware Reasoning (StaR), a multimodal reasoning method that enables agents to perceive the current toggle state, infer the desired state from the instruction, and act accordingly.

title: Learning Active Perception via Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: This work proposes LASER, a self-evolving framework that progressively endows VLMs with multi-step perception capabilities, enabling precise coordinate prediction and integrates Monte Carlo quality estimation with Intersection-over-Union (IoU)-based region quality evaluation to jointly encourage both accuracy and diversity in constructing high-quality preference data.

title: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: FlashAdventure, a benchmark of 34 Flash-based adventure games designed to test full story arc completion and tackle the observation-behavior gap, is introduced and CUA-as-a-Judge, an automated gameplay evaluator, and COAST, an agentic framework leveraging long-term clue memory to better plan and solve sequential tasks are proposed.

title: Automatic XPath generation agents for vertical websites by LLMs
venue: Journal of King Saud University: Computer and Information Sciences
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a new framework that leverages a multi-task decomposition strategy, enabling LLMs, despite their limitations in handling structured information, to learn robust XPath expressions from seed pages and apply them to unseen web pages.

title: Is Extending Modality The Right Path Towards Omni-Modality?
proposal_tldr: This work investigates the effect of extending modality, the dominant technique for training multimodal models, where an off-the-shelf language model is fine-tuned on target-domain and language data, and investigates three key questions: Does modality extension compromise core language abilities?

title: Benchmarking and Boosting Multilingual Capabilities of LVLMs via OCR-Centric Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: This work designs an OCR-centric GRPO training strategy using fully synthesized, label-free OCR data, without expensive task-specific VQA supervision, and improves general multilingual VQA capability, reduces cross-lingual disparities under the vision setting, and transfers gains beyond PM4Bench.

title: An Autonomous RL Agent Methodology for Dynamic Web UI Testing in a BDD Framework
venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on AI and Robotics
proposal_tldr: A novel system architecture is presented, detailing the state representation, action space, and reward mechanisms that guide the autonomous exploration of UI states that transform software quality assurance and streamline continuous testing processes.

title: Carbon and Silicon, Coexist or Compete? A Survey on Human-AI Interactions in Agent-based Modeling and Simulation
proposal_tldr: Existing works in agent-based modeling and simulation are investigated and a novel taxonomy to categorize the interactions derived from them are proposed, providing researchers who develop interactions with comprehensive guidance on how humans and AI interact.

title: Explainable Behavior Cloning: Teaching Large Language Model Agents through Learning by Demonstration
proposal_tldr: An Explainable Behavior Cloning LLM Agent (EBC-LLMAgent), a novel approach that combines large language models with behavior cloning by learning demonstrations to create intelligent and explainable agents for autonomous mobile app interaction is proposed.

title: AutoDirector: Online Auto-scheduling Agents for Multi-sensory Composition
proposal_tldr: AutoDirector is introduced, an interactive multi-sensory composition framework that supports long shots, special effects, music scoring, dubbing, dubbing, and lip-syncing and demonstrates the potential of AI in collaborating with humans in the role of a film director to complete multi-sensory films.

title: HelloFresh: LLM Evaluations on Streams of Real-World Human Editorial Actions across X Community Notes and Wikipedia edits
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: HelloFresh is introduced, based on continuous streams of real-world data generated by intrinsically motivated human labelers, and it is found that HelloFresh yields a temporally consistent ranking.

title: When Efficiency Becomes a Vulnerability: Computational Cost Attacks on WebAgents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes CostBomb, a generation-then-selection attack framework that leverages large language models to generate diverse adversarial prompts and a reinforcement learning–enhanced selector to identify the most effective perturbations.

title: Enhancing Web Search Agents With Self-Play Contrastive Fine-Tuning
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes TAPE (Trajectory Alignment and exPerience pool Evolution), a novel self-evolving fine-tuning framework designed to enhance the generalization and robustness of web search agents without requiring large-scale human annotation.

title: UI-Hawk: Unleashing the Screen Stream Understanding for Mobile GUI Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: Recipe2Plan: Evaluating Planning Abilities of LLMs for Efficient and Feasible Multitasking with Time Constraints Between Actions
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: LEAP & LEAN: Look-ahead Planning and Agile Navigation for LLM Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Generative Context Distillation
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Generative Context Distillation (GCD), a lightweight prompt internalization method that employs a joint training approach that replicates the behavior of models with prompt inputs but also generates the content of the prompt along with reasons for why the model’s behavior should change accordingly.

title: A GENT X PLOIT : End-to-End Redteaming of Black-Box AI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a generic black-box fuzzing framework, A GENT X PLOIT, designed to automatically discover and exploit indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities across diverse LLM agents, and exhibits strong transferability across unseen tasks and internal LLMs, as well as promising results against defenses.

title: The Verifiable Action Card: Trustworthy Human-in-the-Loop Control for Secure Autonomous Agents
proposal_tldr: Results show that grounding approval in the action that will actually execute provides architectural protection against security failures that prompt-level defences and conventional HITL confirmation cannot reliably prevent.

title: Last Step Matters: Early Uncertainty Cannot Predict Failure in Long-Horizon Agents
proposal_tldr: An underlying mechanism explaining the gap in uncertainty quantification is identified: path switching, where agents frequently abandon their current search direction in-trajectory, breaking the link between early signal and final outcome.

title: MemGuard: Persisting Verifier Signals for LLM-Agent Memory Governance
proposal_tldr: Averaged over five seeds, MemGuard achieves the best success metric and lowest average steps in all 16 backbone-benchmark settings, improving over ReasoningBank, the strongest prior baseline among the memory methods the authors evaluate.

title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
proposal_tldr: This work conducts a comprehensive re-evaluation of two memory-based methods, broadening the scope of evaluation along two axes: including multiple self-improving runs to quantify variance, and shuffling the tasks to investigate the effect of task order.

title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
proposal_tldr: This work designs a contrastive study that combines controlled quantitative experiments with paired trajectory analysis and consolidates observations into a taxonomy of three high-level categories and twelve skill-use modes, showing that skills work when noisy trajectories become procedural anchors that stabilize execution.

title: ComboShoppingBench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Budget-Constrained Basket Shopping with Coupons
proposal_tldr: This work introduces ComboShoppingBench, an agentic shopping benchmark for open-ended yet verifiable basket construction in a simulated commerce and takeout environment and demonstrates that even strong agents struggle on this benchmark, highlighting substantial room for improvement in reliable, constraint-aware combo shopping.

title: Beyond Simply Environment Scaling: Designing Effective Environment Distributions for Multimodal Agent Learning
proposal_tldr: This work studies how to build more effective training environment distributions from two dimensions: diversity and difficulty structure, and proposes Ability-aware Environment Selection (AES) and Hierarchical Difficulty Curriculum (HDC), which effectively improve multimodal agent training.

title: Agentic Commerce World: An Auditable and Verifiable Environment for Vibe Commerce
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Agentic Commerce World (ACWorld), an environment for evaluating such agents across ongoing transactions, and validates agent actions before updating shared transaction state and records the resulting interactions, making agent behavior auditable and evaluation reproducible.

title: GABench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on Graph Analysis Tasks
proposal_tldr: GABench is introduced, a comprehensive benchmark for agentic graph analysis that covers four graph analysis task categories: graph retrieval, graph theory, graph machine learning, and graph open-ended question answering and provides practical insights into the development and evaluation of LLM agents for graph analysis.

title: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
proposal_tldr: CADebug, a framework for localizing root causes in CUA trajectories and guiding re-execution and human annotations are used to evaluate RCA predictions and, in controlled re-rollout comparisons, to fix restart points.

title: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes an interactive reward agent (IRA) based on a propose-then-verify framework to acquire and verify evidence from the post-execution environment and applies IRA to reinforcement learning of GUI agents, achieving a 34.0% OSWorld success rate.

title: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
proposal_tldr: Empirical studies show that joint dynamics optimization yields stable improvements over single-objective training, and downstream performance scales steadily with the volume of transition data.

title: DRNOISE: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents in Misleading Evidence Environments
proposal_tldr: DRNOISE, a 100-task benchmark for answer recovery under misleading evidence, is introduced, a 100-task benchmark for answer recovery under misleading evidence that requires active reconciliation of direct claims with record-level evidence.

title: HyMobileAgent: Data-Environment Co-Scaling for Efficient GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This report presents HyMobileAgent, a mobile GUI agent built on Hy3.0-VL-A3B, a vision-native foundation model featuring native any-resolution input, an A3B-scale deployment budget, and a 32K context window to model extended interaction histories.

title: Critic Experience Bank: Self-Evolving Step-Level Confidence Estimation for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces the \method (\methodshort), a self-evolving critic framework in which an LLM critic accumulates evidence from its own past judgments and their observed consequences, reducing ECE by up to $54\% relative to the strongest training-free baseline.

title: Difficulty-Aware Hybrid Routing for Cost-Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Intelligent Communications and Computing (ICICC)
proposal_tldr: The Difficulty-Aware Hybrid Router is proposed, a lightweight framework that jointly leverages query-level, context-level, and draft-level features to classify each request into one of three inference tiers: direct answering by a small model, small-model answering with lightweight verification, or full processing by a large model.

title: Internalizing the Future: A Unified Agentic Training Paradigm for World Model Planning
proposal_tldr: The results demonstrate that effective internal world modeling in LLM agents requires a capability-first training pipeline to achieve grounded and calibrated foresight, and this approach consistently outperforms other training baselines.

title: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
proposal_tldr: Explicit skill libraries make computer-using agents easier to inspect, but it remains unclear whether such libraries can be mined from interaction data in a way that improves downstream policies. We study this question through a three-stage pipeline that segments GUI trajectories, clusters segments

title: ProCUA-SFT Technical Report
proposal_tldr: ProCUA-SFT, a dataset of 3.1M step-level SFT samples distilled from 93K synthetic trajectories across 2,484 application combinations, is presented, producing a fully automated pipeline that synthesizes grounded tasks on live desktops seeded with real-world content.

title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?
proposal_tldr: It is proved that comparing a $k$ -group spread against a two-run noise difference reports an inflation of about 2.25 at six groups, when the true disparity is zero, and given the arity-matched correction and exact randomization test that repair it.

title: FlowBank: Query-Adaptive Agentic Workflows Optimization through Precompute-and-Reuse
proposal_tldr: FlowBank is presented, a three-stage framework for portfolio-based agentic workflow optimization that achieves the highest average score among the evaluated methods while remaining cost-competitive, improving over the strongest automated and handcrafted baselines by 4.26% and 14.92% relative, respectively.

title: AgentJet: A Distributed Swarm Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: AgentJet is a distributed swarm training framework based on a decoupled multi-node architecture that supports heterogeneous multi-model RL, mixed-task training with isolated runtimes, fault-tolerant execution, and live code iteration through hot-swappable clients.

title: MMG2Skill: Can Agents Distill In-the-Wild Guides into Self-Evolving Skills?
proposal_tldr: This work proposes MMG2Skill, a closed-loop framework that compiles guides into editable skills, conditions a fixed vision-language model (VLM) agent on these skills during execution, and revises the skills from trajectory-level root-cause feedback without using benchmark scores.

title: Persistent Memory Modeling and Policy Optimization for Large Language Model Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Electronic Technology and Information Science (ICETIS)
proposal_tldr: Results show that the proposed method can more effectively support continuous state tracking, key history utilization, and global goal maintenance in long-term tasks, demonstrating superior comprehensive advantages in task completion capability, planning quality, constraint satisfaction capability, and policy stability.

title: Skill Availability and Presentation Granularity in Large-Language-Model Agents: A Controlled SkillsBench Study
proposal_tldr: In this controlled subset, skill availability is associated with higher success than no skill, while the tested presentation-granularity changes yield small, uncertain, and model-dependent effects.

title: Do Proactive Agents Need an LLM to Decide When to Act?
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a temporal-graph-learning (TGL) controller that learns these predictions jointly and supplies both outputs in one forward pass, and shows that a small graph model can handle both decisions and improve the language agents it controls.

title: HTMLCure: Turning Browser Experience into State Guided Repair for Interactive HTML
proposal_tldr: HTMLCure is introduced, a browser experience framework that evaluates HTML after the system has interacted with it, and improves raw 27B SFT by 15.3 points and approaching the level of strong reference systems.

title: SkillEvolBench: Benchmarking the Evolution from Episodic Experience to Procedural Skills
proposal_tldr: It is found that current agents often adapt locally but rarely form robust reusable skills, and capacity and cost analyses show that writing more skills or larger Tier-3 resource libraries is not sufficient: additional updates can improve coverage while introducing episode-specific drift and procedural clutter.

title: Interactive Evaluation Requires a Design Science
proposal_tldr: This position paper argues that interactive evaluation should be treated as a principled evaluation paradigm, not merely a new family of agent benchmarks, and proposes a two-axis taxonomy and examines how longstanding evaluation challenges reappear at the trajectory level.

title: SPIKE: An Adaptive Dual Controller Framework for Cost-Efficient Long-Horizon Game Agents
proposal_tldr: Long-horizon multimodal agents in open-world games must stay goal-directed across many low-level interactions under tight token and latency budgets. Existing approaches often trade off costly per-step reasoning against reactive execution that can drift, repeat failures, and recover poorly. Our key i

title: DecisionBench: A Benchmark for Emergent Delegation in Long-Horizon Agentic Workflows
proposal_tldr: DecisionBench is introduced, a benchmark substrate for emergent delegation in long-horizon agentic workflows and a counterfactual ceiling places perfect delegation 15-31 percentage points above measured performance on every suite, locating large unrealized headroom for future orchestration methods.

title: Agent Meltdowns: The Road to Hell Is Paved with Helpful Agents
proposal_tldr: An agent-agnostic infrastructure for injecting simulated local and remote errors into the rollout environment is implemented and used to systematically evaluate agent systems powered by GPT, Grok, and Gemini.

title: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: The Self-Evolving GUI Agent (SE-GA) is proposed, a novel framework that integrates hierarchical memory structures with an iterative self-improvement mechanism that facilitates long-term planning by dynamically retrieving episodic, semantic, and experiential memories during inference.

title: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: Mem-W, a series of latent-memory-native GUI agents that treat memory as part of the agent's continuous context rather than as an auxiliary symbolic scaffold, is introduced, suggesting that latent-context-native memory can serve as a scalable foundation for long-horizon GUI agency.

title: WebTrap: Stealthy Mid-Task Hijacking of Browser Agents During Navigation
proposal_tldr: A mid-task hijacking injection attack that exploits the agent's navigation vulnerabilities, binding the two goals so tightly that standard defense mechanisms cannot restore the system to normal operation, revealing a critical vulnerability in agent systems during long-horizon tasks that they can be stealthily hijacked.

title: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: The extensive experimental results demonstrate that BAMI significantly enhances the accuracy of various GUI grounding models in a training-free setting, and ablation studies confirm the robustness of the BAMI approach across diverse parameter configurations, highlighting its stability and effectiveness.

title: WAAA! Web Adversaries Against Agentic Browsers
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes the first web-focused threat model for agentic browsers and uses it to derive a taxonomy of 20 attacks across both the web and LLM space, and implements 18 of the attacks.

title: FP-Agent: Fingerprinting AI Browsing Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper presents the first controlled measurement study of seven AI browsing agents and human users, and finds that browser fingerprints provide limited discriminative power when shared by multiple AI browsing agents.

title: Odysseus: Scaling VLMs to 100+ Turn Decision-Making in Games via Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: It is shown that pretrained VLMs provide strong action priors, significantly improving sample efficiency during RL training and reducing the need for manual design choices such as action engineering, compared to classical deep RL trained from scratch.

title: AgentSim: A Platform for Verifiable Agent-Trace Simulation
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AgentSim, an open-source platform for simulating RAG agents that generates verifiable, stepwise traces of agent reasoning over any document collection, and constructs and releases the Agent-Trace Corpus (ATC), a large collection of grounded reasoning trajectories spanning three established IR benchmarks.

title: Web2BigTable: A Bi-Level Multi-Agent LLM System for Internet-Scale Information Search and Extraction
proposal_tldr: This work introduces Web2BigTable, a multi-agent framework for web-to-table search that supports both Breadth-oriented and depth-oriented tasks, and sets a new state of the art on WideSearch, achieving an Avg@4 Success Rate of 38.50 and generalises to depth-oriented search on XBench-DeepSearch, achieving 73.0 accuracy.

title: GAIA-v2-LILT: Multilingual Adaptation of Agent Benchmark beyond Translation
venue: Proceedings of the 1st Workshop on Multilinguality in the Era of Large Language Models (MeLLM 2026)
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a refined workflow for adapting English benchmarks into multiple languages with explicit functional alignment, cultural alignment, and difficulty calibration using both automated checks and human review, and introduces GAIA-v2-LILT, a re-audited multilingual extension of GAIA covering five non-English languages.

title: Human-AI-UI Interactions Across Modalities
proposal_tldr: This workshop will explore how UI agents bridge human intent and system behavior by interpreting multimodal inputs and generating adaptive outputs across surfaces from screens to extended reality (XR), and it will examine not only their technical capabilities but also their broader impact, including how agents reshape daily workflows.

title: Beyond Fluency: Toward Reliable Trajectories in Agentic IR
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: This position paper synthesizes failure modes observed in industrial agentic systems, categorizing errors across planning, retrieval, reasoning, and execution, and argues that safe deployment requires moving beyond endpoint accuracy toward trajectory integrity and causal attribution.

title: StressWeb: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Web Agent Robustness under Realistic Interaction Variability
proposal_tldr: Through extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art multimodal web agents, this work shows that stress-based evaluation exposes failure modes and substantial robustness gaps that remain hidden under clean benchmark conditions.

title: CAPTCHA Solving for Native GUI Agents: Automated Reasoning-Action Data Generation and Self-Corrective Training
proposal_tldr: This work develops a dynamic CAPTCHA system spanning seven representative CAPTCHA types, designed to stress primitive and complementary capabilities for CAPTCHA solving, and develops an automated data collection and curation pipeline that generates large-scale CAPTCHA interaction trajectories paired with reasoning traces.

title: MedSPOT: A Workflow-Aware Sequential Grounding Benchmark for Clinical GUI
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MedSPOT, a workflow-aware sequential grounding benchmark for clinical GUI environments, and proposes a strict sequential evaluation protocol that terminates task assessment upon the first incorrect grounding prediction, explicitly measuring error propagation in multi-step workflows.

title: WebPII: Benchmarking Visual PII Detection for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebPII, a fine-grained synthetic benchmark of 44,865 annotated e-commerce UI images designed with three key properties: extended PII taxonomy including transaction-level identifiers that enable reidentification, anticipatory detection for partially-filled forms where users are actively entering data, and scalable generation through VLM-based UI reproduction.

title: Reward Prediction with Factorized World States
proposal_tldr: This paper investigates whether well-defined world state representations alone can enable accurate reward prediction across domains, and shows promising zero-shot results against both VLWM-critic and LLM-as-a-Judge reward models.

title: Avenir-UX: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: Avenir-UX is presented, a user-experience evaluation agent that simulates user behavior on websites and produces standardized usability testing, and its multimodal grounding improves robustness for web-based interaction and UX evaluation scenarios.

title: Overseeing Agents Without Constant Oversight: Challenges and Opportunities
proposal_tldr: This study surfaces challenges for human verification of agentic systems, including managing built-in assumptions, users'subjective and changing correctness criteria, and the shortcomings, yet importance, of communicating the agent's process.

title: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: ACuRL, an Autonomous Curriculum Reinforcement Learning framework that continually adapts agents to specific environments with zero human data is introduced, yielding 3-29% absolute performance gains on the target environments without catastrophic forgetting on others.

title: GuideWeb: A Benchmark for Automatic In-App Guide Generation on Real-World Web UIs
proposal_tldr: This work introduces GuideWeb, a new benchmark for automatic in-app guide generation on real-world web UIs and proposes a comprehensive evaluation suite that jointly measures the accuracy of guide target element selection and the quality of generated intents and guide texts.

title: Strong Reasoning Isn't Enough: Evaluating Evidence Elicitation in Interactive Diagnosis
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: An interactive evaluation framework that explicitly models the consultation process using a simulated patient and a simulated reporter grounded in atomic evidences is proposed, and Information Coverage Rate (ICR) is introduced to quantify how completely an agent uncovers necessary evidence during interaction.

title: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes BEPA (Bi-Level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation), which turns static expert traces into policy-aligned guidance via self-rolled reachable trajectories under the base policy and a per-task, dynamically updated cache used in RLVR (LEVEL-2).

title: iSHIFT: Lightweight Slow-Fast GUI Agent with Adaptive Perception
proposal_tldr: iSHIFT: Implicit Slow-fast Hybrid Inference with Flexible Tokens is introduced, a lightweight agent that integrates latent thinking (implicit chain-of-thought) with a perception control module that enables an MLLM to switch between a slow mode, which leverages detailed visual grounding for high precision and a fast mode that uses global cues for efficiency.

title: DAVE: A VLM Vision Encoder for Document Understanding and Web Agents
proposal_tldr: DAVE, a vision encoder purpose-built for VLMs and tailored for these tasks, is introduced, designed to leverage abundant unlabeled data to bypass the need for costly large-scale annotations for document and web images.

title: SIEVE: Selective Integrity Verification and Escalation for Defending LLM Agents against Indirect Prompt Injection
proposal_tldr: This work proposes SIEVE, which verifies tool transitions and argument sources against an Intent Graph, escalating actions that cannot pass deterministic verification to semantic adjudication, and evaluates SIEVE on AgentLure and AgentDojo against MELON, DRIFT, IPIGuard, and ARGUS.

title: AFRAgent : An Adaptive Feature Renormalization Based High Resolution Aware GUI agent
venue: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
proposal_tldr: AFRAgent is introduced, an instruct-BLIP-based multimodal architecture that achieves superior performance in GUI automation while being less than one-fourth the size of its nearest competitor, and an adaptive feature renormalization-based (a token-level affine transformation) technique that effectively enriches low-resolution image embeddings and fuses high-resolution details.

title: Look It Up: Analysing Internal Web Search Capabilities of Modern LLMs
proposal_tldr: Overall, internal web-based retrieval functions effectively as a low-latency verification mechanism, but falls short as a reliable IR pipeline, highlighting the need for improved retrieval triggering, query formulation, and evidence-aware confidence calibration in web-enabled LLMs.

title: WebRec: Enhancing LLM-based Recommendations with Attention-guided RAG from Web
proposal_tldr: WebRec is proposed, a novel web-based RAG framework, which takes advantage of the reasoning capability of LLMs to interpret recommendation tasks into queries of user preferences that cater to web retrieval.

title: AgentExpt: Automating AI Experiment Design with LLM-based Resource Retrieval Agent
proposal_tldr: An automated data-collection pipeline that links roughly one hundred thousand accepted papers to the baselines and datasets they actually used and a reasoning-augmented reranker that exact interaction chains to construct explicit reasoning chains and finetunes a large language model to produce interpretable justifications and refined rankings are designed.

title: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: A framework that retrieves and filters tutorial videos, converts them into structured demonstration trajectories, and dynamically selects trajectories as in-context guidance during execution is proposed, suggesting that abundant online videos can be systematically distilled into actionable guidance that improves computer-use agents at inference time.

title: CRMWeaver: Building Powerful Business Agent via Agentic RL and Shared Memories
proposal_tldr: To acclimate the agentic model to intricate business environments, the proposed CRMWeaver employs a synthesis data generation and RL-based paradigm during training, which significantly improves the model's ability to handle complex data and varied tasks.

title: Can I Trust You? Advancing GUI Task Automation with Action Trust Score
proposal_tldr: This work introduces TrustScorer, which evaluates the trustworthiness of actions generated by AI agents, enabling a new human-AI collaboration paradigm in GUI task automation, i.e., actions with low predicted trust scores are redirected for human intervention, thereby mingling human precision with AI efficiency.

title: WebRouter: Query-specific Router via Variational Information Bottleneck for Cost-sensitive Web Agent
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebRouter, a novel query-specific router trained from an information-theoretic perspective, which learns a compressed representation of the input prompt while explicitly penalizing the expected operational cost.

title: MacroBench: A Novel Testbed for Web Automation Scripts via Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: The MacroBench benchmark, a code-first benchmark that evaluates whether LLMs can synthesize reusable browser-automation programs (macros) from natural-language goals by reading HTML/DOM and emitting Selenium, is introduced to enable reproducible assessment of macro synthesis for web automation.

title: Multi-Click: Cross-Tab Web Automation via Action Generalization
venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
proposal_tldr: Multi-Click introduces algorithms for identifying analogous elements from structural and visual attributes; techniques for intuitively selecting and visualizing targets; and uses interactive data grids to manage variation in text entry and retrieval tasks.

title: Small Models, Big Results: Achieving Superior Intent Extraction through Decomposition
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work performs structured interaction summarization, capturing key information from each user action and performs intent extraction using a fine-tuned model operating on the aggregated summaries, improving intent understanding in resource-constrained models.

title: Throttling Web Agents Using Reasoning Gates
proposal_tldr: This paper designs a framework that imposes tunable costs on agents before providing access to resources, and introduces rebus-based Reasoning Gates, synthetic text puzzles that require multi-hop reasoning over world knowledge (thereby throttling an agent's model).

title: Language Models Identify Ambiguities and Exploit Loopholes
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: This work designs scenarios where LLMs are given a goal and an ambiguous user instruction in conflict with the goal, and measures different models'abilities to exploit loopholes to satisfy their given goals as opposed to the goals of the user.

title: OmniPlay: Benchmarking Omni-Modal Models on Omni-Modal Game Playing
proposal_tldr: This comprehensive evaluation of six leading omni-modal models reveals a critical dichotomy: they exhibit superhuman performance on high-fidelity memory tasks but suffer from systemic failures in challenges requiring robust reasoning and strategic planning, suggesting that the path toward robust AGI requires a research focus beyond scaling to explicitly address synergistic fusion.

title: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: It is argued that web agents must first acquire sufficient knowledge to effectively engage in cognitive reasoning, and decompose a web agent's capabilities into two essential stages: knowledge content learning and cognitive processes.

title: SCOPE: Stochastic and Counterbiased Option Placement for Evaluating Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: SCOPE, an evaluation framework designed to measure and mitigate selection bias in a dataset-independent manner, consistently outperformed existing debiasing methods in terms of stable performance improvements and showed clearer confidence distributions over correct options.

title: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work takes a step toward privacy-preserving and resource-efficient agents by developing a lightweight vision-language model that runs entirely on local machines and introduces an LLM-as-Judge framework that automatically evaluates and filters synthetic interaction trajectories, producing high-quality data for reinforcement learning without human annotation.

title: Safety Degradation in AI Agents
proposal_tldr: Investigating how expanding retrieval access affects model reliability, bias propagation, and harmful content generation reveals a consistent degradation in refusal rates, bias sensitivity, and harmfulness safeguards as models gain broader access to external sources, culminating in a phenomenon the authors term safety degradation.

title: Planet as a Brain: Towards Internet of AgentSites based on AIOS Server
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces AIOS Server, a runtime framework to host agents and enable global-scale collaboration among decentralized agents, and presents the world's first practically deployed Internet of Agentsites (AIOS-IoA), including AgentHub for agent registration and discovery and AgentChat for interactive communication.

title: Playpen: An Environment for Exploring Learning Through Conversational Interaction
proposal_tldr: It is found that imitation learning through SFT improves performance on unseen instances, but negatively impacts other skills, while interactive learning with GRPO shows balanced improvements without loss of skills.

title: MARS: Memory-Enhanced Agents with Reflective Self-improvement
proposal_tldr: The MARS framework significantly enhances the agents capabilities in handling multi-tasking and long-span information by integrating iterative feedback, reflective mechanisms, and a memory optimization mechanism based on the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve.

title: STEVE: A Step Verification Pipeline for Computer-use Agent Training
proposal_tldr: STEVE, a step verification pipeline for computer-use agent training that adopts the Kahneman and Tversky Optimization to optimize the agent from the binary stepwise labels, achieves leading performance in the challenging live desktop environment WinAgentArena with great efficiency at a reduced cost.

title: Bi-Fact: A Bidirectional Factorization-based Evaluation of Intent Extraction from UI Trajectories
proposal_tldr: A novel method that decomposes intents into atomic facts and performs bidirectional comparisons to assess precision and recall is introduced, establishing a more robust evaluation framework for UI-driven intent understanding.

title: AgentMario: A Multitask Agent for Robotic Interaction With Locker Systems
proposal_tldr: A robotic locker system is needed where automated storage and retrieval of items are required without the need for staff presence. For example, a robot can provide 7/24 available services of medical items pick-up and return, during the COVID-19 pandemic (or under other emergencies). A robotic locker

title: Thinking Forward and Backward: Effective Backward Planning with Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: A backward planning algorithm for LLMs is proposed that first flips the problem and then plans forward in the flipped problem, which helps avoid the backward bias, generate more diverse candidate plans, and exploit asymmetries between the forward and backward directions in planning problems.

title: LocateBench: Evaluating the Locating Ability of Vision Language Models
proposal_tldr: This work proposes LocateBench, a high-quality benchmark dedicated to evaluating the ability to locate an object in an image according to natural language instructions, and measures the accuracy of several large vision language models.

title: Visual Grounding Methods for Efficient Interaction with Desktop Graphical User Interfaces
proposal_tldr: This work explores Instruction Visual Grounding (IVG), a multi-modal approach to object identification within a GUI, and proposes two main methods: IVGocr, which combines a Large Language Model (LLM), an object detection model, and an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) module; and IVGdirect, which uses a multimodal architecture for end-to-end grounding.

title: AUTONODE: A Neuro-Graphic Self-Learnable Engine for Cognitive GUI Automation
venue: International Conference on Automation and Computing
proposal_tldr: The methodology synergizes cognitive functionalities with robotic automation, endowing AUTONODE with the ability to learn from experience, and highlights its proficiency in managing a diverse array of web-based tasks, ranging from data extraction to transaction processing.

title: AllTogether: Investigating the Efficacy of Spliced Prompt for Web Navigation using Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: AllTogether, a standardized prompt template that enhances task context representation, thereby improving LLMs' performance in HTML-based web navigation, is introduced, revealing that models like GPT-4 outperform smaller models in web navigation tasks.

title: SimuWoB: Simulating Real-World Mobile Apps for Fast and Faithful GUI Agent Benchmarking
Adapting LLM Agents with Universal Communication Feedback
venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: On the Fine-Grained Planning Abilities of VLM Web Agents
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

title: A Survey on AI Search with Large Language Models
proposal_tldr: An in-depth review of recent advancements in AI search, focusing on Text-based AI Search, Web Browsing Agents, Multimodal AI Search, Benchmarks, Software, and Products, and examine the limitations of current AI search methods and explore promising future directions.

title: DyPO: Dynamic Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Interactive Reasoning
proposal_tldr: DyPO incorporates four key innovations: distinct thinking and action tokens that integrate real-time environmental feedback during rollouts, removal of divergence regularization for dynamic reasoning transition, masked intermediate observations with simplified advantage estimation for enhanced stability, and auxiliary resampling with rejection sampling to mitigate over-generation noise.

title: CAVEAT: Towards Robust Computer-Use Agents in Incentive-Misaligned Environments
proposal_tldr: CAVEAT-Harness is developed, which targets failures and raises the optimal purchase rate by up to 80.0 percentage points, and targeted post-training further improves a smaller open model, to establish incentive robustness as a distinct challenge for delegated agents and diagnose failure modes.

title: Omni2Web: Benchmarking Audiovisual Website Development
proposal_tldr: Omni2Web, a bilingual benchmark of 918 instances spanning 13,907 edit steps, is introduced, revealing substantial headroom in multimodal intent recovery and code execution and highlighting the promise of pairing Omni rewriters with coding models.

title: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MATE, a lightweight, policy-conditioned auditor that encodes both agent trajectories and natural-language security policies to determine whether a trajectory violates a given policy and to explain why, and shows that practical, fine-grained security auditing for heterogeneous mobile agents is both feasible and effective.

title: Dual-Axis Policy Optimization for LLM Agents: Bayesian Feedback Attribution and Trajectory Mass Normalization
proposal_tldr: Experiments with GRPO and GiGPO on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA show that both axes provide independent gains and that their combi- nation consistently achieves the strongest overall performance across model scales.

title: DeliveryGym: An RL Environment for Long-Horizon Embodied Agent Planning with Adaptive Curriculum
proposal_tldr: DeliveryGym is introduced, a 3D environment for evaluating and training agents on continuous courier shifts that couples multimodal tool interaction with persistent world dynamics and computes trajectory rewards from simulator events, making the costs of an agent's decisions available for reinforcement learning (RL).

title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents
proposal_tldr: A targeted prompt-level defense is evaluated and finds that it can reduce memory injection in many settings, but provides limited protection once the persistent memory has been poisoned.

title: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
proposal_tldr: CUA-Universe is introduced, a scalable environment-to-data pipeline that turns real desktop software into hybrid GUI+CLI environments and training on this data shifts behavior from inefficient GUI interaction and brittle CLI scripting toward effective GUI+CLI orchestration.

title: Beyond Scaling: A Survey of Data-Efficient Learning for LLM Agents
venue: Proceedings of the Thirty-Fifth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
proposal_tldr: An agent-centric view of data-efficient learning is developed, an agentic learning loop is formulated, data efficiency is defined as capability improvement without proportional increases in supervision or real-environment trial-and-error, and methods are synthesized into experience augmentation, agent structural design, and learning paradigms.

title: LEAP: Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for LLM-based Probabilistic Forecasting
proposal_tldr: This work proposes LEAP (Likelihood Elicitation and Aggregation for Probabilistic forecasting), which reorganizes how collected evidence is used in the prediction stage and improves most prediction and calibration metrics across models and remains stronger under controlled comparisons of prior access, inference budget, and aggregation.

title: Analysis of architecture options for foundation-model-based agents: A taxonomy and decision model
Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
proposal_tldr: AdaptRubric is proposed, a Coarse-to-Fine Rubrics Framework that constructs task-adaptive judging criteria through a category-level coarse stage and an instance-level fine stage, and consistently outperforms prior reward agents.

title: IAPO: Influence-Aware Policy Optimization for Credit Assignment in Multi-Turn Service Agents
proposal_tldr: Influence-Aware Policy Optimization (IAPO), which represents each rollout as a typed influence-dependency graph over trainable agent actions, with user and tool observations serving as evidence, is introduced and advances the understanding of credit assignment in multi-turn user interactions.

title: Signal or Noise? A Benchmark Study of Agent Skills in Web Development
proposal_tldr: These findings recast a matched Skill as a hypothesis about a particular Skill-project-model triple rather than a portable asset, reframing injection as a per-deployment routing decision and making length-matched controls and per-model audits a minimum standard for Agent-Skill evaluation.

title: Automata from Agent Traces: Failure and Next-Step Prediction
proposal_tldr: Behavioral topology is shaped more by the deployment harness than by the LLM, providing a model-agnostic structural primitive for safety auditing and runtime monitoring, and addresses both prediction goals.

title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: MileGPO (Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization) is proposed, which derives process-level credit from grouped on-policy rollouts through three designs and indicates that reliability weighting, local progress, and same-state branch evidence complement milestone discovery and resolve ambiguous intermediate credit.

title: Wuying-Browser-Agent: Real-World Centric Fundamental Long-Horizon Browser Agents
proposal_tldr: This work argues that closing this gap requires alignment at every level of the pipeline, including execution, supervision, optimization, and evaluation, rather than scale alone, and presents Wuying-Browser-Agent, a unified framework that addresses each of these levels.

title: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
proposal_tldr: Experiments show that UI-Mate-27B sets a new open-weight state of the art on general computer-use benchmarks, substantially improving long-horizon reliability, and makes three contributions to an environment-grounded training stack with in-context demonstration learning.

title: CoAdapt-GUI: Joint Workflow Context and Policy Adaptation for Unseen GUI Applications
proposal_tldr: This work introduces CoAdapt-GUI, a test-time adaptation framework that jointly adapts structured workflow context and policy from the agent's own target-app rollouts and rewards, and shows that transfer-constrained workflow context provides substantial gains and that joint policy adaptation further improves held-out performance.

title: Tangent: An Empirical Study of Testing Practices for LLM-Based Agent Applications
proposal_tldr: This paper constructs a large-scale dataset of agent applications, tools, and tests, and manually label 2,572 test methods from 240 modules, and derives a taxonomy of 23 testing patterns across test fixtures, data, objectives, and assertions, and characterize tests by level.

title: Parallelizing LLM Agent Execution with Contrastive Task Allocation
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: Experiments on tool-augmented agent workloads show that CoAct improves per-step execution efficiency and resource utilization while achieving competitive or superior task accuracy, demonstrating that contrastive online dispatch can expose substantial parallelism in LLM-agent workflows without retraining the underlying model.

title: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Web agents observe a browser through text, pixels, or both, and the choice is usually fixed once for all tasks, so a stronger agent can overturn the result, and the rerun noise bands and the full measurement protocol are reported.

title: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: It is found that having a tool available does not settle which way the effect goes, and the adoption gap is called the adoption gap.

title: Strategic Evaluation of Planning Strategies for LLM Agents in Cyber-Physical Systems
proposal_tldr: A controlled, physics-grounded benchmark built around planning-induced control trajectories: the ordered planning operations and directives through which an execution architecture acts on other agents and the physical process is introduced.

title: Invisible Ink Threats: Adversarial Goals Behind Legitimate Tasks in Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: I-Bench, a collection of seemingly harmless adversarial tasks targeting confidentiality and integrity attacks across three platforms, and HITLCUA, a comprehensive adversarial testing framework that integrates a real virtual machine operating system environment with isolated Docker-based web platforms, and simulates human participation by allowing CUAs to consult an API-simulated user before proceeding with suspicious operations.

title: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
