proposal_tldr: This work presents Echoverse, which compiles specifications into stateful applications whose tasks are graded against the application's own database, and a co-evolution loop that reads every graded rollout twice: as repairs to the environment, its tasks and its verifier, and as training signal for the model.

title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
proposal_tldr: OmegaUse-OfficeVal is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on long-horizon office-suite tasks with task-level economic grounding, and code-based verifiers from fine-grained rubrics are developed to support stable evaluation.

title: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: Sidekick significantly improved multitasking performance with CUAs compared to baseline systems that presented textual feedback either in a typical chat or in an ambient display, and discussed implications for long-horizon human-agent collaboration.

title: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
proposal_tldr: EvoGUI is introduced, a diagnostic framework that converts normalized GUI trajectories into three complementary visual question answering probes: temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and contrastive one-step successor discrimination.

title: Do Generative AI Assistants Respect robots.txt? Tracing Web Access Beyond Visible Answers
proposal_tldr: It is found that retrieval behavior and answer correctness can diverge: assistants may access pages without surfacing the retrieved content, or fail to access even allowed resources, raising broader legal and governance concerns about whether AI-assisted web access adequately respects content owners' rights and restrictions.

title: DevicesWorld: Benchmarking Cross-Device Agents in Heterogeneous Environments
proposal_tldr: DirsWorld turns cross-device collaborative operation into an executable, reproducible, and diagnostically useful evaluation problem for research on reliable cross-device agents, and evaluates five frontier LLM-agent systems on a fixed evaluation set.

title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
proposal_tldr: KnowAct-GUIClaw is introduced, a novel Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework designed to address OpenClaw's GUI manipulation deficits and break through its cross-platform and recursive self-improvement constraints, and achieves superior efficiency, accuracy and cross-platform adaptability.

title: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
proposal_tldr: Enter--Propagation--Recovery (E-P-R), a trajectory-level framework that asks where memory first changes an action, whether that change carries forward, and whether the agent can recover after leaving a correct path is proposed, to diagnose how models consume retrieved memory across a multi-step action trajectory.

title: Prismata: Confining Cross-Site Prompt Injection in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Prismata is presented, a defense enforcing contextual least privilege for web agents, constraining both what the agent sees and what it can do, and substantially reduces attack success while preserving benign task utility.

title: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
proposal_tldr: WebRetriever is introduced, a large-scale benchmark encompassing 800 websites and 1,550 tasks across diverse domains, including consumer, professional, and enterprise sectors, with comprehensive coverage of user intent patterns, and NavEval (Navigation Evaluation), a novel LLM-as-Judge framework that leverages rich interaction context beyond visual screenshots.

title: EvoCUA-1.5: Online Reinforcement Learning for Multi-turn Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: EvoCUA-1.5 extends self-evolving computer-use agents from offline experience learning to online reinforcement learning, where policies interact with executable sandbox environments and improve from verifiable task outcomes and provides a practical framework for scaling online RL in multi-turn computer-use agents.

title: Knowledge-augmented form-filling agent for higher education services
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
proposal_tldr: Experiments on public recruitment forms show that KAFA improves field matching and end-to-end form completion across different complexity levels, demonstrating the potential of combining large language models with structured, vector, and graph-based knowledge for robust form filling in education-oriented web services.

title: SovereignPA-Bench: Evaluating User-Owned Personal Agents under Evolving Intent, Platform Mediation, and Consent Constraints
proposal_tldr: SovereignPA-Bench is introduced, a controlled benchmark of whether such an agent follows the user's current intent, resists steering, shares only what a service needs, asks before exceeding its authority, asks before exceeding its authority, and reports truthfully.

title: FORGE: Research-Trajectory Hijacking Attacks on Deep Research Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents FORGE (Fabricated Orchestrated Reasoning chain for aGent Exploitation), a two-level attack that combines intra-document reasoning fabrication with inter-document chain coordination to hijack subtask planning.

title: OrchestrXR: A Multi-Agent System for Idea-to-Prototype XR Study Authoring
proposal_tldr: OstrXR supports a controllable workflow across study design, scene generation, and interaction generation through structured schemas, multi-agent orchestration, and interactive human-agent interfaces, producing a Unity-based prototype from a researcher's idea.

title: KC-Agent: A Dual-Process Cognitive Architecture for Efficient ML Model Improvement
venue: Annual International Computer Software and Applications Conference
proposal_tldr: KC-Agent is presented, a dual-process cognitive architecture for automated ML model improvement that combines fast pattern recognition with deliberate incremental updates that implements structured memory systems enabling System 1 to leverage successful solutions previously discovered by System 2, achieving efficient pattern-based responses without costly recomputation.

title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources
proposal_tldr: RESOURCE2SKILL is presented, a framework that distills multimodal resources, including tutorial videos, repositories, articles, and reference artifacts, into executable skills for software agents, and confirms the value of multimodal skill format, hierarchical organization, source diversity, selection strategy, and online acquisition.

title: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
proposal_tldr: This work introduces the Agent-Computer Observation Interface (AOI), a model-agnostic perception layer that decouples continuous, adaptive observation from discrete actions through three gated components: inter-step keyframe capture, volume-gated audio transcription, and CU-model-generated visual narration that persists as text.

title: When Search Agents Should Ask: DiscoBench for Clarification-Aware Deep Search
proposal_tldr: DiscoBench is introduced, a benchmark for clarification-aware deep search, designed to evaluate whether search agents can proactively identify ambiguity, ask effective clarification questions, and recover correct reasoning paths through user interaction.

title: Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap: An Execute-Distill-Verify Paradigm for Agentic Experience Learning
proposal_tldr: Results show EDV consistently outperforms strong baselines, validating that reliable experience construction is essential for robust agent self-evolution.

title: EvoClawBench: Can Agents Learn Reusable Skills from Their Own Runs?
proposal_tldr: EvoClawBench results indicate that learning reusable skills from an agent's own runs is selective and cost-sensitive, rather than an automatic benefit of adding skill authoring to an agent loop.

title: CalVerT: Augmenting Agents with Calibrated Verifier Telemetry Improves Action and Learning in Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
proposal_tldr: CalVerT raises F1 by triggering retrieval in cases where agents over-rely on parametric knowledge, while cutting redundant retrieval in cases where agents have sufficient context to answer and can augment existing QA frameworks without training.

title: Beyond Static Endpoints: Tool Programs as an Interface for Flexible Agentic Web Services
proposal_tldr: This work presents ToolPro, which represents an agent's tool intent as an executable tool program that compactly encodes multi-step service interactions with explicit effect types, and instantiate ToolPro over MCP-style services with WebAssembly sandboxing and evaluates it on diverse workflows of real-world applications.

title: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
proposal_tldr: This work presents HANSEL (Highlighting Agent Navigation Steps as Evidence Links), a system that extracts interactive, verifiable evidence from web-agent trajectories and demonstrates that reframing verification as an interactive activity, rather than passive consumption of agent explanations, leads to more efficient human oversight of AI agents.

title: OpenRath: Session-Centered Runtime State for Agent Systems
proposal_tldr: The central thesis is that Session provides agent systems with a first-class runtime value for auditable composition, limited to controlled runtime properties, while broad quantitative comparisons, live-provider quality, optional-backend availability, and memory quality are left for follow-on evaluation.

title: When Web Agents Finish but Still Fail: Reproducible Triggers and Trace Diagnostics for Parallel Web Exploration
proposal_tldr: Results show that synthetic-data GRPO reduces abstention and improves partial correctness, but leaves a completion-correctness gap that requires evidence-grounded coverage and synthesis diagnostics.

title: LabOSBench: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents for Scientific Instrument Control
proposal_tldr: This work introduces LabOSBench, a challenging benchmark for multimodal GUI agents built on a suite of web-based scientific-instrument simulators that provides a reproducible, low-cost testbed for advancing computer-using agents toward scientific-instrument control.

title: UXBench: Measuring the Actionability of LLM-Generated UX Critiques
proposal_tldr: UXBench is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs as interaction-grounded UX judges and shows that UX judging is neither saturated nor one dimensional: models differ meaningfully in report actionability.

title: OSGuard: A Benchmark for Safety in Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: OSGuard is introduced, a dual-granularity benchmark suite for evaluating safety in computer-use agents under benign, unchanged user instructions that enables more precise diagnosis of whether models can both recognize unsafe proposed actions and improve full-task safety when deployed as guardrails.

title: Speculative Rollback Correction for Quality-Diverse Web Agent Imitation
proposal_tldr: Speculative Rollback Correction (SRC) is proposed, a branch-level imitation framework for resettable agent environments that uses fixed-horizon branch review and improves the recovery-versus-query tradeoff over step-level review while retaining verifier-passing solution variants.

title: WebChallenger: A Reliable and Efficient Generalist Web Agent
proposal_tldr: WebChallenger is introduced, a web agent framework that addresses each gap through architecture design rather than model scale, built around PageMem, a structured page representation deterministically constructed from the DOM that exposes each page as a hierarchy of semantic sections with short summaries.

title: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: HiViG, a History-aware Visually Grounded test-time framework, built around a multimodal critic trained on real GUI trajectories to abstract past interactions into a compact record and to evaluate actions with visual grounding, is introduced.

title: AdMem: Advanced Memory for Task-solving Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a unified and automatic memory framework that integrates semantic, episodic, and procedural memory in a bi-level design combining short-term and long-term stores and highlights the importance of comprehensive, adaptive memory for advancing LLM-based agents.

title: HLL: Can Agents Cross Humanity's Last Line of Verification?
proposal_tldr: Humanity's Last Line of Verification (HLL) is introduced, a controlled benchmark that uses interactive CAPTCHA verification to evaluate whether agents can cross this boundary through grounded, human-like interaction rather than recognition alone.

title: A Primer in Post-Training Reasoning Data: What We Know About How It Works
proposal_tldr: This paper is the first primer to synthesize over 150 key public studies and system reports on post-training reasoning data around four questions: what data objects exist, what makes them useful, how they are constructed, and how they scale.

title: CostGuard: A Cost-Aware Agentic AI Framework for Efficient Enterprise LLM Workflows
venue: 2026 International Conference on Data Science for Cyber-Physical Systems Resilience using Advanced Applications (ICDCA)
proposal_tldr: Agentic AI pipelines compose sequences of large language model (LLM) invocations spanning planning, execution, and review phases, rendering the aggregate monetary outlay unpredictable from any individual call. Existing percall optimisers-cascades and routers-reduce expenditure one invocation at a ti

title: Agent Skills Should Go Beyond Text: The Case for Visual Skills
proposal_tldr: This work proposes an automatic system that converts agent experience into reusable multimodal skills by preserving textual reasoning, spatial references, visual boundaries, and interaction patterns from task trajectories, and experiments show that visual skills consistently outperform text-only skills.

title: "I Strongly Suspect This Website Is a Scam": Benchmarking PII Leakage and Detection without Defense in Autonomous Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper identifies a detection--action gap, which reveals that defenses conditioned on the agent's own recognition of an attack are gating on the wrong signal, motivating output-level interception of outbound submissions that operates independently of the agent's reasoning loop.

title: GTA: Generating Long-horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A scalable framework, GTA, is introduced that integrates crawling, retrieval-based seeding, in-context generation, and automated quality control to produce realistic tasks paired with executable trajectories and is released with reproducible evaluation.

title: Cyclical Entropy Eruption: Entropy Dynamics in Agent Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: This work identifies a previously underexplored phenomenon in agent RL, which is term cyclical entropy eruption, and proposes SEAL (Separation-Enhanced Agent Learning), a lightweight auxiliary loss that separates correct and incorrect trajectories in representation space, directly targeting the root cause of entropy eruption.

title: Do Agents Know What They Can't Do? Evaluating Feasibility Awareness in Tool-Using Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes FeasiGen, an automatic pipeline for constructing infeasible agent tasks by identifying the critical tools required for successful task completion by extracting tool-calling traces from successful executions across multiple agent systems, and masks these tools to automatically transform solvable tasks into infeasible ones.

title: PRO-CUA: Process-Reward Optimization for Computer Use Agents
proposal_tldr: Pro-CUA is proposed, a process-reward optimization framework for training CUAs with iterative step-level reinforcement learning that enables dense and flexible credit assignment without relying on golden answers or offline expert trajectories, while reducing distribution shift by training on the agent's own execution states.

title: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
proposal_tldr: sys is a framework that could produce high-fidelity synthesized interactive environments for GUI agents across platforms with verifiable rewards, suitable for both large-scale evaluation and downstream agent training.

title: Push Your Agent: Measuring and Enforcing Quantitative Goal Persistence in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: Long-horizon language agents can make many plausible local tool calls yet fail to persist until a requested count is actually complete. We study this gap as Quantitative Goal Persistence (QGP): whether an agent keeps working until an external verifier confirms enough distinct valid items. PushBench

title: CaptchaMind: Training CAPTCHA Solvers via Reinforcement Learning with Explicit Reasoning Supervision
proposal_tldr: CaptchaMind, an RL-based solver trained with explicit reasoning process supervision, substantially outperforming all existing methods without closed-source APIs is presented.

title: CutVerse: A Compositional GUI Agents Benchmark for Media Post-Production Editing
proposal_tldr: Cutverse is introduced, a benchmark designed to systematically evaluate autonomous GUI agents in realistic media post-production environments, and a lightweight parser is developed that transforms raw screen recordings and low-level interaction logs into structured, compositional GUI action trajectories with precise grounding.

title: AQuaUI: Visual Token Reduction for GUI Agents with Adaptive Quadtrees
proposal_tldr: AquaUI is proposed, a training-free inference-time token reduction method for GUI agent models that utilizes the non-uniform information density in screenshots and implements AQuaUI, a conditional quadtree algorithm that leverages the continuity between consecutive screenshots within a single request.

title: SimGym: A Framework for A/B Test Simulation in E-Commerce with Traffic-Grounded VLM Agents
proposal_tldr: SimGym, a framework for simulating A/B tests on e-commerce storefronts using vision-language model (VLM) agents operating in a live browser, reduces experimental cycles from weeks to under an hour, enabling rapid experimentation without exposing real buyers to candidate variants.

title: Skim: Speculative Execution for Fast and Efficient Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Across standard web-agent benchmarks paired with three backboneagents (WebVoyager, AgentOccam, BrowserUse), Skim reduces median per-task cost by 1.9x and latency by 33.4% with no accuracy loss.

title: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
proposal_tldr: Across 14 frontier LLMs and four web environments spanning information retrieval and shopping tasks, it is shown that an agent's actions and interaction timings are sufficient to identify the underlying model with up to 96% F1.

title: SimPersona: Learning Discrete Buyer Personas from Raw Clickstreams for Grounded E-Commerce Agents
proposal_tldr: SimPersona is introduced, a novel framework that learns discrete buyer types from historical traffic and exposes them to LLM-based web agents as compact persona tokens and achieves conversion-rate alignment with real buyers, exhibits interpretable behavioral variation across buyer types, and outperforms a baseline with more parameters on goal-oriented shopping tasks.

title: WinDeskGround: A Benchmark for Robust GUI Grounding in Complex Multi-Window Desktop Environments
proposal_tldr: This paper constructs a diverse meta-dataset of 1,356 high-fidelity instruction-target pairs and conducts comprehensive evaluations of five leading MLLMs, demonstrating that while top-tier agents excel in simplified settings, their accuracy declines under partial occlusion.

title: Checkup2Action: A Multimodal Clinical Check-up Report Dataset for Patient-Oriented Action Card Generation
proposal_tldr: C2A supports systematic study of the balance between coverage, actionable guidance and safe patient communication and measures issue coverage and precision, priority consistency, department and timing accuracy, action complexity, usefulness, readability and safety.

title: A Closed-Loop Modular Language Agent with Step Verification and Local Correction for Multi-Step Task Solving
proposal_tldr: The proposed closed-loop modular language agent framework integrating task planning, action execution, step verification, local regeneration, and replanning improves process stability and recovery capability in multi-step task solving.

title: EvoMAS: Learning Execution-Time Workflows for Multi-Agent Systems
proposal_tldr: EvoMAS is a framework for execution-time multi-agent workflow construction that outperforms single-agent baselines and recent automated multi-agent workflow design methods, and analyses show that explicit task-state construction and learned workflow adaptation provide complementary benefits.

title: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Region4Web, a framework that reorganizes the AXTree into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction, exposing the page's functional organization as the basis for page state understanding and proposes PageDigest, a web-specific inference pipeline that delivers this region-level observation to the actor agent as a compact per-page digest that persists across steps.

title: SafeHarbor: Hierarchical Memory-Augmented Guardrail for LLM Agent Safety
proposal_tldr: This work proposes SafeHarbor, a novel framework designed to establish precise decision boundaries for LLM agents, and designs a local hierarchical memory system for dynamic rule injection, offering a training-free, efficient, and plug-and-play solution.

title: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: This work proposes AutoFocus, a training-free, uncertainty-aware active visual search framework for GUI grounding, and generates global and local region proposals and introduces Shape-Aware Zooming to balance tight localization with contextual preservation.

title: Planner Matters! An Efficient and Unbalanced Multi-agent Collaboration Framework for Long-horizon Planning
proposal_tldr: A planner-centric reinforcement learning approach is introduced, which exclusively optimizes the planner using trajectory-level rewards from a VLM-as-judge, while freezing the other components in a systematic compute-allocation analysis.

title: AutoSurfer - Teaching Web Agents through Comprehensive Surfing, Learning, and Modeling
proposal_tldr: This work presents AutoSurfer, a comprehensive web trajectory generator that addresses limitations through three key innovations, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods - Explorer, OS-Genesis, and SynthAgent - achieving up to 24.23% overall task completion accuracy.

title: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
proposal_tldr: This work presents DynamicUI, an agent designed for dynamic interfaces, which takes screen-recording videos of the interaction process as input and consists of three components: a dynamic perceiver, a refinement strategy, and a reflection.

title: PolicyBank: Evolving Policy Understanding for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: PolicyBank is proposed, a memory mechanism that maintains structured, tool-level policy insights and iteratively refines them -- unlike existing memory mechanisms that treat the policy as immutable ground truth, reinforcing"compliant but wrong"behaviors.

title: The Amazing Agent Race: Strong Tool Users, Weak Navigators
proposal_tldr: The compositional structure of AAR reveals that agents fail not at calling tools but at navigating to the right pages, a blind spot invisible to linear benchmarks.

title: WebSP-Eval: Evaluating Web Agents on Website Security and Privacy Tasks
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WebSP-Eval, an evaluation framework for measuring web agent performance on website security and privacy tasks, and identifies stateful UI elements are a primary reason for agent failure.

title: Aligning Progress and Feasibility: A Neuro-Symbolic Dual Memory Framework for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: A Neuro-Symbolic Dual Memory Framework that explicitly decouples semantic progress guidance from logical feasibility verification and significantly outperforms existing competitive baselines on ALFWorld, WebShop, and TextCraft, while drastically reducing the invalid action rate and average trajectory length.

title: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
proposal_tldr: OmniGUI is introduced, the first step-level benchmark designed to evaluate GUI agents in omni-modal smartphone environments, and foundational omni-modal models capable of natively processing interleaved inputs are selected to serve as agent proxies for the initial baselines.

title: VACP: Visual Analytics Context Protocol
proposal_tldr: The Visual Analytics Context Protocol (VACP), a framework designed to make VA applications "agent-ready" that extends generic protocols by explicitly exposing application state, available interactions, and mechanisms for direct execution, is introduced.

title: InconLens: Interactive Visual Diagnosis of Behavioral Inconsistencies in LLM-based Agentic Systems
proposal_tldr: InconLens is introduced, a visual analytics system designed to support interactive diagnosis of LLM-based agentic systems with a particular focus on cross-run behavioral analysis and enables developers to more efficiently identify divergence points, uncover latent failure modes, and gain actionable insights into improving the reliability and stability of agentic systems.

title: TRUST-CUA: Trustworthy Computer-Using Generalist Agents for Intelligent User Interfaces (Workshop)
proposal_tldr: This workshop aims to produce an IUI-oriented checklist for trustworthy CUA interaction design, a shared evaluation profile (“CUBench-IUI”), and a curated set of design patterns and open research challenges to guide the next year of IUI research on agentic systems.

title: LiveWeb-IE: A Benchmark For Online Web Information Extraction
proposal_tldr: This study introduces \dataset, a new benchmark designed for evaluating WIE systems directly against live websites, and proposes Visual Grounding Scraper (VGS), a novel multi-stage agentic framework that mimics human cognitive processes by visually narrowing down web page content to extract desired information.

title: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: Results show that video-execution reward modeling can serve as a scalable, model-agnostic evaluator for CUAs, and design spatiotemporal token pruning, which removes homogeneous regions and persistent tokens while preserving decisive UI changes.

title: UIS-Digger: Towards Comprehensive Research Agent Systems for Real-world Unindexed Information Seeking
proposal_tldr: This work introduces UIS-QA, the first dedicated UIS benchmark, comprising 110 expert-annotated QA pairs, and proposes UIS-Digger, a novel multi-agent framework that incorporates dual-mode browsing and enables simultaneous webpage searching and file parsing.

title: Behind the Prompt: The Agent-User Problem in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: This work investigates the agent-user problem through a large-scale corpus from an agent-native social platform: 370K posts from 47K agents across 4K communities, finding that individual agent actions cannot be classified as autonomous or operator-directed from observables.

title: "When to Hand Off, When to Work Together": Understanding Concurrent Human-Agent Interaction in Shared Co-Creative Workspaces
proposal_tldr: A decision model and five design implications for concurrent human-agent collaboration are presented and a second probe is developed that tracks user actions and selectively updates its plan.

title: Caesar: Deep Agentic Web Exploration for Creative Answer Synthesis
proposal_tldr: To advance from passive retrieval to creative discovery of new ideas, autonomous agents must be capable of deep, associative synthesis. However, current agentic frameworks prioritize convergent search, often resulting in derivative summaries that lack creativity. Caesar is an agentic architecture de

title: The Headless Firm: How AI Reshapes Enterprise Boundaries
proposal_tldr: The claim that agentic AI induces a structural change in how coordination costs scale is formalized as a coordination cost model with two falsifiable empirical predictions: the marginal cost of adding an execution provider should be approximately constant in a mature hourglass ecosystem; the ratio of total coordination cost to task throughput should remain stable as ecosystem size grows.

title: Training-Free Agentic AI: Probabilistic Control and Coordination in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
venue: Annual International Computer Software and Applications Conference
proposal_tldr: ReDeRef (Recursive Delegation and Reflection), a lightweight, training-free control framework that improves agent selection and routing decisions during recursive delegation in multi-agent LLM systems without training or fine-tuning, is introduced.

title: Tuning Qwen2.5-VL to Improve Its Web Interaction Skills
proposal_tldr: This work fine-tunes Qwen2.5-VL-32B, one of the strongest open-source VLMs available, and focuses on improving its reliability in web-based control, and increases success rates from 86% to 94% under the most challenging setting.

title: LLM-WikiRace Benchmark: How Far Can LLMs Plan over Real-World Knowledge Graphs?
proposal_tldr: LLM-Wikirace is a simple benchmark that reveals clear limitations in current reasoning systems, offering an open arena where planning-capable LLMs still have much to prove, and shows that world knowledge is a necessary ingredient for success, but only up to a point.

title: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
proposal_tldr: A novel MLLM-centered framework for GUI agents, which consists of agentic-Q estimation and step-wise policy optimization, which endows Ovis2.5-9B with powerful GUI interaction capabilities, achieving remarkable performances on GUI navigation and grounding benchmarks and even surpassing contenders with larger scales.

title: To Think or Not To Think, That is The Question for Large Reasoning Models in Theory of Mind Tasks
proposal_tldr: It is concluded that achieving robust ToM requires developing unique capabilities beyond existing reasoning methods, as well as two intervention approaches: Slow-to-Fast adaptive reasoning and Think-to-Match shortcut prevention to further verify and mitigate the problems.

title: See, Plan, Snap: Evaluating Multimodal GUI Agents in Scratch
proposal_tldr: This work introduces ScratchWorld, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal GUI agents on program-by-construction tasks in Scratch, and proposes an execution-based evaluation protocol that validates the functional correctness of the constructed Scratch programs through runtime tests within the browser environment.

title: Spider-Sense: Intrinsic Risk Sensing for Efficient Agent Defense with Hierarchical Adaptive Screening
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Spider-Sense framework, an event-driven defense framework based on Intrinsic Risk Sensing (IRS), which allows agents to maintain latent vigilance and trigger defenses only upon risk perception, and introduces S$^2$Bench, a lifecycle-aware benchmark featuring realistic tool execution and multi-stage attacks.

title: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: ToolTok is proposed, a novel paradigm of multi-step pathfinding for GUI agents, where operations are modeled as a sequence of progressive tool usage, and introduces a semantic anchoring mechanism that grounds each tool with semantically related concepts as natural inductive bias.

title: MalURLBench: A Benchmark Evaluating Agents' Vulnerabilities When Processing Web URLs
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: This work proposes MalURLBench, the first benchmark for evaluating LLMs' vulnerabilities to malicious URLs and proposes URLGuard, a lightweight defense module that identifies and analyzes key factors that impact attack success rates and proposes URLGuard, a lightweight defense module.

title: From User Interface to Agent Interface: Efficiency Optimization of UI Representations for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: UIFormer is the first automated optimization framework that synthesizes UI transformation programs by conducting constraint-based optimization with structured decomposition of the complex synthesis task, and is presented as a lightweight plugin that applies transformation programs for seamless integration with existing LLM agents, requiring minimal modifications to their core logic.

title: Reflecting with Two Voices: A Co-Adaptive Dual-Strategy Framework for LLM-Based Agent Decision Making
proposal_tldr: DuSAR (Dual-Strategy Agent with Reflecting) is proposed -- a demonstration-free framework that enables a single frozen LLM to perform co-adaptive reasoning via two complementary strategies: a high-level holistic plan and a context-grounded local policy.

title: SelfCorrect-Agent: Toward robust and generalizable LLM-based agents
Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents
proposal_tldr: PRAXIS enables the practical adoption of AI agents in fast-evolving stateful environments by helping them learn new procedures effectively and shows preliminary generalization to unseen tasks in similar environments.

title: DigiData: Training and Evaluating General-Purpose Mobile Control Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper introduces DigiData, a large-scale, high-quality, diverse, multi-modal dataset designed for training mobile control agents, and proposes dynamic evaluation protocols and AI-powered evaluations as rigorous alternatives for agent assessment.

title: Can Agent Conquer Web? Exploring the Frontiers of ChatGPT Atlas Agent in Web Games
proposal_tldr: An early evaluation of Atlas's web interaction capabilities using browser-based games as test scenarios, including Google's T-Rex Runner, Sudoku, Flappy Bird, and Stein suggests that while Atlas demonstrates capable analytical processing, there remain notable limitations in dynamic web environments requiring real-time interaction.

title: WebGen-V Bench: Structured Representation for Enhancing Visual Design in LLM-based Web Generation and Evaluation
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: WebGen-V is the first work to enable high-granularity agentic crawling and evaluation for instruction-to-HTML generation, providing a unified pipeline from real-world data acquisition and webpage generation to structured multimodal assessment.

title: GUIrilla: A Scalable Framework for Automated Desktop UI Exploration
proposal_tldr: GUIRILLA is introduced, a scalable data crawling framework for automated exploration of desktop GUIs that systematically collects realistic interaction traces and accessibility metadata intended to support the training, evaluation, and stabilization of downstream foundation models and GUI agents.

title: WARC-Bench: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
proposal_tldr: This work introduces WARC-Bench (Web Archive Benchmark), a novel web navigation benchmark featuring 438 tasks designed to evaluate multimodal AI agents on subtasks, and explores two common training techniques: supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

title: Creative Adversarial Testing (CAT): A Novel Framework for Evaluating Goal-Oriented Agentic AI Systems
proposal_tldr: The Creative Adversarial Testing (CAT) framework is introduced, a novel approach designed to capture and analyze the complex relationship between Agentic AI tasks and the system's intended objectives, enabling more effective optimization and development of Agentic AI systems.

title: TGPO: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization for Robust Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
proposal_tldr: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization (TGPO), an offline reinforcement learning framework that proposes a tree-structured trajectory representation merging semantically identical states across trajectories to eliminate label conflicts, is proposed.

title: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: A modular evaluation framework is proposed that decomposes agent pipelines into interpretable stages for detailed error analysis and shows how this approach reveals actionable weaknesses missed by standard metrics - paving the way for more robust and generalizable web agents.

title: AIssistant: Human-AI Collaborative Review and Perspective Research Workflows in Data Science
venue: Pacific-Asia Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
proposal_tldr: This work introduces AIssistant, the first open-source agentic framework for Human--AI collaborative generation of scientific perspectives and review research in data science, demonstrating that agent-augmented pipelines substantially reduce effort while maintaining research integrity through strategic human oversight.

title: Bridging the Capability Gap: Joint Alignment Tuning for Harmonizing LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
proposal_tldr: Theoretical analysis proves that MOAT ensures a non-decreasing and progressively convergent training process, and experiments demonstrate that MOAT outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving average improvements on held-in tasks and held-out tasks.

title: Cybernaut: Towards Reliable Web Automation
proposal_tldr: Cybernaut is presented, a novel framework to ensure high execution consistency in web automation agents designed for robust enterprise use, enabling reliable confidence assessment and adaptive guidance during task execution in real-world systems.

title: Cognitive Duality for Adaptive Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Inspired by the dual-process theory of human cognition, a principled decomposition into fast System 1 and slow System 2 cognitive processes is derived, which provides a unifying perspective on existing web agent methodologies, bridging the gap between offline learning of intuitive reactive behaviors and online acquisition of deliberative planning capabilities.

title: Efficient Morphology-Aware Policy Transfer to New Embodiments
proposal_tldr: This work investigates combining morphology-aware pretraining with parameter efficient finetuning techniques to help reduce the learnable parameters necessary to specialize a morphology-aware policy to a target embodiment and finds that tuning as few as less than 1% of total parameters will improve policy performance compared the zero-shot performance of the base pretrained a policy.

title: WebDS: An End-to-End Benchmark for Web-based Data Science
proposal_tldr: WebDS is introduced, the first end-to-end web-based data science benchmark, challenging agents to perform complex, multi-step, tool-based operations, across heterogeneous data formats, to better reflect the realities of modern data analytics.

title: ASPERA: A Simulated Environment to Evaluate Planning for Complex Action Execution
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: ASERA, a framework comprising an assistant library simulation and a human-assisted LLM data generation engine, allows developers to guide LLM generation of high-quality tasks consisting of complex user queries, simulation state and corresponding validation programs, tackling data availability and evaluation robustness challenges.

title: iPanda: An LLM-based Agent for Automated Conformance Testing of Communication Protocols
proposal_tldr: ianda is proposed, the first framework that leverages LLMs to automate protocol conformance testing and significantly outperforms pure LLM-based approaches, improving the success rate of test-program generation by factors ranging from 4.675 times to 10.751 times.

title: WebArxiv: A Reproducible Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Web Agents on arXiv Tasks
proposal_tldr: WebArxiv is introduced, a static-snapshot benchmark comprising 510 time-invariant tasks, each with a unique deterministic ground truth, to equip foundation-model-based web agents with a lightweight dynamic-memory mechanism for adaptive retrieval and reasoning over relevant context.

title: How Far are We From Generating Missing Modalities With Foundation Models?
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
proposal_tldr: This work identifies and formalizes three potential paradigms for missing modality reconstruction, and performs a comprehensive evaluation across these paradigms, covering 42 model variants in terms of reconstruction accuracy and adaptability to downstream tasks.

title: Towards Sustainable Web Agents: A Plea for Transparency and Dedicated Metrics for Energy Consumption
proposal_tldr: An initial exploration of the energy and CO2 cost associated with web agents is provided and it is shown how different philosophies in web agent creation can severely impact the associated expended energy.

title: PAFFA: Premeditated Actions For Fast Agents
proposal_tldr: PAFFA (Premeditated Actions For Fast Agents), a method that makes LLMs faster and more accurate in completing tasks on the internet using a novel inference-time technique that requires no task-specific training, is introduced.

title: From Context to Action: Analysis of the Impact of State Representation and Context on the Generalization of Multi-Turn Web Navigation Agents
proposal_tldr: This work investigates the optimization of context management, focusing on the influence of interaction history and web page representation, and highlights improved agent performance across out-of-distribution scenarios, including unseen websites, categories, and geographic locations through effective context management.

title: ML Research Benchmark
proposal_tldr: A novel benchmark is introduced and evaluates it using agent scaffolds powered by frontier models, including Claude-3 and GPT-4o, indicating that the Claude-3.5 Sonnet agent performs best across the authors' benchmark, excelling in planning and developing machine learning models.

title: Will the Inclusion of Generated Data Amplify Bias Across Generations in Future Image Classification Models?
proposal_tldr: This work investigates the effects of the generated data on image classification tasks, with a specific focus on bias, and develops a practical simulation environment that integrates a self-consuming loop, where the generative model and classification model are trained synergistically.

title: A Survey on Complex Tasks for Goal-Directed Interactive Agents
proposal_tldr: This survey compiles relevant tasks and environments for evaluating goal-directed interactive agents, structuring them along dimensions relevant for understanding current obstacles.

title: SYNERGAI: Perception Alignment for Human-Robot Collaboration
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
proposal_tldr: SYNERGAI is a unified system designed to achieve both perceptual alignment and human-robot collaboration and incorporates an automatic mechanism that enables perceptual misalignment correction with users by updating its 3DSG with online interaction.

title: RealWeb: A Benchmark for Universal Instruction Following in Realistic Web Services Navigation
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
proposal_tldr: Traditional methods of interacting with web pages, such as clicking and scrolling, greatly hinder users, especially those with disabilities and the elderly from conveniently accessing web services. By following user instructions, automatic web service navigation agents accomplish complex tasks on th

title: Equipping Transformer with Random-Access Reading for Long-Context Understanding
proposal_tldr: This work proposes $\textbf{random access}$, a novel reading strategy that enables transformers to efficiently process long documents without examining every token, and Experimental results from pretraining, fine-tuning, and inference phases validate the efficacy of the method.

title: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for Computer-Use Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Do GUI Grounders Truly Understand UI Elements?
venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: Agent-Ops: A Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework for End-to-End SOP Automation in E-Commerce Operations
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: Use across 100 Account Managers validates that LLM-based agents achieve enterprise-grade reliability when augmented with robust web automation, comprehensive document understanding, and systematic SOP refinement.

title: RetailBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Autonomous Decision-Making and Strategy Stability of LLM Agents in Realistic Retail Environments
proposal_tldr: The Evolving Strategy & Execution framework is proposed, which separates high-level strategic reasoning from low-level action execution, enabling adaptive and inter-pretable strategy evolution over time, and improves operational stability and efficiency compared to other baselines.

title: Web Sitemap Knowledge Can Enhance Autonomous Browsing
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

title: JARVIS or Ultron? A Survey on the Safety and Security Threats of Computer-Using Agents
venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
proposal_tldr: A systematization of knowledge is presented on the safety and security threats of CUAs that provides future researchers with a structured foundation for exploring un-explored vulnerabilities and offers practitioners actionable guidance in designing and deploying secure Computer-Using Agents.

title: PUO-Bench: A Panel Understanding and Operation Benchmark with A Privacy-Preserving Framework
proposal_tldr: A Panel Understanding and Operation (PUO) benchmark, comprising annotated panel images from appliances and associated vision-language instruction pairs, and a Privacy-Preserving Framework (PPF) to address privacy concerns in cloud-based panel parsing and reasoning are proposed.

title: Realistic Environmental Injection Attacks on GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Chameleon, an attack framework with two main novelties that automatically generates diverse and high-fidelity webpage simulations, enabling robustness against dynamic visual contexts and transforms attention weights into explicit supervisory signals that guide the agent’s focus toward the trigger region, mitigating the difficulty caused by its limited visual prominence.

title: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: It is shown that domain-general automatic evaluators can significantly improve the performance of agents for web navigation and device control and are used to improve the performance of existing agents via fine-tuning and inference-time guidance.

title: PADRE: Pseudo-Likelihood based Alignment of Diffusion Language Models
proposal_tldr: The proposed framework (PADRE) uses a novel objective pseudo-likelihood based objective for alignment of dLLMs that has the same optima as PGRL based optimization, but does not need to evaluate likelihood from dLLMs.

title: SoK: Frontier AI’s Impact on the Cybersecurity Landscape
proposal_tldr: An in-depth analysis of frontier AI’s impact on cybersecurity and a systematic framework for risk assessment and mitigation is established and long-term research questions essential for understanding AI’s future impacts and unleashing its defensive capabilities are presented.

title: OpenFlo: Automated UX Evaluation via Simulated Human Web Interaction with GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: OpenFlo is presented, a user-experience evaluation agent that simulates user behavior on websites and produces standardized usability testing, enabling it to interact with real web pages end-to-end while maintaining a coherent trace of the user journey.

title: Reasoning Is More Than the Model: Harness-Aware Evaluation of Agents on Verifiable Reasoning Tasks
proposal_tldr: AlphaDiana moves agent evaluation beyond asking whether a system succeeds toward explaining why a model-harness system succeeds or fails, and standardizes models, harnesses, benchmarks, execution environments, scorers, budgets, and trajectory logging, enabling controlled comparisons across both models and harnesses.

title: From the Wild Web to the Z OO : A Realistic Environment for Evaluating Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Z OO is introduced, a simulated web environment that enables realistic workflows across multiple interconnected web applications — including email, identity management, e-commerce platforms, collaborative tools, and web analytics — within a single network that provides full access to backend state and supports deterministic re-initialization.

title: "Stop trying to make fetch happen": Towards a Modality-Aware Understanding of Unnecessary Resources on the Web
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM Internet Measurement Conference
proposal_tldr: This paper provides the first modality-aware measurement of unnecessary resources on the web and introduces four dimensions of webpage fidelity to characterize modalities on the web, estimating that modality-aware selective loading could avoid up to 159 million metric tons of CO2e annually.

title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
proposal_tldr: It is argued that failure knowledge is conditional knowledge and should be conditionally exposed, and this principle is instantiated in Sentry, a failure-management layer that runs alongside the agent.

title: MCRI: A Four-Dimensional Framework for Analyzing and Evaluating Agent Skills
proposal_tldr: Results indicate that MCRI-Eval provides a useful pre-execution signal for prioritizing promising skills before costly execution-based evaluation, and improves top-1 skill selection across all three benchmarks.

title: AgentBreaker: Evaluating Context-Aware Indirect Prompt Injection Risks in Modern Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper presents AgentBreaker, an IPI attack framework that autonomously composes adversarial phrases tailored to page-specific context that outperforms existing IPI frameworks, thereby accurately evaluating web agents’ susceptibility to IPI and providing stepping stones for countering this emerging threat.

title: Characterizing and Repairing Obsolete Android GUI Tests under UI Evolution
proposal_tldr: GUIRevive, an automated GUI test repair approach that addresses semantic ambiguity in widget identification and target unreachability under UI evolution by integrating semantic-aware reasoning, functionality-preserving validation, and goal-guided UI exploration is proposed.

title: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
proposal_tldr: Final scores alone provide an incomplete account of web agent behavior and motivate human grounded, trajectory aware verification, and step level evidence shows that substantial early progress can coexist with a final failure.

title: DeskForge: Dense Supervision from Desktop Environments for Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: DerekForge is introduced, a controllable desktop environment that composes and explores real applications to generate large-scale supervision for computer-use agents and shows that controllable composition of real desktop environments provides a scalable source of supervision for improving both GUI grounding and long-horizon computer use.

title: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
proposal_tldr: This work argues that GUI agents should not pursue perfect knowledge but learn to act correctly under imperfect priors, and proposes a framework that couples knowledge acquisition with noise-robust utilization that more effectively rejects erroneous priors while leveraging correct ones.

title: ActionGuard: Tool Call Authorization under Poisoned Skills
proposal_tldr: Results show that execution-boundary authorization grounded in trusted user intent and runtime evidence can restrict unauthorized Tool Calls induced by skill injection, while maintaining high benign-task completion.

title: cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: Computer use agents (CUAs), which use graphical user interfaces (GUIs) to complete tasks on a computer, have recently surpassed human performance on many standard benchmarks, including difficult long-horizon tasks. Their capabilities are undoubtedly impressive, however, a key barrier to the widespre

title: Measuring AI-Agent Accessibility of Web Applications: A Construct-Development Framework
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science, Communication and Technology
proposal_tldr: The Agent Accessibility Measurement Framework (AAMF) is proposed, which defines 25 indicators with explicit formulas, an equal-weight baseline score, a failure-criticality-weighted composite score, and a five-layer Agent Interaction Stack (AIS) that keeps in-page interaction apart from out-of-band discovery.

title: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
proposal_tldr: It is found that correctly inferring user preferences is necessary but not sufficient for task success, as execution failures in downstream web interactions remain a significant bottleneck even when agents align with the target preference.

title: FOCUS: Training-Free Decision-Preserving Context Compression for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper recast context compression as a causal decision preservation problem over discrete interaction units and introduces FOCUS, a training-free context compression framework that operates entirely at test time that requires no offline data collection or fine-tuning.

title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
proposal_tldr: EngiWorld provides the first rigorous foundation for measuring progress toward agents that operate professional engineering software end to end, and introduces an artifact-centric evaluation methodology built on a unified domain-verifier suite.

title: Learning from Viable Failure Prefixes: Milestone Viability Potential Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Milestone Viability Potential Policy Optimization (MVPO), a potential-routed policy optimization algorithm that learns from viable failure prefixes and outperforms eight strong baselines, including GRPO and GiGPO.

title: EnterpriseBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Enterprise-Level Strategic Reasoning and Decision-Making
proposal_tldr: EnterpriseBench is introduced, a benchmark that evaluates LLM agents across this spectrum, from static question answering to dynamic decision-making, and shows that it provides a practical benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in realistic enterprise strategic reasoning and decision-making.

title: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
proposal_tldr: The experiments show that strong performance on general benchmarks does not transfer to professional scientific workflows, and that this gap is not a visual-grounding problem alone: failures arise from domain-specific operational knowledge, sparse pretraining coverage of scientific software, weak cross-tool artifact handoff, and critical states exposed only visually.

title: ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents
proposal_tldr: A novel recommendation agent framework, termed as ReMem, that combines OCR-based multimodal perception with time-evolving dynamic memory, which allows the agent to preserve evolving user preferences without relying on external memory modules or disrupting the standard autoregressive generation process.

title: Actions with Receipts: Jointly Binding Claims, Evidence, and Execution for Replayable Tool-Agent Auditing
proposal_tldr: A claim-anchored execution contract is introduced that jointly binds the emitted claim, its exact source span, the ordered execution prefix that produced it, and the source version and access state observed by that execution.

title: Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models
proposal_tldr: FTA is introduced, a controlled benchmark that fixes the failed observation and required evidence state before generation, making post-failure claims directly auditable and associated with substantially lower post-failure reporting errors while useful-response rates remain high within this blocked-task benchmark.

title: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
proposal_tldr: GUITAR, a state-centric diagnostic framework that performs structured failure analysis over both states and transitions, using a State Transition Graph (STG) by mapping visually diverse screens to shared functional states, demonstrates the diagnostic and actionable value of structure-aware evaluation within the evaluated mobile and web tasks.

title: AX is the New AEO
proposal_tldr: It is argued that AX is the new AEO, and in the agentic web era, being readable beats being talked about, and improving a site's AX is the strongest lever a business has.

title: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles
proposal_tldr: This work introduces LongPuzzleBench, 114 levels in six puzzle games played through native GUI actions, where one objective can take a human over a thousand actions on persistent boards and dead ends go unannounced.

title: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: WebPageBench is an open framework for evaluating web agents in which every task is verified from the interface's own event log, and sensitivity to interface form can be measured under a fixed task specification.

title: LLMs are General Asynchronous Agents
proposal_tldr: This work develops an asynchronous LLM framework that lets users (or the agents themselves) define inference coroutines with overlapping memory states and showcases that Qwen 3.x models are capable of asynchronous operation for streaming video understanding, videogames, and monitoring, without task-specific training.

title: Controlled knowledge updating in memory-enabled AI agents: beyond model editing and recall
proposal_tldr: This work proposes a substrate-aware view of controlled knowledge updating organized by three principles: substrate proportionality, temporal defeasibility, and auditable continuity, which treats knowledge updating as a longitudinal control problem and motivates evaluation criteria that include update selection, temporal consistency, interference, reversibility, efficiency, and robustness.

title: CodeSkill: Latent Skill Abstraction for Long-Horizon Code Agents
proposal_tldr: By shifting RL from token-level exploration to experience-level reasoning, CodeSkill improves optimization efficiency and long-horizon behavioral coherence, highlighting the effectiveness of explicit behavioral abstraction for scalable agentic code generation.

title: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
proposal_tldr: Investigation to Act (P2A) is introduced, an active probing framework for the browser-agent loop that addresses an asymmetric bridge between symbolic DOM hypotheses and screenshot layout by rendering on-demand symbolic DOM structure back into pixels.

title: What Does a Skill Actually Do? Estimands and Evaluation Validity for Tool and Skill Use in LLM Agents: A Critical Review
proposal_tldr: This critical narrative review examines what these evaluations estimate and which conclusions their designs support and provides a methodological synthesis and a reporting checklist to help align claims about tools and skills with the comparisons their evaluation designs support.

title: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
proposal_tldr: SURFPRM is proposed, a graph-guided process preference synthesis framework for comparative Web PRMs that outperforms baseline-trained models on average on WEBPRMBENCH and rival leading proprietary LLMs, and elevates the GMCP proportion from 24.19% to 74.60%, producing the curated SURFPRM-DATA dataset.

title: HM-ROUTER: Joint Model and Harness Routing for Agentic Systems
proposal_tldr: HM-Router is introduced, a routing method that jointly selects a model and harness for each query, with an interaction term inspired by canonical polyadic tensor decomposition to capture how their compatibility varies with the query.

title: CLAIRE: A Schema-Grounded Hybrid Workflow for Healthcare Administrative Form Completion
proposal_tldr: CLAIRE (Clinical Language and Agentic Intelligence for Reasoning and Entry), a hybrid workflow that separates field-state discovery, source-to-field mapping, deterministic validation, bounded correction, escalation, and audit tracing, is developed and evaluated.

title: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: CUA-Sandbox is introduced, which separates private state capsules from shared runtimes through state-scoped execution and transactional lifecycle operations, including resets and branches, while retaining the original software interfaces and task evaluators.

title: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: Findings show that agents often fail to recognize side-channel leakage as a privacy risk, where an agent's actions inadvertently reveal private information retained from a prior website, despite an explicit instruction not to disclose it.

title: StraTune: Adaptive Selection of Revision Operators for Self-Evolving LLM Skills
proposal_tldr: StraTune (strategy-guided skill tuning), which lets a frozen optimizer LLM choose the revision operator at every round from the optimization state, which is defined as the current execution feedback together with the recorded outcomes of earlier strategies and forms.

title: Trust and Task Completion in the World of Consumer AI Agents
proposal_tldr: An evaluation is built that scores trust and completion on the same runs, in a simulated world of businesses with their own websites, inboxes, and phone lines, and of people who write back, to measure Fo, Wajo's personal assistant, against a base model with basic instructions on three foundation models, and against the Fo harness with its guardrails switched off.

title: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: ShareMem is introduced, a memory architecture that shares reusable experience while grounding its application in the receiving user's own preferences, and improves step success, average task success, and dialogue-macro coding scores, respectively, over matched user-local memory across all four models.

title: From Anomalies to Failures: Constructing Causal Error Graphs for Agentic Trace Diagnosis
proposal_tldr: CEG-Agent introduces an explicit taxonomy of anomalies, errors, and failures, and constructs Causal Error Graphs (CEGs), a unified typed representation that links execution events, diagnostic nodes, and failure outcomes through causal relations.

title: MetaPermit: Scalable and Auditable Access Control for AI Agents via LLM-Inferred Meta-Attributes
proposal_tldr: The results show that MetaPermit produces 31% more consistent authorization decisions than LLM-driven authorization and outperforms the state-of-the-art defenses CaMeL and IPIGuard in both task completion and robustness to IPI attacks, with no malicious tool calls executed.

title: AgentXploit: Autonomous Repository-to-Runtime Red-Teaming for AI Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents AgentXploit, a two-role auditing system that separates repository-level attack-path discovery from runtime exploitation and introduces AgentXploit-Bench, containing 72 reproducible vulnerabilities across 12 open-source AI-agent systems and frameworks.

title: A Wrong Turn Does Not Ruin the Journey: Deviation-Guided Skill Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: It is argued that skill self-evolution should identify where productive problem solving begins to break down, rather than reflect coarsely over the entire failure, and proposed SkillPivot, a deviation-point-guided framework for skill self-evolution.

title: The Hard Part Comes After Search: Benchmarking Web Agents on Synthesizing, Organizing, and Displaying Knowledge
proposal_tldr: Existing computer-use agent benchmarks do not fully evaluate agents acting as assistants. A useful assistant retrieves information across complex, multi-step workflows, synthesizes it into artifacts (documents, presentations, spreadsheets), and navigates program interfaces to produce a coherent fina

title: Guides That Cause Actions: An Offline Study of Guide-Action Mutual Reinforcement in Multimodal Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents WebMRE, an offline benchmark of 541 tasks and 5,293 steps derived from successful WebArena trajectories, with fully audited test labels and a deterministic protocol that scores a checkpoint identically on every run without any environment.

title: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction
proposal_tldr: The MaP is proposed, a unified framework that seamlessly harmonizes divergent GUI navigation tasks and effectively mitigates gradient conflicts and significantly outperforms the direct mixture training, establishing a robust paradigm for multi-task GUI navigation.

title: Few-Shot Demonstrations Elicit the Use of In-Context World Representations in LLMs
proposal_tldr: Extending few-shot settings to few-shot settings, where each demonstration is generated from a different world with either the same or different graph topologies, enhances its prediction on 6 models from 4 model families, and finds that few-shot demonstrations relocate the world representation and increase its predictive use.

title: MCPGen: Benchmarking LLMs on Executable MCPWorkflow Development
proposal_tldr: MCPGen is introduced, an executable benchmark for Model Context Protocol (MCP) workflow development that evaluates three diagnostic tasks: workflow reconstruction, tool creation, and backward-compatible workflow extension and evaluates 11 representative LLMs in a single-turn foundation-model setting.

title: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
proposal_tldr: This paper evaluates six strong browser-use agents, three GUI-only agents that see only screenshots, and humans, evaluating the construction of challenging instances from tasks agents already solve, turning difficulty into a programmable property of the environment.

title: Automatic multimodal UX improvement recommendations from LLM agent user simulations
proposal_tldr: AMUSER is presented, a multimodal framework which simulates user behaviour and automatically generates prioritised UX improvement recommendations from resulting data and suggests an asymmetric role of multimodality: visual access during simulation improves recommendations through richer traces, while providing visual inputs during recommendation generation can modestly degrade quality.

title: AutoGym: Blueprint-First Generation of Verifiable Agent Gyms
proposal_tldr: AutoGym is presented, a framework that generates complete gyms (tasks, executable environments, and verifiers) from a minimal domain seed or prior model trajectories, including instances that challenge frontier models.

title: AI Smart Glasses for Wearable Intelligence: From Egocentric Sensing to Agentic Personalization
proposal_tldr: By centering smart glasses as wearable-intelligence platforms, this survey provides a unified framework for organizing technologies, applications, and open challenges in this emerging area.

title: EconSkills: Studying Skill Transfer and Retrieval for Web Agents on Live Economic Data
proposal_tldr: EconSkills is introduced, a skill library and evaluation framework that distills verified EconWebArena trajectories into parameterized standard operating procedures for retrieving live economic data and establishes that reusable economic web procedures can transfer across task instances.

title: RideWay: Benchmarking Efficient Task Completion for Tool-Using Language Agents
proposal_tldr: RideWay makes interaction efficiency measurable alongside task success, while exposing the boundary of count-based tool-use evaluation, together with Efficiency Utility, a success-gated metric that discounts successful trajectories for excess tool calls and user-facing turns relative to task-specific reference effort.

title: A11yLTLNav: Automatic Detection of Accessibility Navigation Failures
proposal_tldr: This work organizes accessibility navigation failures into a failure taxonomy and formalizes a browser-observable subset as executable Linear Temporal Logic properties over action-state traces and transforms accessibility knowledge into reusable checks of interface behavior over time.

title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
proposal_tldr: Affora is presented, a design system that supports both readers and agents while preserving visual freedom and familiar human workflows through a shared interface rather than a separate agent-only surface.

title: ProgramDistill: From Interactive Web Apps to Verifiable Reference-Guided SWE Tasks
proposal_tldr: ProgramDistill is introduced, a benchmark evaluating coding agents on features discovered through interaction with fully functional reference applications, and provides a scalable benchmark with controlled difficulty for evaluating and diagnosing coding agents, and a natural basis for future curriculum-based training.

title: Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning
proposal_tldr: Refinement of multi-modal QA trajectories is proposed, viewing each trajectory as a round-level dependency DAG that exposes which rounds are globally load-bearing for the final answer, and fine-tune agents on trajectories refined through this DAG.

title: AI-augmented ACT-R modeling in real interfaces: automating visual perception, knowledge acquisition, and motor misexecution
proposal_tldr: EvisiTor is an AI-augmented extension of the VisiTor eyes-and-hands tool for ACT-R that automates two forms of work commonly performed by the modeler: perception of the live interface and acquisition of task knowledge, while identifying instruction specificity and individual variability as targets for future work.

title: CADWorld: Computer-Use Benchmark for Long-Horizon Computer-Aided Design
proposal_tldr: It is found that weaker agents often fail before producing a valid artifact, whereas stronger agents increasingly fail on structural, geometric, and construction-process requirements, and CADWorld exposes a gap between general GUI competence and reliable execution of persistent, verifiable engineering workflows.

title: Evaluating Open-Weight E-Commerce Agents with Environment-Grounded Verification
proposal_tldr: A deterministic and reproducible e-commerce environment is built that precommits each trial's customer and trajectory parameters, including the persona, difficulty, target cart, and an item reveal schedule, and the resulting capability profiles distinguish under-action, over-purchase, unsupported product attributes, and poor search.

title: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time
proposal_tldr: This work defines real-time as five measurable properties, each with an equation and a worked example: continuous task arrival, live concurrent execution, online rating updates, freshness with contamination resistance, and bounded feedback latency from a failed run to a reusable training environment.

title: Trustworthy Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Cybersecurity and Systems Survey on Threat Landscapes, Defense Architectures, and Open Challenges
proposal_tldr: This survey systematically analyze threat surfaces across intra-execution loops and interaction planes, formulate a multi-layered zero-trust defense-in-depth architecture integrating Dual-LLM isolation, Capability-Based Access Control, kernel eBPF probes, and sandboxed runtimes, and map technical controls to international AI governance frameworks.

title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: Results show that LifeMem enables effective experience reuse in lifelong learning, achieving both reduced forgetting on learned tasks and superior cross-task transfer.

title: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces OdoBot, a novel web-agent architecture that completes tasks at a fraction of the cost when compared to conventional web agents, achieved by leveraging a behavioral model of the underlying application constructed by analyzing successful task-execution demonstrations.

title: Decoupling Readiness from Release for Tail-Aware Scheduling of Agentic LLM Workflows
proposal_tldr: This work presents a tail-risk-aware turn release scheduling method that jointly decides which ready turn to release next and how much released but unfinished work to maintain, and reduces the P95 of workflow flow time under contention, achieving up to a \(3.50\times\) speedup.

title: Mr.LHDR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Real-World Long-Horizon Deep Research Agents
proposal_tldr: Findings reveal sustained, dependency-consistent evidence integration, rather than isolated fact retrieval, as a key bottleneck for current deep research agents.

title: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: A training-free framework that combines a query-independent layout-derived interaction prior with instruction relevance and feature novelty to rank visual evidence according to both potential future utility and diversity, allowing retained visual evidence to shrink monotonically across budgets while remaining reusable throughout the trajectory.

title: TrajMark: Ownership Attribution and Segment-Level Tamper Localization for Coding-Agent Trajectories
proposal_tldr: TrajMark is proposed, a training-free, symmetric-key, visible-only trajectory watermarking framework that separates robust ownership attribution from fragile local integrity verification, and provides a design-level analysis of owner recoverability, integrity collision probability, structural overhead, and localization behavior.

title: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: AppSim-Bench is proposed, which addresses this trade-off through controllable simulated apps that preserve task-relevant interaction logic while supporting deterministic evaluation and removes major sources of environmental stochasticity, enabling reproducible cross-model comparison.

title: xDailyBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Professional Consultation for Real-Life Problems
proposal_tldr: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for everyday assistance, yet existing benchmarks only partially reflect the requests users naturally make in practice. Real-world requests are often open-ended, casually specified, and context-dependent, requiring models not only to follow explicit

title: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes activation-conditioned selective knowledge control, a lightweight method that achieves selective knowledge retention via neuron-level gradient manipulation and effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting on prior applications while sustaining robust adaptation to new ones.

title: The Assumed Reader: AI Agents, Hypertext, and the Vulnerable Limits of Interpretation
venue: Proceedings of the 37th ACM Conference on Hypertext
proposal_tldr: This paper argues for reframing hypertext as a relational environment where the machine reader and hypertext topology are mutually constituted, and adversarial structures can exploit that entanglement.

title: Rhythms of Work: Multi-Scale Interpretation of Human Behavioral Traces for Workplace Agents
proposal_tldr: A multi-resolution vocabulary of semantically normalized operators, recurring motifs, coherent episodes, and day-level rhythms, each preserving the structure salient at its own horizon is constructed, each preserving the structure salient at its own horizon.

title: Efficient GUI Agents: A Systems Survey of Observation, Memory, Action, and Runtime Optimization
proposal_tldr: This survey studies efficient GUI agents through an end-to-end systems lens that preserves the current technical axes of observation efficiency, context and memory efficiency, action efficiency, and planner-side/system efficiency.

title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Predicted-state matching, a training objective where the predicted representation must distinguish the true resulting state from those reached by alternative actions, is introduced and outperforms world models trained with supervised next-state prediction.

title: Beyond the Verdict: Evidence-Aligned Evaluation of Visual Prompt-Injection Guardrails
proposal_tldr: This work studies the problem in web-agent guardrails, where a VLM judges whether on-screen text conflicts with a user instruction, and proposes two training-free interventions that improve grounding without changing verdicts.

title: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users'Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
proposal_tldr: A three-week diary study with 8 blind users using OLLA, a screen-reader-accessible CUA prototype, collecting 1,258 commands across 12 applications with screenshots, UI trees, model responses, and action traces reveals grounding, planning, constraint-tracking, and termination failures, while interviews reveal beyond-automation needs.

title: WorldBench: Culturally Grounded Benchmark for Multilingual Agents
proposal_tldr: WorldBench is presented: a comprehensive, multilingual benchmark of genuine, persona-grounded everyday workflows, where agents can act in a sandbox via structured actions, and Constrained Task Success (CTS), which combines natural language instructions and testbeds to score task completion, minimal modification, and other complementary metrics through deterministic and LLM-as-a-Judge evaluations.

title: ExBind: A Controlled Diagnostic Benchmark for Visual-to-Executable Correspondence
proposal_tldr: ExBind is designed for controlled diagnosis rather than population-scale ranking or end-to-end editing evaluation, and samples representation-independent latent binding instances and compiles them into SVG, DOM, canvas, tree, graph, and table cases with deterministic mappings to executable references.

title: Using Grounded Theory for Agent Behavior Analysis at Scale
