proposal_tldr: This work proposes AutoTraceGT (Automated Trace analysis through Grounded Theory), the first multi-agent pipeline that automates grounded theory on agent trajectories and suggests Grounded Theory offers a scalable analytic tool for ML researchers and agent developers studying what agents actually do.

title: How Fast Do Agents Rot? An Empirical Study of Long-Horizon Degradation in LLM Agents for Production Decision-Making
proposal_tldr: The results argue for horizon-aware evaluation and reliability budgeting in place of aggregate pass-rate metrics, and for teams responsible for agent orchestration and reliability at scale to consider horizon-aware evaluation and reliability budgeting in place of aggregate pass-rate metrics.

title: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: A budget-aware framework that systematically orchestrates when and what to teach and integrates a solvability-aware teacher gate to dictate the teacher model and a score-guided turn selection mechanism to decide what informative turns to retain is proposed.

title: GeoAgent: Evaluating VLM Geolocalization Through Embodied Navigation
proposal_tldr: This work introduces GeoAgent, an agentic environment-based benchmark that requires agents to navigate Street View environments to refine their geolocalization through sequential reasoning, and establishes the challenges of embodied navigation and geospatial reasoning.

title: A Systematic Survey of Agentic Skills: Architecture, Lifecycle, and Security
proposal_tldr: A unified systems foundation and reference architecture for the agentic skills ecosystem is established, formalize skills as externalized procedural knowledge bridging high-level cognitive planning with deterministic execution environments, and systematically delineate the architecture across a nine-stage lifecycle.

title: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes that LLM web agents can learn simple environment observations at test time, and introduces trial steps for agents to decompose a complex environment observation into sub-modules, and implements a label-free learning method, Test-Time Environment Decomposition (TTED), to adapt agent behaviors with experience during inference.

title: Finding Where the Buck Stops: An Automated Failure Attribution-Based Reflection Framework for Multi-Agent Collaboration
proposal_tldr: The generalizability of the diagnose-then-correct paradigm is established and it is demonstrated that in low-resource settings, focusing reflection on reasoning steps after the decisive error step achieves comparable quality to reflecting on the complete failure trajectory.

title: String: An Agentic OS Where Every App Is a Markdown File
proposal_tldr: String is presented, an open-source runtime that gives this new class of software user an interface of its own and treats the job as an operating-systems problem and what three months of production use taught us.

title: Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents
proposal_tldr: Iron is introduced, an intent-aligned, self-improved, and annotation-efficient framework for training GUI agents that employs a novel dual learning strategy that utilizes a stepwise cycle-consistent reward to achieve fine-grained alignment between low-level actions and high-level intents, thereby improving instruction grounding and intent understanding.

title: FigMirror: Ground It, Code It, Plot It
proposal_tldr: FigMirror is proposed, an agentic framework that unlocks coordinate grounding and coding capabilities present in modern computer-use models through Grounded Measurement, which locates visual elements by coordinates and measures their properties through executable code.

title: BekchiAI: Measuring, Observing, and Controlling LLM Agents in One Click
proposal_tldr: BekchiAI is a complementary web-based observability and control layer for deployed agents, providing full token and latency telemetry as well as remote run termination and the benchmark, evaluation tools, and platform are publicly released.

title: AgentJudgeBench: A Multi-Difficulty Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Judges on Agentic Tool-Calling
proposal_tldr: The first benchmark to systematically study LLM-as-a-judge reliability for agentic tool-calling over workflow DAGs, as distinct from the broader LLM-as-a-judge task of open-ended text or preference evaluation, exposes fundamental limitations of current LLM judges and yields practical guidelines for reliable evaluation in agentic systems.

title: Paint What You See: Benchmarking Dexterous Visual Tool Use in Multimodal Agents
proposal_tldr: EASEL is proposed, a benchmark evaluating a controlled instance of dexterous visual tool use that adopts reference-guided visual reconstruction as its primary proxy task: the agent incrementally paints a canvas to match a reference image.

title: Semantic Tree: Leveraging Semantic UI Representation for Test Case Generation
venue: International Conferences on Information Science and System

title: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
proposal_tldr: BrowserForge is presented, a framework that generates web interaction data at scale by driving many browser sandboxes in parallel over the open web, and fine-tuning a compact multimodal model on this corpus raises its success rate on the live Online-Mind2Web from 25.66% to 33.33% and consistently improves step accuracy on the static Multimodal-Mind2Web.

title: Not All Tokens Are Equal: Region-Aware Consistency Repair of Backdoors in MLLMs
proposal_tldr: RACER is presented, a model-level repair framework motivated by a key observation: backdoors induce abnormal layer-to-layer evolution in internal representations, which is modality-dependent, concentrating primarily in the token region encoding the trigger features that the backdoor model actually relies on.

title: From Language Models to Agentic AI: A Survey of Autonomous, Action-Enabled, and Collaborative LLM Agents
proposal_tldr: A unified, taxonomy-driven, and deployment-oriented survey of agentic AI systems, synthesizing recent advances through a modular reference architecture and a four-dimensional taxonomy that characterizes agents along the axes of autonomy, tool use, collaboration, and safety–governance is presented.

title: Agent-G$^2$: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: A Gaussian guidance framework that draws the depth per task from a Gaussian whose center and spread are estimated online from rollouts already collected for policy optimization, requiring no probe rollouts or learned depth predictor is proposed.

title: ClawProBench: Trace-Aware Evaluation of AI Agents with Runtime Coverage and Frozen Workplace-Style Holdouts
proposal_tldr: ClawProBench is presented, a trace-aware benchmark for runtime-native agent evaluation instantiated on OpenClaw, a live agent runtime with workspace tools and native surfaces for browsing, memory, messaging, scheduling, skills, and subagents.

title: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
proposal_tldr: Embedding-based evaluations should report lexical baselines, label-type stratification, and deployable-fusion diagnostics, to show that embedding-based evaluations can conflate visible-label recovery with semantic GUI grounding.

title: Training Needs Trustworthy Worlds: Verified Synthetic Web Environments for Agent Learning
proposal_tldr: These results show that verified synthetic environments can serve as a scalable and reliable training substrate for compact web agents, shifting synthetic webagent learning from surface-level plausibility toward executable, state-grounded supervision.

title: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: Experiments on GUI agent benchmarks show that LACL-GUI provides more effective learning signals and consistently improves agent performance over prior methods, highlighting the value of trajectory-level supervision in contrastive RLVR.

title: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
proposal_tldr: RecVerse is presented, a GUI-grounded simulation agent that perceives pages through screenshots and produces faithful multi-turn trajectories and significantly outperforms existing baselines in both behavioral fidelity and intent consistency.

title: FigmaTrace: Capturing Creative Nuances in Human Figma Design Workflows
proposal_tldr: This work first defines a unique, expert curated taxonomy of design skills and best practices which is further expanded into a set of 126 open ended, subjective, long horizon tasks and uses this dataset to train four models and shows that training on FigmaTrace leads to a performance improvement comparable to frontier closed models.

title: AgentDecarbonizer: Carbon-Aware Execution for AI Agents
proposal_tldr: AgentDecarbonizer, a carbon optimizer for AI agents that runs alongside OpenClaw, conservatively estimates task duration and selects deadline-feasible execution schedules, while accounting for cache recomputation overhead during spatial shifting.

title: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work presents ComponentBench, a benchmark and diagnostic pipeline for component-level evaluation of computer-use agents on modern web UIs, and introduces a scalable pipeline for auditing realized structural difficulty after implementation and synthesizing structured failure analyses across tasks and component families.

title: Breaking Planner Integrity Boundary: Enviroment State-Text Injection Attack on LLM-Driven Embodied Agents
proposal_tldr: Investigation of environment-state text as an independent attack surface and the first closed-loop Environment State-Text Injection (ESTI) attack for LLM-driven embodied agents show that grounding, consistency, and executability jointly determine whether manipulated state evidence can propagate through the embodied closed loop and produce verifiable environmental changes.

title: HxAgent: Iterative Agent Planning for End-to-End Web Application Testing
proposal_tldr: HxAgent is introduced, an iterative LLM-based planning agent with a proactive correction strategy that achieves 97.4% Exact-Match accuracy on MiniWoB++, comparable to the best baselines without human demonstrations and surpassing the recent WALT by 10.5%.

title: DebateGuard: Action-Level Deliberation for Web Agents under Deceptive Interfaces
venue: 2026 7th International Conference on Computer Vision and Data Mining (ICCVDM)

title: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
proposal_tldr: Experiments on WebArena and WebVoyager demonstrate that SynWeaver consistently outperforms strong synthesis baselines and yields more effective supervision for both in-domain and out-of-domain generalization.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Foundation Models: A Survey
proposal_tldr: A coherent map of the rapidly expanding landscape of visual RL is provided to provide researchers and practitioners with a coherent map of the rapidly expanding landscape of visual RL and to highlight promising directions for future inquiry.

title: BioWeaver: Adaptive Workflow Orchestration for Biomedical Data Integration with Progressive Deep Web Exploration
venue: International Conference on Statistical and Scientific Database Management
proposal_tldr: BioWeaver is presented, an adaptive workflow orchestration system that converts natural-language biomedical questions into executable scientific workflow graphs and suggests that adaptive workflow graphs provide a practical foundation for reproducible, source-grounded biomedical data integration across heterogeneous and deep web resources.

title: DSAgentBench: Can Agents Automate End-to-End Data-Science Workflows in Real Computer Environments?
proposal_tldr: DSAgentBench is introduced, the first benchmark to evaluate whether agents can automate full data-science workflows inside real computer environments, and reveals a substantial capability gap between current agentic systems and real data-science workflows.

title: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
proposal_tldr: This work introduces MobileJudgeBench, a benchmark for systematically evaluating LLM-as-judge methods on mobile agent trajectories, and reveals benchmark quality metrics reliably predict real-world judge utility.

title: MELLON - Multimodal Enhanced LLM for Online Navigation
proposal_tldr: This work proposes three innovative multimodal enhancements: Multimodal Enhanced LLM for Online Navigation (MELLON), VQAgent, and Multimodal Ranker to enhance the performance of web navigation agents.

title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching
proposal_tldr: A regression-free framework where a frozen MLLM performs instruction parsing and a dedicated grounding model handles precise localization without learning any coordinate regression parameters is proposed.

title: CAP: A Scalable Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-Site Browser Agents with Complex Actions and Perception
proposal_tldr: CAP is introduced, a scalable benchmark for evaluating browser agents on cross-site, human-like web tasks that require non-trivial UI interactions and visual understanding and a decomposition-and-recomposition pipeline that first abstracts each website into a structured site card capturing user-facing functions, complex execution operations, and perceptual requirements, and then recomposes these components into realistic cross-site workflows.

title: Boosting Vision-Language Model for Cross-Device GUI Agent Grounding and Navigation
venue: Conference on Multimedia Information Processing and Retrieval

title: Passing the Turing Test on Screen: A Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agent Humanization
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: This work introduces the ''Turing Test on Screen,'' formally modeling the interaction as a MinMax optimization problem between a detector and an agent aiming to minimize behavioral divergence, and establishes the Agent Humanization Benchmark (AHB) and detection metrics to quantify the trade-off between imitability and utility.

title: Trustworthy LLM-Based Agents for Data-Centric AI
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: This tutorial delivers a systematic, data-centric roadmap to build LLM agents that are not merely capable but provably trustworthy, unifying advances in LLM agents, robust machine learning, and data-centric AI.

title: From Generic Intelligence to Personalized AI: A Tutorial on Foundations of LLM Personalization
venue: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining V.2
proposal_tldr: This tutorial provides a systematic overview of LLM personalization, covering core paradigms such as user-aware representations, prompt-based adaptation, memory augmentation, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and continual learning.

title: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
proposal_tldr: Experiments on long-horizon embodied and web-agent benchmarks show that MemPrism consistently improves the task performance, especially as trajectories become longer, while reducing memory token consumption.

title: RealGUINoise: An Interactive Cross-Platform Benchmark for GUI Agent Robustness under Real-World Interface Noise
proposal_tldr: RealGUINoise is introduced, an interactive cross-platform, extensible benchmark for systematically evaluating GUI Agents under common realistic interface noise in fully interactive environments, exposing a critical gap between capability in clean environments and dependable operation in real-world settings.

title: Predicting Task Difficulty Without Rollouts
proposal_tldr: It is found that AUC can mask poor difficulty estimates, identify token-level entropy as a useful predictive signal, and demonstrate how residuals between expected and observed difficulty can expose environment flaws such as contamination and infeasibility.

title: LoginTrap: Uncovering Task-Agnostic Phishing-Style Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks against LLM-based Web Agents
proposal_tldr: The findings identify login inducement as a systematic authentication boundary risk and motivate further research on authentication-aware defenses for web agents, which are effective across agent architectures and defenses.

title: FinReportBench: Measuring and Improving Institution-Grade Financial Report Generation
proposal_tldr: Large language models can produce fluent financial analysis, but fluency alone does not establish whether a report is suitable for institutional delivery. We introduce FinReportBench, an expert-grounded benchmark for measuring and improving institution-grade financial report generation. Expert revie

title: InsightEmb: Learning Action-Intent Embeddings for Agentic Insight Retrieval
proposal_tldr: InsightEmb is a contrastive embedding framework that learns transferable progress-oriented retrieval geometry using only mathematical reasoning data, enabling effective training from publicly available reasoning data without expensive environment-specific supervision.

title: "Allow"to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: A systematic study of mobile GUI agents' ability to grant only permissions that are necessary for the delegated task remains largely unexamined, and suggests that separating task execution from permission authorization is a promising design direction for future work.

title: From Bug Reports to Browser-Executable Procedures: An LLM-Driven Agent for Web GUI Bug Reproduction
proposal_tldr: The results show that explicit context reconstruction and state-aware browser execution effectively support report-derived browser reproduction, while historical replay shows that successful procedures often expose the original bug-present behavior on restored buggy versions.

title: LiveEvalBench: Toward Open-World Evaluation for Web Generation
proposal_tldr: Experiments across diverse real-world web-generation scenarios show that LiveEvalBench aligns closely with human expert judgment and provides fine-grained insights into frontier models' web generation capabilities.

title: PredAct-Bench: Benchmarking Tool-Augmented Dialogue under Controlled Tool Noise
proposal_tldr: PREDACTBENCH is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating dialogue agents paired with statistically imperfect tools, using education as a measurable testbed where ground truth outcomes and clear intervention decisions are available and a benchmark for AI-assisted human decision-making, where the AI uses noisy predictors to help guide a user.

title: RADAR: Readiness for AI Discovery and Agentic Reach
proposal_tldr: RADAR lets governments at any income level see it and offer a concrete agenda to fix it, so that public services are not only described by AI but actually reachable through it.

title: A domain-independent task-oriented fusion framework on task-oriented dialogues
FTDI: A Budget-Aware Self-Healing Framework for LLM Multi-Agent Code Generation
Alignment Is Local: A Paired Diagnostic for GUI Agents under User-Side Persuasion
proposal_tldr: It is shown that a one-line guardrail achieves large single-shot ASR reductions, up to roughly 40 points, at near-zero over-refusal cost, which overstates deployed robustness by a systematic and predictable margin.

title: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: RMSWeb, a three-part recipe for Qwen3-VL-Instruct at 8B and 32B, achieves the strongest reported Online-Mind2Web result among similarly sized open-weight models in a comparison and a leading reported accuracy-cost trade-off on WebVoyager and WebTailBench, with the caveat that external evaluation protocols differ.

title: SPECTRA: On-Device Cognitive Perturbation and Trajectory Analysis for Autonomous Edge-Cloud GUI Grounding
proposal_tldr: SPECTRA is proposed, a lightweight autonomous request framework for edge-cloud GUI grounding, comprising Saliency-Guided Targeted Perturbation and Efficient Cognitive Trajectory Analysis, which conducts a visual cognitive stress test and quantifies the topological divergence of the agent's high-dimensional cognitive trajectories during the prefill phase, avoiding inefficient output decoding.

title: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
proposal_tldr: The findings suggest that efficient local CUAs require selective compute allocation, failure-aware control mechanisms, and agentic frameworks designed around the capabilities and limitations of local models.

title: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
proposal_tldr: Results suggest that AAPT performs best when candidate actions can be enumerated in advance, whereas reactive execution remains stronger when they cannot, and on an external benchmark, AAPT matches the overall performance of a reactive baseline, although the two methods exhibit complementary strengths.

title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation
proposal_tldr: A three-class detection framework distinguishing humans, bots, and AI agents is presented, and it is shown that the binary-vs-agent confusion is architectural: a binary human-vs-bot detector misroutes agent sessions because its label space lacks an agent class.

title: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
proposal_tldr: Desktop-Delta Bench is introduced, an offline step-level benchmark with 2,013 human-verified instances from novel, multi-app Linux trajectories across ~15 applications and 50 task domains that complements end-to-end benchmarks by filling the missing diagnostic layer between GUI grounding and final task success, enabling targeted improvements to desktop CUA verification, reliability, and recovery.

title: OrchBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Plans in Isolation via Deterministic Simulation
proposal_tldr: OrchBench is established as an efficient and interpretable benchmark for comparing and diagnosing multi-agent orchestration plans, finding that preserving task-critical information is more important than simply increasing the number of agents, and the benefits of parallelism diminish as coordination failures accumulate.

title: ClawRec: A Claw-Native Recommender System
proposal_tldr: This paper presents ClawRec, the first recommender system designed to operate natively in this environment, and introduces Claw-native recommender systems, a new paradigm that moves beyond platform-local ranking to produce unified, complementary recommendation slates spanning diverse sources and content forms.

title: From Blind Edits to Verified Repair: Building Trustworthy User-Side LLM Agents for Web Accessibility
proposal_tldr: A verified repair instrument pairing a trilingual seeded-violation benchmark with an audit-inject-verify loop that accepts a change only if violations strictly decrease, so regression on the automated checks is impossible by construction.

title: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes the SeekJudge framework, a model-based reward to match or surpass native rule-based reward in online RL, measured by downstream success rate on held-out RL test goals and is the first model-based reward to match or surpass native rule-based reward in online RL.

title: SQBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Task Delivery by Language-Model Agents in Production-Oriented Workflows
proposal_tldr: SQBench is introduced, a benchmark for evaluating production-oriented task delivery by language-model agents and shows that functional completion alone does not fully characterize delivery quality and that risk determinations should be reported separately.

title: First International Workshop on Conversational Interfaces for Agentic Web Browsing: Are We Ready to Move Beyond GUIs?
venue: International Conference on Conversational User Interfaces
proposal_tldr: The workshop aims to advance a research agenda for understanding how to design inclusive conversational web browsing and to identify key design challenges, opportunities, and open questions for the CUI community.

title: SEE: Structure-aware Exploring & Exploiting for Long-horizon GUI Agent Trajectory Synthesis
proposal_tldr: See, a two-stage data synthesis framework consisting of an efficient exploration stage that builds an explicit UI transition graph over screens and elements, and a graph-based synthesis stage that composes diverse multi-step trajectories via planning and controlled sampling, yields reproducible and explainable data generation.

title: RT-SHCUA: Real-Time Self-Hosted Computer-Use Agent for UAV Control
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes a real-time and security-oriented restructuring of SHCUA-based UAV control, which transforms its outputs into contract-bound UAV skill invocations with explicit timing, state, authority, fallback, and evidence semantics.

title: The Chronos Vulnerability: A Taxonomy of Temporal Persistence and Memory-Based Deception in Agentic AI
proposal_tldr: This study formalizes the threat model for persistence-based attacks and the threat of Dynamics Blindness in the context of the World of Workflows benchmark, demonstrating that traditional endpoint content filters are insufficient for the current stateful architecture.

title: EvoMem: Timeline-Grounded Validity Adjudication for Non-Monotonic Multi-Agent Memory
venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
proposal_tldr: EvoMem is presented, a lightweight plug-in for post-retrieval evidence structuring that converts retrieved interaction traces into an evolutionary timeline: it pools backend evidence, selects salient timepoints under a fixed budget, and summarizes each timepoint to trace updates and suppress outdated answers.

title: Beyond Sequential Interaction: Benchmarking Parallel Execution and Coordination for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: Results show that parallel execution can improve both success rate and efficiency on decomposable, long-horizon GUI tasks, pointing to a direction worth further study.

title: Beyond Generalist LLMs: Specialist Agentic Systems for Structured Code Workflow Execution
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a specialist workflow for the transformation of Business Process Model and Notation diagrams into executable agentic workflows and finds that generalist agents generate code inconsistently in both functionality and quality, limiting their suitability for industrial settings where reliability and maintainability are essential.

title: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
proposal_tldr: Tactile is presented, an open-source tool layer that gives agents a more reliable "hands and feet" for desktop use and suggests that reliable computer use requires not only stronger models, but also a reusable execution substrate that exposes software actions as semantic, verifiable, and auditable objects rather than anonymous screen coordinates.

title: AnovaX: A Local, Multi-Agent Voice Assistant with LLM Planning, Typed Executors, and Adaptive Recovery
proposal_tldr: The point of the project is less to compete with Siri or Alexa than to show that a legible, few-thousand-line assistant is enough to open apps, type into them, run searches, coordinate concurrent actions, recover from single-step failures, and be driven entirely from a phone in another room -- without the LLM ever touching the keyboard.

title: BackendForge: Benchmarking Agentic End-to-End Code Generation with Backend Services
proposal_tldr: BackendForge is introduced, a benchmark of 56 contract-defined backend generation tasks rewritten from real open-source applications that suggests that current LLMs can implement many local API behaviors, but still struggle to produce complete backend services.

title: Designing Agent-Ready Websites for AI Web Agents: A Framework for Machine Readability, Actionability, and Decision Reliability
proposal_tldr: Preliminary evidence that enhanced structural clarity, action cues, evidence signals, and temporal validity indicators can substantially improve the reliability and efficiency of AI browser agents is provided.

title: UNIBROWSE: A Data-to-Agent Framework for Multimodal BrowseComp
proposal_tldr: UNIBROWSE, a unified data pipeline that for the first time simultaneously generates training data covering all three information-flow patterns, augments curated knowledge graphs with live web retrieval for improved fidelity, and introduces a novel metric of exploration degree to filter low-signal instances for efficient reinforcement learning is introduced.

title: MAG: A Web-Agent Benchmark and Harness for Multimodal Action and Guide Generation
proposal_tldr: MAG is introduced, the first benchmark that unifies task execution and guide writing into a single Multimodal Action and Guide task, with two grounding schemes over screenshots: Set-of-Mark element selection and raw pixel coordinates.

title: SLBench: Evaluating How LLM Agents Follow Logical Relations in Skills
proposal_tldr: This work introduces SkillLogic, a framework for analyzing logical relations in skill files and constructing executable tests from them, and establishes logical-relation following as a distinct reliability challenge for skill-guided agents.

title: CurateEvo: Data-Curation Evolving for Agentic Post-Training
proposal_tldr: CurateEvo, a failure-driven dynamic evolution framework for agentic post-training data curation, which represents the curation strategy as executable code and iteratively rewrites it using failed trajectories from a held-out development set and substantially reduces curation overhead.

title: Progress- and Reliability-Oriented Group Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
proposal_tldr: ProGPO (Progress- and Reliability-Oriented Group Policy Optimization), a learned-critic-free method for context-consistent step-level learning that improves over matched agentic RL baselines under comparable computational overhead.

title: Do GUI Agents Believe Their Eyes? Diagnosing State-Belief Reliance on Pixels versus Structure
proposal_tldr: This work formalizes visual state reliance, the attribution of a state belief to pixels, structure, or priors, and measures it with paired single-channel interventions over 735 probes spanning real web, mobile, and desktop interfaces, to give a measurable diagnostic of whether agent state beliefs are visually grounded.

title: AstraGame: Effective and Efficient VLM Agent Serving for Large-Scale Game Testing in an Industry Setting
proposal_tldr: AstraGame is presented, a VLM-based game testing framework that leverages a decoupled architecture to orchestrate collaboration between specialized small models and large cognitive VLMs, and proposes to parallelize perception and reasoning tasks for temporal saturation, implement widget-level semantic caching to transform repetitive inference into efficient cache lookup, and structure action protocols for token efficiency.

title: APeB: Benchmarking Personalization Ability of Large Language Model Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces personalized product search (PPS), a testbed for agentic personalization under raw queries and diverse histories, and constructs Agent Personalized Benchmark (APeB) from action logs, pairing underspecified intents with rich histories and user-viewed candidate items.

title: Atomic Task Graph: A Unified Framework for Agentic Planning and Execution
proposal_tldr: Atomic Task Graph (ATG) is proposed, a unified control framework for planning and execution that consistently outperforms strong baselines in success rate and execution efficiency across three interactive benchmarks using only 7B-8B backbones.

title: Navigation Alone Is Not Enough: Evaluating Explanatory Assistive UI Agents
proposal_tldr: NeXUI is introduced, a benchmark for assistive agents that must navigate interfaces while explaining each step in clear language for nonvisual use and provides a clearer way to study agents that can support blind and visually impaired users in modern computing environments.

title: SkaaS: A Skill-as-a-Service Architecture for Stateful Service Reasoning in Manual Procedures via FSM-Constrained Multimodal LLMs
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
proposal_tldr: Under the Everything-as-a-Service (XaaS) paradigm, human skills can be provisioned as cloud services. title: AGEE: A multi-dimensional process-level metric for evaluating agent exploration over knowledge graphs
GUICrafter: Weakly-Supervised GUI Agent Leveraging Massive Unannotated Screenshots
proposal_tldr: GUICrafter is proposed, a weakly-supervised GUI agent leveraging massive unannotated screenshots to substantially reduce the reliance on expensive human annotations, and achieves competitive, or even superior, performance to advanced systems like UI-TARS while using only 0.1% of its data.

title: Rehearsed Multi-Agent Live Product Demonstrations with Real-Time Voice Question Answering
proposal_tldr: Rhetor is proposed, a multi-agent system that takes a running web application and its source-code repository as input and produces a rehearsed live demonstration with segment-synchronized narration and real-time voice question answering.

title: ECHO: Learning Epistemically Adaptive Language Agents with Turn-Level Credit
proposal_tldr: Epistemic Decision Processes (EDPs), a belief-state formulation of multi-turn information seeking in which actions produce external observations that update the agent's posterior over a latent task variable, and ECHO, a practical clipped policy-gradient objective that assigns turn-level credit using posterior-sensitive rewards.

title: LUMOS: A Semantic Operating-System Layer for Accessibility-Grounded AI Agents
proposal_tldr: LUMOS (Language Model Unified Machine-Readable Operating-System Semantics), a semantic interaction layer between AI agents and operating systems, is introduced and suggests a path toward AI-native operating systems and machine-readable interaction layers.

title: Agent vs. Parametric World Models: Hybrid Planning for Reliable Language Agents
proposal_tldr: This work proposes Hybrid World-Model Planning (Hybrid-WM), which keeps the language model as the planner while using a small parametric transition model to predict action validity, state deltas, risk, and value, and suggests that lightweight parametric transition models can serve as effective grounding mechanisms for language-agent planning without replacing semantic reasoning.

title: Contextual Associations Between Webpage Elements for Web Accessibility: An Empirical Study
proposal_tldr: This registered report investigates whether human-perceived contextual associations between webpage elements can be recovered from the accessibility tree using link prediction, and whether the learned associations generalize across websites.

title: Ko-WideSearch: A Korean Breadth-Search Benchmark for Exhaustive Set Enumeration by Web Agents
proposal_tldr: I introduce \textsc{Ko-WideSearch}, a Korean breadth-search benchmark built by an automated synthesize-and-verify pipeline, which spans 228 tables over 190 entities and sixteen categories across three difficulty tiers, set by two structural knobs.

title: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: VisCritic is introduced, a visual process reward framework that verifies agent actions by directly comparing pre-action and post-action screenshots in visual feature space, and generally improving benchmark metrics while providing visual diagnostic cues.

title: ENVS: Environment-Native Verified Search for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
proposal_tldr: Environment-Native Verified Search (ENVS) is proposed, a training-time search-and-filter pipeline that uses the environment to construct verified supervision before policy optimization: it branches over behaviorally distinct GUI actions in live OSWorld VMs, verifies successful leaves, and trains from globally balanced step-level supervision.

title: How Should Agents Read Demonstrations? Hierarchical Structure Beats Flat Action Logs
proposal_tldr: These results offer a concrete design recommendation for PbD pipelines and, more broadly, for any system that feeds procedural context to an LLM agent: segment action sequences into named subgoal groups rather than presenting flat step lists.

title: Beyond the Current Observation: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models in Controllable Non-Markov Games
proposal_tldr: This work introduces RNG-Bench (Reconstructive Non-Markov Games), a benchmark suite designed to isolate a base model's ability to reconstruct past observations and act on them during multi-step interaction, and fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on optimal-policy rollouts and filtered model demonstrations improves performance on RNG-Bench and transfers to existing benchmarks without degrading general multimodal capability.

title: Beyond Domains: Reusing Web Skills via Transferable Interaction Patterns
proposal_tldr: SkillMigrator is presented, an agent that learns reusable web skills and transfers them across sites by matching layout structure rather than specific element references, and reduces the average LLM-action count on successful trajectories by 8-10% across both WebArena and Mind2Web at matched success rate.

title: MIRAGE: Stealthy Visual Prompt Injection for Vulnerability Detection in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This paper proposes MIRAGE, a novel visual indirect prompt injection framework for targeted next-action hijacking that leverages diffusion models to generate perceptually benign adversarial images strictly confined to the attacker-controlled boundaries permitted by the trusted service provider.

title: StepGuard: Guarding Web Navigation via Single-Step Calibration
proposal_tldr: The StepGuard is developed, a new framework of Guarding Web Navigation via Single-Step Calibration that significantly improves navigation and answer accuracy, setting new state-of-the-art performance on standard web navigation benchmarks.

title: LongWebBench: Evaluating Structural and Functional Webpage Generation in Long-Horizon Settings
proposal_tldr: Experiments with state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary VLMs under single-image and multi-image settings reveal that structural fidelity degrades as webpage length increases, while visually plausible generations often fail to support executable multi-step interactions.

title: FraudSMSWalker: Benchmarking Agentic Large Language Models for SMS-to-Webpage Fraud Detection
proposal_tldr: FraudSMSWalker is positioned as a benchmark for measuring whether web agents can make fraud judgments that remain both accurate and evidence-grounded when direct reputation shortcuts are suppressed.

title: ACCORD: Action-Conditioned Contextual Grounding for Language Agents
proposal_tldr: ACCORD (Action-Conditioned Contextual Grounding), a simple and effective agent framework for adaptive grounding that actively probes the environment for missing information and integrates relevant context from the agent's trajectory that would otherwise be overlooked.

title: Abstracting Cross-Domain Action Sequences into Interpretable Workflows
proposal_tldr: WorkflowView is introduced, a framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to abstract low-level action sequences into high-level activities and demonstrates that LLM-based abstraction is a robust and efficient path forward for transforming low-level behavioral data into high-level, interpretable, and actionable insights.

title: Multi-Modal Agents for Power Distribution Defect Detection: An Evaluation of Foundation Models
proposal_tldr: Experimental results demonstrate the strengths and limitations of current foundation models in these three dimensions, providing empirical evidence for deploying autonomous agents in high-stakes industrial environments.

title: MemVenom: Triggered Poisoning of Multimodal Memories in Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work identifies and systematically study multimodal memory poisoning, an overlooked yet practical attack surface in web-agent systems, and proposes MemVenom, a unified black-box attack framework that poisons graph-structured external memory with coordinated text-image evidence.

title: STAGE-Claw: Automated State-based Agent Benchmarking for Realistic Scenarios
proposal_tldr: STAGE-Claw is introduced, an automated framework for building and evaluating realistic personal-agent scenarios in state-based personal-computing environments and offers a scalable, state-based way to evaluate agents in realistic user scenarios.

title: RunAgent SuperBrowser: A Theory of Autonomous Web Navigation Grounded in Human Browsing Behaviour
proposal_tldr: We present SUPERBROWSER, an autonomous web-navigation agent designed against a single guiding hypothesis: a web agent should browse the way a person browses. A human reading a page does not retain every pixel they have seen; they look at a few candidate targets, decide on one, and remember only what

title: Bayesian-Agent: Posterior-Guided Skill Evolution Across LLM Agent Harnesses
proposal_tldr: Bayesian-Agent is introduced, a native and cross-harness framework that treats reusable agent skills as Bayesian evidence objects, and maintains posterior beliefs over skill reliability and failure modes, and turns those beliefs into auditable skill actions and model-facing guardrails.

title: What You See Is Not What AI Gets: DPAgent-in-the-Middle Defense Against AI-Groomed Deceptive Patterns
proposal_tldr: DPAgent is presented, an agentic, reasoning-aware framework that orchestrates four specialized agents combining latent-space purification with defensive prompting to explore, detect, and repair privacy deceptive interfaces in live web environments, demonstrating the promise of agent-in-the-middle defenses for securing the web UI supply chain against deceptive design and emerging AI threats rooted in data void exploitation.

title: MacArena: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on an Online macOS Environment
proposal_tldr: MacArena is introduced, a benchmark of 421 manually verified tasks spanning 50 applications that combines a curated port of OSWorld tasks, content sourced from macOSWorld, and 49 new macOS-native tasks, all running on Apple's native Virtualization framework on Apple Silicon.

title: TIDE: Proactive Multi-Problem Discovery via Template-Guided Iteration
proposal_tldr: This work introduces TIDE, a template-guided iterative framework with two complementary mechanisms: thought templates, reusable schemas distilled from previously solved cases that specify what contextual signals to attend to and how to connect them, anchoring each prediction in a recognizable problem class.

title: Inclusion arena: A theoretically grounded framework for evaluating large foundation models via application-embedded pairwise comparisons
StickyMemory: Robust Web Agents with Episodic Memory and Self-Verification
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity, Digital Forensics, and AI Applications (ICCSDFAI)
proposal_tldr: Tools effects are never checked, and early decisions are often lost, which makes web agents very difficult with long and multi-step tasks. We introduce StickyMemory, a simple controller that combines a behavior-cloned actuator with two extensions rolling episodic memory summaries and a simple self-v

title: Janus: Edge Content Negotiation for Agent-Oriented Web QoS
venue: International Workshop on Quality of Service
proposal_tldr: LLM agents increasingly retrieve web content through tool calls, yet current web delivery paths remain optimized for human browsing rather than machine reasoning. A typical page carries layout, scripts, image assets, and boilerplate that increase network transfer and context tokens without improving

title: PCLLM: An Integrated LLM-Driven System for Automating Desktop Operations via Direct Mouse and Keyboard Control
proposal_tldr: PCLLM is proposed, a novel end-to-end system that automates PC operations by integrating large language models (LLMs) with computer vision techniques to directly control the mouse and keyboard and adopts task completion rate as the primary metric.

title: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents: Comprehensive Evaluation with a Lightweight Framework
proposal_tldr: A lightweight evaluation framework based on the Minimal Failure Set (MFS), the minimal set of HTML elements whose removal causes task failure, is proposed, finding that extractive HTML reduction methods require either high computation cost or domain-specific optimization to reduce agent latency while maintaining performance.

title: GUITestScape: Towards Open-set Evaluation on Exploratory GUI Testing
proposal_tldr: GUITestScape is presented, an interactive benchmark covering 61 real-world Android applications and 508 preset defects spanning interaction and display types, and GUIJudge is introduced, an open-set evaluator that decomposes an agent's testing trajectory into independently diagnosable capabilities.

title: Architecture-Sensitive Supervised Fine-Tuning for Screen-Conditioned Action Prediction: A PiSAR Benchmark
proposal_tldr: Three supervised fine-tuned models are benchmarked against frontier zero-shot baselines on a 661-row held-out slice of PiSAR, a 12,929-tuple corpus of screen-anchored behavioural rationales curated from public app-store reviews, Pew American Trends Panel demographics, and the OPeRA shopper traces.

title: Does The Way You Plan Matter? An Empirical Study of Planning Representations for LLM Web Agents
proposal_tldr: This work introduces PlanAhead, a static planner-executor framework that evaluates the impact of plan representation in agent performance, and introduces two novel evaluation metrics: Achievement Rate (AR) and Solved-Task Consistency (STC).

title: Adaptive Multimodal Agents-Based Framework for Automatic Workflow Execution
proposal_tldr: A novel multimodal multi-agent framework that achieves automatic workflow execution through a distinct two-phase pipeline that facilitates superior task decomposition and adaptive navigation performance and is validated in a real-world context.

title: Dossier: Deep Research via Ledger-Driven Branching Search and Query Encoding Learning
proposal_tldr: Dossier is introduced, a deep research agent that replaces linear paths with locally parallel, branching search managed by a persistent Research Ledger, and Evidence-Aligned Query Learning (EAQL), a training mechanism that fine-tunes query encoders to condition on the Research Ledger to improve the quality of each retrieval step.

title: Experiments in Agentic AI for Science
proposal_tldr: This paper details two novel frameworks for developing autonomous, agentic AI in scientific workflows, utilizing a hybrid Local Body, Remote Brain architecture via Google Colab, utilizing Python-based local orchestrators to invoke large language model (LLM) cloud backends.

title: PANDO: Efficient Multimodal AI Agents via Online Skill Distillation
proposal_tldr: This work introduces PANDO, a single-rollout online skill-distillation framework that maintains a structured Skill Library and combines progress reflection, confidence-based skill demotion, hierarchical routing, visual compression, and cache-aware prompting and introduces three trajectory-level efficiency metrics to make efficiency visible beyond terminal success.

title: SGR-Bench: Benchmarking Search Agents on State-Gated Retrieval
proposal_tldr: This work introduces SGR-Bench, a benchmark for this setting containing 100 expert-curated tasks spanning six source families and 12 public data ecosystems, and evaluates eight CLI-based agentic LLM systems and three commercial search-agent products.

title: DeepWeb-Bench: A Deep Research Benchmark Demanding Massive Cross-Source Evidence and Long-Horizon Derivation
proposal_tldr: A deep research benchmark that is substantially harder than existing benchmarks for the current frontier, and every reference answer is accompanied by a source-provenance record with four disclosure levels and cross-source checks where available, making scores easier to audit against the underlying evidence.

title: Teaching AI Through Benchmark Construction: QuestBench as a Course-Based Practice for Accountable Knowledge Work
proposal_tldr: This work introduces a course-based practice that teaches AI through benchmark construction, using deep research systems as a concrete example of AI-era knowledge work, and presents QuestBench as a benchmark artifact and as a reusable classroom setting for a larger educational question: how students can remain responsible knowledge actors as AI enters learning and professional work.

title: Latent Action Reparameterization for Efficient Agent Inference
proposal_tldr: Large language model (LLM) agents often rely on long sequences of low-level textual actions, resulting in large effective decision horizons and high inference cost.
